title: Landon Dickerson feels he let team down in his return to lineup
summary: The Eagles got left guard Landon Dickerson back in the lineup for Monday night's game against the Cowboys, but his return wasn't enough to snap the team's losing streak.
full_text: The Eagles got left guard Landon Dickerson back in the lineup for Monday night's game against the Cowboys, but his return wasn't enough to snap the team's losing streak. That streak reached five games as the Cowboys outscored the home team 28-7 over the final 43 minutes of the game. The Eagles' last real chance came when they got the ball down 10 with just over six minutes to play, but pass protection broke down on their first two snaps with Cowboys defensive tackle Quinnen Williams getting a sack on the second one. The Eagles wound up turning it over on downs and the Cowboys put the finishing touches on a 38-21 win. Dickerson got beat on the Williams sack and he was hard on himself while speaking to reporters after the game. Dickerson said that the "two plays at the end there f—king lose us the game” and he said that it hurt to feel you "let your guys down." "I didn’t play good enough ," Dickerson said, via NBCSportsPhiladelphia.com. "These guys work their ass off to come in here and compete every day. I wasn’t good enough." Dickerson said he felt fine in his return from a knee injury and the Eagles ran behind him with success early in the game, but Saquon Barkley had to leave with an injury and the run game became less of an option once Dallas moved in front on the scoreboard. That had more to do with defensive breakdowns than anything Dickerson was doing, but that didn't impact his negative assessment of his play in his first game back.
author: Josh Alper

title: Javonte Williams: Good to give confidence to keep calling runs
summary: Given the number of factors that go into determining winners and losers in NFL games, it's hard to pin the Cowboys' back-to-back losses solely on running back Javonte Williams carrying the ball 23 times in Weeks 5 and 6.
full_text: Given the number of factors that go into determining winners and losers in NFL games, it's hard to pin the Cowboys' back-to-back losses solely on running back Javonte Williams carrying the ball 23 times in Weeks 5 and 6. Offensive balance is always a good thing, though, and it wasn't hard to notice a difference in how the Cowboys were attacking the Eagles on Monday night. Williams kept getting the ball and it didn't feel like a coincidence that they fed an effort that resulted in a convincing 38-21 road win. Williams ran 25 times for a career-high 155 yards and sealed the win with a fourth quarter touchdown. The Cowboys also gave the ball to Tyler Goodson 11 times while Dak Prescott was connecting with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens for three touchdowns through the air. "It was good to give [head coach Brian Schottenheimer] the confidence to keep calling the runs," Williams said, via the team's website. "He made a big emphasis on that this week — to get at least 25 rushes in a game. . . . We were just trying to get back to a balanced offense, and I feel like we did a great job tonight. We've got a high-powered offense, and when you've got G.P., CeeDee, Jake Ferguson, those guys on the outside, I mean, it's going to open up the running." The Cowboys only managed 29 points in their losses to the Packers and Buccaneers in the previous two games and that's not a recipe for success for a team that's built around an ability to score points in bunches. Monday night was more like it and the Cowboys will be trying to stay in the groove they found in Philadelphia.
author: Josh Alper

title: Cowboys are the betting favorites to win the NFC East after win in Philadelphia
summary: The Cowboys are not in first place in the NFC East, but they will be at the end of the season, if the betting odds are to be believed.
full_text: The Cowboys are not in first place in the NFC East, but they will be at the end of the season, if the betting odds are to be believed. After Monday night's win in Philadelphia, Dallas is a +115 favorite to win the NFC East. Just behind the Cowboys are the Giants at +125. The Commanders are long shots at +800 and the Eagles are the longest shots at +1500. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said after the game that the importance of winning on the road in the division wasn't lost on him. "I think it gets us right back into the hunt in the NFC East," Schottenheimer said. The 4-2-1 Giants have a 1.5-game lead over the 3-4 Cowboys, and the Giants beat the Cowboys in Week 1, so it might seem like the Giants should be favored. But the perception among bettors is that the Cowboys remain the better team, as they were expected to be before the season. The Giants-Cowboys rematch is Week 17 in Dallas. The NFC East may be on the line when the two teams meet again.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Saquon Barkley addressed teammates after loss: "Never quit, never give up"
summary: The Eagles fell to 2-5 on Monday night, but Barkley doesn't want to see anyone quitting on the season.
full_text: Eagles running back Saquon Barkley said after Monday night's loss to the Cowboys that he had addressed his teammates to tell them how important it is that they keep competing, even as they struggle through a five-game losing streak. The 2-5 Eagles are long shots to make the playoffs, but Barkley reminded teammates that they can still turn the season around. "I'm not really a big talker, to be honest," Barkley told reporters. "Felt like the moment was right. I just, how I look at life, I feel like you just never quit. You never give up. You just keep fighting, no matter what, whatever the situation is, how it looks. And I feel like that we have the men in the locker room to do it. We put ourselves in this situation. We've got to get ourselves out of it. I know that I've got to take more of a a role of being vocal, using my voice. I'm more of a lead-by-example type of guy, but it happens when you have guys banged up." Barkley said quarterback Jalen Hurts is ordinarily the team's vocal leader. Hurts is out for the season because of blood clots, and Barkley said he and some of his veteran teammates have to take it upon themselves to fill that void. "I think we're doing a great job leading, and we're working our ass off," Barkley said. "And it sucks when the results aren't going the way you wanted to go. I'm going to sound a broken record, but I really bought into this mindset. Just got to keep believing in the process, keep working and keep going. The results may not be what we want right now, but it doesn't matter. We've got to go back to work. It takes all of us." Barkley came into the game with a hamstring injury, aggravated it on his first run, and hurt his back while trying to play while compensating for the lack of mobility in his hamstring. But he said he's not thinking about shutting things down to preserve his health. "It sucks when it's not going the way you want it to go," Barkley said. "I truly love this game and I feel like if you're able to go, you've got to push your body to the limit."
author: Michael David Smith

title: Oregon QB Dante Moore won't return this season from his concussion
summary: Oregon quarterback Dante Moore, who entered the season as one of the top prospects in the 2027 draft, will not play again during the 2026 season.
full_text: Oregon quarterback Dante Moore, who entered the season as one of the top prospects in the 2027 draft, will not play again during the 2026 season. Coach Dan Lanning announced on Monday that Moore's concussion from last month will sideline him for the balance of the schedule . "If it was up to Dante in any shape, way, he would be out there playing for the guys," Lanning said. "This isn't a selfish decision on Dante's part, saying, 'I don't want to come back, the season doesn't look the way I want it to look.' That's not at all what this is." Lanning said that Moore has not been cleared to return from the concussion suffered on September 26 against USC. After taking an illegal hit while sliding, Moore was taken to a local hospital by ambulance for evaluation. "We said before that this is a serious deal that he'll 100% be able to fully recover from, that hasn't changed," Lanning said. "But for him to be out there on the field for us, that's not going to happen. We'd love to have Dante out there, he's still going to be a big part of this team." The Ducks entered the season ranked No. 2. They're now 4-3 and out of the top 25. Under the NCAA's new five-year rule, Moore can return to college football in 2027, delaying his entry to the draft until 2028.
author: Mike Florio

title: John Harbaugh defends Cam Skattebo's helmet-lowering technique
summary: On Sunday, Giants running back Cam Skattebo drew a rare flag for impermissible use of the helmet.
full_text: ' On Sunday, Giants running back Cam Skattebo drew a rare flag for impermissible use of the helmet. On Monday, Giants coach John Harbaugh defended Skattebo's technique. "I'm quite sure [Skattebo is] not trying to use his helmet as a weapon , as a battering ram," Harbaugh told reporters, via Jordan Raanan of ESPN. "It's not the way he's thinking. He's leading with his shoulder. That's what he's trying to do. . . . So, I didn't have a problem with the technique personally at all, but we haven't heard from the league. Maybe they'll be able to enlighten us a little bit on it in terms of what they want us to teach, and that would be great." The language from the rulebook is as clear as it can be. Under Rule 12, Article 10(a), it's a foul if a player "lowers his head and makes forcible contact with his helmet against an opponent." The NFL adopted that rule in 2018, as a proposal that was cobbled together, presented to ownership, and passed without any advance discussion or scrutiny from the media. Infractions are almost always fined after the fact. Skattebo's violation was flagged . In Week 6 alone, the NFL imposed five fines for impermissible use of the helmet. In Week 5, six such fines were levied. For the year (including the preseason), 31 fines for impermissible use of the helmet have been imposed. It's only an issue for coaches when it results in 15 yards of field position; the fines are paid by the players. If the league wants to truly get rid of the maneuver, flags need to fly. And then coaches will be incentivized to come up with a plan other than allowing players to use their helmets like a battering ram. For now, Skattebo has vowed to keep doing it. If he does, the fines will increase. Eventually, he'll be looking at a suspension. And the officials will surely be watching him more closely for further violations — and possibly throwing more flags.
author: Mike Florio

title: Monday Night Football: Cowboys run past Eagles 38-21
summary: Javonte Williams had a career-high 155 yards, and Dak Prescott threw three touchdowns.
full_text: The Cowboys saved their season, at least for another week, and the Eagles' postseason hopes took a huge hit Monday night. Dallas beat Philadelphia 38-21 to end a two-game losing streak and move to 3-4. The Eagles, who are decimated by injuries, have lost five in a row to fall to 2-5. They started the game without quarterback Jalen Hurts and wide receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, among others, and finished it without running backs Saquon Barkley and Dameon Pierce. Barkley, who was returning after missing two games with a hamstring injury, left with a back injury. He had seven carries for 62 yards and a touchdown and two catches for 9 yards in limited usage before his new injury. Pierce left in the fourth quarter with an undisclosed injury after 14 carries for 47 yards and a touchdown. The game was back-and-forth for most of the night, with six lead changes. The last came on CeeDee Lamb's 16-yard touchdown reception and Dak Prescott's 2-point conversion that gave the Cowboys a 28-21 lead with 1:30 left in the third quarter. Brian Schottenheimer, whose play calling was criticized after he abandoned the run in the second half last week, called for more runs than passes. The Cowboys ran it 38 times for 204 yards and threw it 27 times for 212 yards. The Eagles had zero tackles for loss. Javonte Williams set a career-high with 155 yards and scored a touchdown on 25 carries. He is the Cowboys' first 150-yard rusher since Ezekiel Elliott in 2018. Prescott was 15-of-27 for 212 yards and three touchdowns. Lamb caught five passes for 74 yards and two touchdowns and George Pickens had four receptions for 57 yards and a touchdown. Tanner McKee, starting for the second consecutive week in place of Hurts, went 23-of-35 for 211 yards with a touchdown and an interception. Cowboys linebacker DeMarvion Overshown picked him in the second half. Rookie wide receiver Makai Lemon caught seven passes for 67 yards and a touchdown.
author: Charean Williams

title: Dez Bryant wants a full investigation following a Sunday citation for assault
summary: Former Cowboys receiver Dez Bryant wants a full investigation following an incident that resulted in the three-time Pro Bowler being cited for assault.
full_text: Former Cowboys receiver Dez Bryant wants a full investigation following an incident that resulted in the three-time Pro Bowler being cited for assault. Bryant shared his version of the situation with Jackson Thompson of Outkick . Bryant claims that a police officer aimed a gun at Bryant in front of his daughters Sunday following a confrontation with a man that Bryant contends threatened to shoot him. He accused a pair of drivers of cutting him off, and it went from there between Bryant and one of the men. "He go to threatening me and basically saying, um, he’ll insinuate that he’ll, you know, he’ll shoot me or whatever," Bryant told Thompson. Replied Bryant, "You pull that gun, I’m telling you right now, you better use it because if you don’t I’m going to do something to you." The man was recording Bryant with his phone. Bryant told Thompson that he knocked the phone out of the man's hand. The man then threatened to call police; Bryant encouraged him to do it. A responding officer drew a gun on Bryant. Bryant's girlfriend arrived at the scene with Bryant's daughters and began recording the interaction. The man, 19-year-old Noah Reyes, gave his version to the California Post on Monday. Reyes also shared the footage he recorded. "Several callers reported that multiple individuals were involved in the altercation as well as a possible weapon," a Southlake (Texas) Police Department spokesperson told the Post in a statement. "Based on that information, officers drew their firearms upon arrival as a precaution to address any potential threats and ensure the safety of everyone at the scene. Several individuals were temporarily detained as part of the investigation. No firearms were recovered at the scene. "The altercation reportedly began as a traffic incident near Kimball Avenue, where one of the involved individuals, identified as 37-year-old Desmond Bryant, reported he was cut off by another motorist. Both parties subsequently entered the parking lot, where an argument ensued and the alleged assault occurred. "Following the investigation, Bryant, was issued a citation for Assault by Contact, a Class C misdemeanor, and was released at the scene." Bryant is due in court on November 20. Reyes plans to sue Bryant for an injury to his hand. A first-round pick in 2010, Bryant spent eight seasons with the Cowboys. He played for the Saints in 2018 and the Ravens in 2020.
author: Mike Florio

title: Saquon Barkley is questionable to return with back injury
summary: The Eagles running back entered with a right hamstring injury.
full_text: Saquon Barkley missed two games with a right hamstring injury. He returned tonight, but the Eagles running back was in obvious pain for much of the night. He is now questionable to return with a back injury. It is his third injury of the season, with a stinger earlier this season. Barkley has seven carries for 62 yards and a touchdown and two catches for 9 yards. He has played 10 snaps. The Eagles are in trouble without him, now down 10 points to the Cowboys. Dallas drove 78 yards in nine plays to the Philadelphia 6 before settling for Brandon Aubrey's 24-yard field goal.
author: Charean Williams

title: Cowboys regain lead on CeeDee Lamb's second TD
summary: The back-and-forth between the Cowboys and Eagles continues in the second half.
full_text: The back-and-forth between the Cowboys and Eagles continues in the second half. Only 4:14 after the Eagles took a 21-20 lead, the Cowboys regained it 28-21. Dak Prescott threw a dart to CeeDee Lamb, who caught the ball in the end zone for a 16-yard touchdown. It was Lamb's second touchdown of the night. His first covered 9 yards. Lamb has five catches for 74 yards. The Cowboys drove 61 yards in nine plays, converting two third downs. That included a defensive holding penalty on Riq Woolen, who was covering Lamb, on a third-and-9. The 5-yard penalty, which came on an incompletion, extended the drive with an automatic first down. Prescott has completed 14 of 25 passes for 206 yards and three touchdowns. He ran in the 2-point conversion to make it a 7-point lead.
author: Charean Williams

title: NFL fines Caleb Williams $11,941 for displaying "unauthorized logo" on his shoes in Week 6
summary: The No Fun League is also the No Footwear League.
full_text: '' The No Fun League is also the No Footwear League. More specifically, no footwear made by companies that don't pay the league. Per a source with knowledge of the situation, the league has fined Bears quarterback Caleb Williams $11,941 for displaying an "unauthorized logo" on his shoes during the Week 6 win over the Falcons in Atlanta. Williams was wearing Caddix cleats, which do not have a deal with the NFL for the use of its shoes in NFL games. Williams has appealed the fine, and his argument will be, we're told, that he believes the shoes are safer than the shoe options that are officially licensed by the NFL. He has worn the same type of shoe throughout the 2026 preseason and during all regular-season games in which he has played. He was not fined for Week 1 and Week 2. He has yet to be fined for the Week 7 Thursday night game against the Patriots. It's his intention, we're also told, to continue wearing the shoes. The fine letter, dated October 20, does not mention the possibility of Williams being prevented from playing with the Caddix logo visible on his shoes. It's an interesting situation for the league. If a player subjectively believes that a given shoe that isn't made by a company that pays the NFL for the privilege of displaying its logo is safer, should the player be prevented from wearing it? Then there's the separate question of whether objective data supports that the shoe is safer. If that's the case, it will be another example of the commitment to health and safety yielding on occasion to dollars and cents. The Bears return to action next Monday night against the Seahawks. And it will make plenty of sense to eyeball the items that Williams has on his feet.
author: Mike Florio

title: Eagles take 21-20 lead on Cowboys to open second half
summary: Rookie Makai Lemon scored his first NFL touchdown, a 4-yard reception from Tanner McKee.
full_text: Rookie Makai Lemon scored his first NFL touchdown, a 4-yard reception from Tanner McKee. That put the Eagles back in front of the Cowboys, 21-20, after Jake Elliott's PAT. The Eagles took the second-half kickoff and went 84 yards in 17 plays, taking 9:16 off the clock. They converted 4-of-5 third downs and had a fourth-down conversion on the one third down they didn't convert. The Eagles now have 238 yards. McKee is 14-of-22 for 129 yards and a touchdown, and Lemon has five receptions for 54 yards and a touchdown. Saquon Barkley has touched the ball on every play he's been on the field, with seven carries for 62 yards and two catches for 9 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: A 16-game international week was never a possibility during 2020 CBA talks
summary: On Sunday, Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers claimed that, during the 2020 Collective Bargaining Agreement negotiations, a discussion was had regarding the possibility of a full-blown "international week."
full_text: On Sunday, Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers claimed that, during the 2020 Collective Bargaining Agreement negotiations, a discussion was had regarding the possibility of a full-blown " international week ." With all 32 teams playing in foreign countries on the same weekend. It sounded odd, and impractical. As best we can tell, it was never a serious consideration during the 2020 CBA talks — if it was even a consideration at all. While it's possible that the league chose 17 regular-season games over the ability to stage up to 16 annual international games, there was never a specific plan to play all 16 international games in the same week . It's borderline ludicrous on its face. No games in any U.S. stadiums? Sixteen games played all over the world? With a Thursday night game, 14 on Sunday, and one on Monday night? It would be a logistical nightmare for the NFL, which would be staging a full slate of games in foreign soil in the same four-day window. The goal was, and still is, to turn the European games into a TV package, with multiple games starting at 9:30 a.m. ET. Emptying the international tank on one and only one weekend would make no sense. And there's no way the NFL would have accepted 16 international games plus two byes. The league experimented with two byes in 1993, and the networks hated it. A second bye extends the season, but it dilutes the number of games played in plenty of weeks with byes. In 1993, eight of 28 teams were off in Week 3, Week 4, Week 6, and Week 8. Six teams were off in Week 6, Week 11, and Week 13. Four teams were off in Week 10. And two teams were off in Week 12. While two byes may be needed to sell an 18-game season to the players, the league wouldn't have added a second bye to a 16-game season. (Indeed, it didn't add a second bye to a 17-game season.) More importantly, and despite Rodgers's claim, a full-league international week never was (and never will be) a realistic possibility.
author: Mike Florio

title: NFL announces Jay-Z as the Super Bowl LXI halftime act
summary: As expected, the selection of Super Bowl halftime show producer Jay-Z to perform at halftime of Super Bowl LXI at SoFi Stadium is . . .
full_text: As expected , the selection of Super Bowl halftime show producer Jay-Z to perform at halftime of Super Bowl LXI at SoFi Stadium is . . . Jay-Z. The NFL made the announcement at halftime of Monday night's Cowboys-Eagles game. “For several years, we’ve had the privilege of working closely with Jay-Z and Roc Nation, and I’ve seen the extraordinary impact he has had on the Super Bowl Halftime Show,” NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said in a statement. “When we first reached an agreement with Roc Nation to produce the show, I had just one request: that Jay-Z take the stage himself one day, whenever the moment felt right to him. I couldn’t be more excited for fans around the world to experience the artistry, creativity and cultural impact he will bring to the Super Bowl stage.” The partnership between Roc Nation and the NFL to produce the Super Bowl halftime show was struck in 2019. Given the audience that the Super Bowl attracts, the halftime show has become the biggest annual stage in all of music.
author: Mike Florio

title: Monday Night Football: Cowboys lead Eagles 20-14 at halftime
summary: The Cowboys gained 275 yards, scoring on four of five possessions.
full_text: '' The Cowboys and Eagles played an entertaining first half, combining for 34 points and 429 yards. The teams scored six times in nine possessions, and the Cowboys lead 20-14 at halftime. The Cowboys scored on four of five possessions, getting a 55-yard field goal from Brandon Aubrey, a 9-yard CeeDee Lamb touchdown reception, a 21-yard George Pickens touchdown reception and a 27-yard Aubrey field goal. Aubrey's chip-shot field goal came on the final play of the half, but on third down as the Cowboys left the field with a timeout in their pocket. Poor clock management cost them a chance at another play from the Philadelphia 9-yard line. The Cowboys outgained the Eagles 275 to 154, with 18 runs and 21 passes. Dak Prescott is 12-of-21 for 174 yards and two touchdowns, and Javonte Williams has 10 carries for 67 yards. Lamb has four catches for 58 yards and a touchdown and Pickens has caught three passes for 51 yards and a touchdown. The Eagles scored on their first two drives, going 75 yards in only four plays and 76 yards in 13 plays. They have gotten plenty of help from the Dallas defense, which has five penalties. Four of those resulted in first downs, and three came on third- or fourth-down stops. Saquon Barkley, who missed the past two games with a hamstring injury, has six carries for 50 yards and a touchdown. His first carry went for 29 yards and his second was an 8-yard touchdown run. Barkley also has two catches for 9 yards. Dameon Pierce has seven carries for 36 yards and a touchdown. Tanner McKee is 7-of-13 for 68 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: George Pickens' highlight-reel TD catch puts Cowboys back on top
summary: Brian Schottenheimer said he wanted to see more out of wide receiver George Pickens this week.
full_text: Brian Schottenheimer said he wanted to see more out of wide receiver George Pickens this week. Pickens gave him a highlight-reel touchdown catch. On third-and-3 from the Philadelphia 21, Dak Prescott threw a dot to the back corner of the end zone. Pickens, who was tightly covered by safety Andrew Mukuba, made a spectacular catch and managed to get both feet in bounds. It was Pickens' second catch of the night on three targets, and he has 30 yards. The Cowboys lead 17-14 as neither defense has a stop yet. The Cowboys have outgained the Eagles 191 to 140, with one extra possession. Prescott is 8-of-13 for 96 yards and two touchdowns.
author: Charean Williams

title: Eagles take advantage of Cowboys' defensive mistakes for 14-10 lead
summary: The Cowboys defense isn't good, and they can't get out of their own way either.
full_text: The Cowboys defense isn't good, and they can't get out of their own way either. The Cowboys had the Eagles stopped on fourth-and-1 at the Philadelphia 44 on an aborted snap. Defensive lineman Quinnen Williams was called for offsides, though, giving the Eagles a first down. It was Williams' second offsides penalty in the first quarter and the Cowboys' third. The Cowboys stopped the Eagles on third-and-7 at the Dallas 9, too, only to have LT Overton called for roughing the passer. The rookie hit Tanner McKee in the facemask. Dameon Pierce ran it in from the 5 on the next play. The Eagles lead 14-10, gaining 132 yards and scoring two touchdowns on two drives. The Eagles have ruled out wide receiver Britain Covey (knee).
author: Charean Williams

title: Cowboys lead Eagles 10-7
summary: The Cowboys are leaning on their run game after hearing criticism all week about their pass-happy ways last week.
full_text: The Cowboys are leaning on their run game after hearing criticism all week about their pass-happy ways last week. After Javonte Williams scored with 9:19 remaining in the third quarter against the Packers in Week 6, the Cowboys threw on 37 of 38 plays in what turned into a 23-13 loss. The Cowboys have nine runs and six passes thus far tonight against the Eagles. They have a 10-7 lead. After an opening 55-yard field goal from Brandon Aubrey, the Cowboys drove 82 yards in nine plays. Williams, who has 40 yards on five carries, and Tyler Goodson, who has 21 yards on four carries, led the Cowboys down the field. But wide receiver CeeDee Lamb scored the touchdown on a 9-yard pass from Dak Prescott. Prescott is 3-of-6 for 49 yards and a touchdown.
author: Charean Williams

title: Saquon Barkley scores on second carry for 7-3 Eagles lead
summary: The Cowboys got a 55-yard field goal from Brandon Aubrey to end their first drive.
full_text: The Cowboys got a 55-yard field goal from Brandon Aubrey to end their first drive. The Eagles did even better. Despite missing starting quarterback Jalen Hurts and wide receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, the Eagles had no problem going right down the field. That's because Saquon Barkley is back. The Eagles running back, who is returning from a hamstring injury, caught a dump off from Tanner McKee for a 12-yard gain. Barkley then went 29 yards on the next play, though it appeared he aggravated his hamstring after awkwardly getting around safety Caleb Downs. With Barkley on the sideline for one play, McKee connected with rookie Makai Lemon for 21 yards. After an offsides penalty on Cowboys defensive lineman Quinnen Williams, Barkley went around the right side for an easy 8-yard touchdown. The Eagles lead 7-3 with 10:25 left in the first quarter. Barkley has 37 yards and a touchdown on two carries and one catch for 12 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: Monday Night Football: Jonathan Greenard, Saquon Barkley are active for Eagles vs. Cowboys
summary: The Eagles will have outside linebackers Jonathan Greenard (ankle) and Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) tonight.
full_text: The Eagles will have outside linebackers Jonathan Greenard (ankle) and Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) tonight. Both are active. Greenard and Hunt went into today with questionable designations. Greenard missed Week 5 with his injury and had no designation in Week 6 and played 24 of 79 snaps against the Panthers last week. He has been on the injury report every week this season and missed the first two games with a pectoral injury. Hunt missed last week's game with his injury. Running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is also dressed as he returns after missing the past two games. The Eagles will start Tanner McKee at quarterback, and former Cowboys quarterback Joe Milton will serve as McKee's backup. The Eagles' inactives are outside linebacker Nolan Smith (concussion), wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), quarterback Cole Payton, defensive back Michael Carter II (abdomen) and offensive lineman Jake Majors. Payton will serve as the emergency third quarterback. The Cowboys' inactives are offensive tackle Drew Shelton (hamstring), wide receiver KaVontae Turpin (ribs), linebacker Dee Winters (calf), running back Emari Demercado and outside linebacker Tyrus Wheat.
author: Charean Williams

title: Christian McCaffrey has mild hamstring strain, 49ers optimistic he'll play after bye
summary: The 49ers announced running back Christian McCaffrey had a thigh injury during Sunday's loss to the Falcons, but the diagnosis of his injury was different on Monday.
full_text: ' The 49ers announced running back Christian McCaffrey had a thigh injury during Sunday's loss to the Falcons, but the diagnosis of his injury was different on Monday. Fortunately for the 49ers, the outlook was similar to the one McCaffrey shared after the game. Head coach Kyle Shanahan said on Monday that McCaffrey has a mild hamstring strain while confirming McCaffrey's belief that it won’t be an issue when the team returns from their bye in Week 9. "Yeah, we think so, with it just being that ," Shanahan said, via 49ersWebzone.com. "I mean, you never know for sure, but we're pretty optimistic about it. So is he." McCaffrey ran seven times for 39 yards and a touchdown while also catching six passes for 61 yards on Sunday. Mike Evans, Nick Bosa, and Deebo Samuel are among the other players the 49ers also hope to have available after the bye, but it will be a while before there are firmer updates on their chances of playing.
author: Josh Alper

title: Cardinals RB Jeremiyah Love will practice Wednesday
summary: Jeremiyah Love has missed the past two games with a sprained left ankle, but the Cardinals running back is close to returning.
full_text: Jeremiyah Love has missed the past two games with a sprained left ankle, but the Cardinals running back is close to returning. "Jeremiyah will be out there at practice on Wednesday, so we'll see how the week goes ," coach Mike LaFleur said Monday, via video from PHNX_Cardinals. Love, the third overall pick, injured his right ankle in the preseason. He played through his left ankle injury, which he sustained in Week 4, before the Cardinals shut him down to let it heal. Bam Knight and Tyler Allgeier have replaced Love in the backfield. Love has 67 carries for 245 yards and a touchdown and 11 catches for 36 yards and a touchdown. The news is not as good for defensive tackle Walter Nolen III, who has an ankle injury. LaFleur said Nolen will not practice Wednesday, but "a lot can happen in these next two days."
author: Charean Williams

title: Jordan Love, Christian Watson off Packers' injury report
summary: The Packers had quarterback Jordan Love and wide receiver Christian Watson on their injury report last week.
full_text: ' The Packers had quarterback Jordan Love and wide receiver Christian Watson on their injury report last week. Watson was limited in all three practices last week, while Love was limited on Wednesday and a full participant the rest of the week. Love played all 67 snaps in the loss to the Lions on Sunday, and Watson played 54 snaps. Both players are off Monday's estimated report. That's good news for the Packers, who have a quick turnaround with a game against the Panthers on Thursday night. title: Zac Taylor on Shemar Stewart being inactive: He's making progress, but we have a deep group
summary: The decision to make defensive end Shemar Stewart a healthy scratch on Sunday was the subject of a question for Bengals head coach Zac Taylor at a Monday press conference.
full_text: The decision to make defensive end Shemar Stewart a healthy scratch on Sunday was the subject of a question for Bengals head coach Zac Taylor at a Monday press conference. Stewart was a first-round pick in 2025, so seeing him on the inactive list would seem to be a negative sign for his development to this point in his career. Taylor noted that Stewart missed time with a knee injury he suffered this summer and said the second-year player is "doing all the right things," but got caught in a numbers game due to how much depth the team has up front on defense. "It’s a really deep D-line group and it’s really tough to choose who’s gonna be inactive there," Taylor said. "Keep encouraging him because he’s doing everything the right way and he’s really making the progress we’re hoping to see. I don’t want to do that every week, but we’re gonna have to be creative with where we pull from. That’s just part of it." The Bengals had nine defensive linemen active on Sunday, so, progress or not, Stewart is pretty low on the depth chart relative to his draft status. If that doesn't change in the coming weeks, there will likely be more questions about what kind of future he has in Cincinnati.

title: Ashton Jeanty struggling to find room to run, averaging 3.1 yards per carry
summary: Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty has not been the player they thought they were getting when they selected him with the sixth overall pick in the 2025 NFL draft.
full_text: Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty has not been the player they thought they were getting when they selected him with the sixth overall pick in the 2025 NFL draft. After Sunday's loss to the Rams, in which Jeanty ran for just 15 yards on eight carries, Jeanty has a total of 106 carries for 328 yards this season, an average of just 3.1 yards per carry. No runner in the league who's getting the ball as much as Jeanty has such a low average. Jeanty's inability to make big plays running the ball can't just be blamed on the offense or his blocking, as his backup, rookie fourth-round pick Mike Washington, is averaging a solid 4.9 yards per carry this season. A low yards-per-carry average could be excused if Jeanty were getting tough gains in short-yardage situations, but he's not doing that, either. He has only 15 rushing first downs; every other running back with at least 90 carries this season has more rushing first downs than Jeanty. And Jeanty has just one rushing touchdown. If there's a bright side, it's that Jeanty has made plays catching the ball. In Sunday's loss he caught all eight of the passes thrown to him, for 61 yards and a touchdown. For the season, Jeanty has 34 catches for 312 yards and three receiving touchdowns. Jeanty said after Sunday's game that he's not discouraged. "It's a long season, we've got a lot of football left, so regardless of what it looks like, we've got to keep working, keep getting better, no matter what it looks like," Jeanty said. So far, what it looks like is a young running back falling well short of expectations.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Andrew Berry: We're excited to keep Maliek Collins in Cleveland
summary: The 5-3 Browns have another reason to celebrate on Monday.
full_text: The 5-3 Browns have another reason to celebrate on Monday. Cleveland announced that defensive tackle Maliek Colins has signed his two-year contract extension with the club. The deal was agreed to over the weekend . "Since we signed Maliek in the 2025 offseason, he has been a disruptive player in the middle of our defense and one of the top interior pass rushers in football ," Browns General Manager Andrew Berry said in a statement. "His non-stop motor, selflessness and endless pass rush arsenal make him a perfect fit for our attack-style defense. As much as he has contributed to our defensive success on the field, the things he does behind the scenes are just as impactful. “For the past two years, Maliek has been THE veteran, stabilizing presence in the meeting rooms, on the practice field and in the facility. His impact on our young defensive line's growth can't be overstated. We're excited to keep Maliek in Cleveland for several more years.” Collins registered a career-high 6.5 sacks in 12 games with the Browns last season. In seven games so far this year, he’s tallied 3.5 sacks, six tackles for loss, and eight QB hits. A third-round pick in 2016, Collins has tallied 40.5 career sacks for the Cowboys, Raiders, Texans, 49ers, and Browns.

title: Prisco's NFL Week 8 Power Rankings: Lone unbeaten Vikings take over top spot
summary: Pete Prisco shares his Week 8 Power Rankings for the 2026 NFL season, including some big risers and fallers
full_text:
Legit question: How good are the undefeated Minnesota Vikings ?
That isn't to demean the Vikings, the league's last undefeated team, but rather to ask an honest football question. Can a team that is so limited on offense be considered good?
The Vikings are 6-0 after beating the Indianapolis Colts , 16-10, on Sunday, but they are winning games without a real semblance of an offense that scores or scares.
They have scored 125 points in their six games, which means 10 touchdowns on the season. That is historically bad. They are a tough watch on the eyes, even if they showed a little more life on offense against the Colts.
We will learn a lot more about the Vikings over the next four weeks. They play at the Lions , home against the Bills , at the Packers and the 49ers in Mexico. That's quite the string of games.
They will need to be better on offense for sure. But the defense is the gold standard right now in the league, thanks to the uber-aggressive coordinator Brian Flores.
Minnesota takes over the top spot in my Power Rankings this week after the 49ers and Kansas City Chiefs both lost, leaving the Vikings as the only team without a blemish.
The Minnesota offense was a little better in the victory over the Colts, but Indianapolis isn't very good on defense. The Vikings are ranked first in scoring defense and 23rd in scoring offense. That is a heck of a disparity for an unbeaten team.
Quarterback Kyler Murray has to be better. The passing game has to improve from its 29th-ranked yards-per-game mark. If not, the next four games could be a big problem for the Vikings, and their stay at the top won't last long.
The bottom of my rankings has a new team this week. The Miami Dolphins , fresh off their first victory of the season over the New York Jets , have moved above the Los Angeles Chargers .
The Chargers are the only team without a victory this season, and they couldn't lose this past week because they were on a bye. At 0-6, they play their city rival, the Los Angeles Rams , this week. It might mean a stay at the bottom for the Chargers as the heat intensifies for all in that building.
author: Pete Prisco

title: 2027 Super Bowl headliner announced: Jay-Z picks himself to perform for Super Bowl LXI
summary: This is a public service announcement sponsored by Roc Nation
full_text:
The moment we've all been waiting for is here: the NFL halftime show performer announcement. Jay-Z and his company, Roc Nation, are in charge of selecting the performer, and the rapper has chosen himself.
Jay-Z, a New York native, is bringing East Coast hip-hop to the West Coast.
The 56-year-old will take the Super Bowl LXI halftime stage on February 14, 2027, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. The stadium is home to the Los Angeles Rams and Los Angeles Chargers.
The announcement was made across social media with a video. The video was playing "Public Service Announcement" with Jay-Z himself sitting on a stage.
Jay-Z it is! Perfect. pic.twitter.com/L6xnBfedeX
"From Reasonable Doubt to standing on the Super Bowl Halftime stage, this has been a journey," Jay-Z said, via press release. "Thirty years of music, work, and culture on the world's biggest stage. This run continues to be a dream come true."
This marks the first time the rap mogul will perform during the halftime show in any capacity and according to NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell, it's been years in the making.
"For several years, we've had the privilege of working closely with Jay-Z and Roc Nation, and I've seen the extraordinary impact he has had on the Super Bowl Halftime Show," Goodell said. "When we first reached an agreement with Roc Nation to produce the show, I had just one request: that Jay-Z take the stage himself one day, whenever the moment felt right to him. I couldn't be more excited for fans around the world to experience the artistry, creativity and cultural impact he will bring to the Super Bowl stage."
Roc Nation partnered with the NFL in 2019 to produce the halftime show, and since then the 89-time Grammy nominee has been a key decision-maker on who will perform on the biggest stage in football.
The "99 Problems" singer has not announced if he will have any special guests, but since the NFL typically throws in a few surprises for these performances, there is a good chance that pattern will continue. One name that could show up at the Valentine's Day game is Jay-Z's Valentine, Beyoncé.
The superstar singer previously performed in two halftime shows. She headlined the 2013 halftime show and performed with Coldplay and Bruno Mars at halftime in 2016. She also sang the national anthem at Super Bowl XXXVIII in 2001, in her hometown of Houston. On Christmas Day 2024, she took the stage during halftime once again in her home city, for what is commonly referred to as the "Beyonce Bowl.
Beyoncé is no stranger to NFL performances, and considering the two have toured together and have numerous songs, it would make sense.
HOV is currently on the JAŸ-Z30 Tour, celebrating the 30th anniversary of his debut studio album "Reasonable Doubt" and the 25th anniversary of "Blueprint."
The last time a rapper headlined the halftime show was two years ago when Kendrick Lamar performed and brought out special guest SZA. Other rappers to take the Super Bowl halftime show this decade include Eminem, Snoop Dogg, Dr. Dre and Lil Jon.
The Super Bowl is historically the most-watched game of the year and the halftime show is historically the most-watched performance of the year. Last year, Bad Bunny was the halftime performer. For a look at every Super Bowl performer in NFL history, click here .

title: Every Super Bowl halftime performer ever: Full list as Jay Z announces himself as the 2027 artist
summary: Explore the full list of halftime show performers
full_text:
Allow me to reintroduce the Super Bowl halftime performer ... his name is Jay-Z.
Using a snippet from one of his most iconic songs, "Public Service Announcement," the rapper was announced as the Super Bowl LXI halftime performer. This is the first time he will take the Super Bowl halftime stage.
Here is a look at the announcement:
GOAT’s out of the bag. @sc #AppleMusicHalftime #SBLXI pic.twitter.com/6wnIqTKjZB
Roc Nation, co-founded by Jay-Z, partnered with the NFL in 2019 to produce the halftime show. HOV has a major influence in choosing the performer, and this year he went with himself.
While the 89-time Grammy nominee has not announced any special guests yet, there are already numerous names that come to mind for potential additions, including superstar singer Beyoncé, previous halftime performers Rihanna and Eminem.
The Super Bowl, concluding the 2026 season, will be played at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California on February 14, 2027.
The halftime show has been headlined by some of the biggest artists of all time and has delivered wild, iconic moments throughout the Super Bowl's 60-year history.
Last year, Bad Bunny headlined, taking the stage at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara , California. Lady Gaga joined him on stage to perform her hit, "Die With A Smile," marking her third Super Bowl appearance and first as a halftime show guest.
Other past headliners include Kendrick Lamar, Rihanna, Usher and Beyoncé.
For artists who play the Super Bowl halftime show, the audience is exponentially bigger than any they have ever encountered. It was not always like that, however.
So what were the shows like before they became must-see television? Do you remember that killer halftime show featuring the Rockettes, Chubby Checker and 88 grand pianos in 1988? Do you remember the captivating "Be Bop Bamboozled" at the Orange Bowl in 1989? No -- no, you do not. Ditto Carol Channing (twice) or any of those four contrived Up With People performances in the late '70s and early '80s.
Before Michael Jackson, the Super Bowl halftime show was an endless wasteland of college marching bands and flag-spinning tributes -- from salutes to Hollywood (twice), to Motown, to the Big Band Era, to the Caribbean, to Duke Ellington. We also got New Kids on the Block (1991) not singing any of their biggest hits and Gloria Estefan (1992) providing the soundtrack for Olympic figure skaters Dorothy Hamill and Brian Boitano of "What would Brian Boitano do?" fame -- because nothing says a Minnesota Super Bowl like the lead singer of the Miami Sound Machine.
Then the King of Pop arrived at the Rose Bowl in 1993 -- and the Super Bowl halftime show was never the same again.

title: Who will Jay-Z bring out for the 2027 Super Bowl halftime show? Four possible guests
summary: Will Jay Z bring out any guests? If he does, here are some guesses of who they could be
full_text:
It's official: Jay-Z will take the stage for the Super Bowl halftime show on February 14, 2027, at SoFi Stadium. Jay-Z and his company, Roc Nation, are partners with the NFL on the halftime show, having produced the event since 2019. The rapper is a key decision-maker in who performs, and this year he chose himself.
While we know who the performer will be during the biggest game in American sports, we do not know who will be playing in the Super Bowl. We'll have to wait until the last day of January for that one.
Another mystery that remains is who, if anyone, will be his special guest(s). Many halftime show performers bring out additional artists, and while Jay-Z has not announced any yet, there is a good chance he will.
Here is a look at artists that he could bring out, based on their past history and collaborations:
Queen Bey is first on the list for obvious reasons. The superstar singer has been married to Jay-Z since 2018 and shares three children together.
The two have worked together numerous times, including their first collaboration before they were dating, "'03 Bonnie and Clyde." Their most popular song together is arguably "Crazy in Love," released in 2003. Other collaborations include "Drunk in Love," "Part II (On the Run)," "Deja Vu" and "Lift Off." They toured together, so they are used to sharing the same stage.
She also has a history of performing on the NFL stage. She headlined the 2013 halftime show and performed with Coldplay and Bruno Mars at halftime in 2016. She also sang the national anthem at Super Bowl XXXVIII in 2001, in her hometown of Houston. On Christmas Day 2024, she took the stage during halftime in Houston for what is commonly referred to as the "Beyoncé Bowl."
Jay-Z was pivotal in Rihanna's early success. In 2005, as CEO of Def Jam Records, Jay-Z had Rihanna audition for him and others, and the rest is history. She eventually left Def Jam for Roc Nation in 2010.
The two have multiple songs together, including "Umbrella," "Run This Town," and "FourFiveSeconds."
Earlier this year, she was a surprise guest at his tour, joining him on stage at Yankee Stadium, a main character in many of Jay-Z's songs.
Rihanna is another potential special guest, who is no stranger to the NFL. She was the Super Bowl headliner in 2023 and had one of the most memorable performances in recent history, announcing her pregnancy during the event.
Blu Ivy Carter is the oldest child of Jay-Z and Beyoncé. She performed as a dancer during Beyonce's 2024 Christmas Day halftime show in Houston. Blu Ivy also joined her mom for the Cowboy Carter tour, once again as a dancer. For being so young, she already has a huge fanbase, with concertgoers holding signs for her, yelling her name at shows and tweeting about her talents.
Not only has Ms. Carter performed on an NFL stage before, but she is also often seen attending NFL games with her dad. The Super Bowl halftime show could turn into a family affair.
Slim Shady joined Jay Z on stage during his current tour, and the two could have another reunion at the Super Bowl. The two collaborated on the song "Renegade" on Jay-Z's album The Blueprint.
Like the others on the list, Eminem has experience as an NFL performer. His comes via the 2022 Super Bowl, where he was a special guest on an iconic hip-hop lineup.

title: NFL makes rare double flex move by tweaking the schedule in Week 9 and Week 11
summary: The NFL just tweaked the schedule for two different weeks in November
full_text:
The NFL rarely announces two weeks' worth of schedule changes at the same time, but that's exactly what the league did Monday.
For just the second time this year , the NFL has decided to utilize its flex scheduling powers. This time around, the league is changing the television network for four games while tweaking the kickoff time for one of them.
Of the games that were rescheduled, two will kick off in Week 9, while the other two will take place in Week 11.
Let's take a look at the changes, starting with the two moves that got made in Week 9.
With this change, the Raiders-49ers game will now be moved into the prime viewing window for Week 9. Fox has the national doubleheader that week, and the network will now have three games to feature in the 4:25 p.m. ET window, with Packers-Patriots and Cardinals-Seahawks also airing on Fox at that time.
With 49ers-Raiders moving to Fox, the Texans at Chargers will be the only CBS game in the late window, kicking off at 4:05 p.m. ET.
Now, let's check out the changes for Week 11
The Bills will be moving from Fox to CBS in Week 11, which is certainly the notable news here. Fox actually had a Bills game earlier this season, which is probably one reason this flex went through: the network probably wouldn't have been thrilled to lose that game if it had been its only chance to feature Josh Allen this season.
With these four flex moves now in the books, there's still one big question to answer in Week 9 and that's whether the NFL ends up flexing the Sunday night game. The Buccaneers are currently scheduled to play in Chicago on Sunday night, but with Tampa Bay sitting at 2-5, the NFL could flex the game. The league has to decide whether to move the kickoff time by the end of the day on Tuesday (Oct. 27).
As things currently stand, this is the only Sunday night game on the Bears' schedule, so the NFL might be hesitant to move them out of it. Not to mention, the Bucs have won two of their past three games, so they've certainly looked more competitive over the past few weeks following a 0-4 start.
Based on those two facts, it wouldn't be surprising at all if the Buccaneers-Bears end up staying put.

title: Eagles vs. Cowboys prediction: Dallas visits injury-ravaged Philadelphia on 'Monday Night Football'
summary: Dallas has dropped two straight games, but Philadelphia enters the NFC East matchup without Jalen Hurts
full_text:
In the Week 7 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Philadelphia Eagles play host to the division rival Dallas Cowboys .
Philadelphia has lost four consecutive games after starting the season 2-0, and enters this game ravaged by injuries. Not only is Jalen Hurts out in the wake of blood clots being found in his calf and lungs, but DeVonta Smith , Dontayvion Wicks , Nolan Smith and more will also miss the game, while Saquon Barkley , Landon Dickerson , Jonathan Greenard and Jalyx Hunt are all questionable.
Dallas has lost back-to-back games in dispiriting fashion, with its offense sputtering at the worst possible time, combining for 29 points against the Buccaneers and Packers after scoring 30-plus in each of the previous three games. The defense was already under fire early in the season, and now the Cowboys have questions on the side of the ball where they were supposed to be elite.
Which of these two teams will stop their losing skid? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.
Dallas has struggled badly on offense over the last two weeks. The Cowboys did total over 300 yards against both the Buccaneers and the Packers, but those totals are misleading. They were entirely unable to deal with blitzes for essentially all of both contests, and that failure brutally undermined their passing attack. ( Dak Prescott , typically excellent against blitzing defenses, went just 20 of 38 for 194 scoreless yards when confronting extra rushers in those games.) They also ran the ball for a mere 98 yards combined in those two games, despite the fact that star guard Tyler Smith returned to the fold.
The struggles came a bit as a surprise considering the Cowboys had previously been cooking offensively, racking up yardage and points through the first four weeks of the season. But both Todd Bowles and Jonathan Gannon came out with a plan that toyed with Dallas' protection rules up front, and the Cowboys found themselves unable to respond. They'll need a significantly better plan on Monday night, but it's notable that the Eagles blitz far less often than the Bucs and Packers did against the Cowboys.
The Bucs and Packers sent extra rushers after Prescott on 38.8% of his dropbacks in Weeks 5 and 6, per Tru Media. The Eagles have blitzed just 24.1% of the time so far - the fourth-lowest rate in the NFL . Vic Fangio would have to significantly depart from his modus operandi for Philadelphia to employ a strategy similar to the one that dominated Dallas over the last two weeks. For what it's worth, Philly has blitzed on at least 38% of opponent dropbacks just once since Fangio became the team's defensive coordinator. It would be wildly out of character to break out such a strategy here - but it's one worth pursuing considering Dallas' struggles.
Philly checks in 20th in opponents' EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media, allowing opponents to complete only 60.4% of passes at an average of 7.0 yards per attempt, but giving up eight touchdown passes against just three interceptions and being helped along by 14 opponent drops - second-most in the league.
Cornerbacks Quinyon Mitchell , Riq Woolen and Cooper DeJean are tough to beat, but they have also been asked to cover for too long on some dropbacks because of the Eagles' inability to generate pressure. Philly has gotten a sack, hit or hurry on only 32.9% of opponent dropbacks, and they rank below-average in both average time to pressure and average time to throw. Quarterbacks, in other words, have been fairly comfortable in the pocket. And if you let Prescott get comfortable in the pocket, he can pick you apart with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens , among his other targets.
The Cowboys seem highly unlikely to find success running the ball, which they haven't done all year. Javonte Williams has seven rushing touchdowns, but he's also averaging only 3.7 yards per carry, down considerably from his 4.8 average last season. The offensive line is not clearing rushing lanes for him, and he's not making anybody miss to make up for it. It's a brutal combination, and with Philly allowing only 4.0 yards per carry, it's not an advantageous one here.
The Eagles enter this game just about as banged up as possible on offense. Quarterback Jalen Hurts is out. His top two receivers, DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, are also out. Guard Landon Dickerson remains on injured reserve, though he has been designated to return and listed as questionable for this game. Running back Saquon Barkley is questionable as well, and his top two backups — Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley — are on injured reserve.
Without Hurts under center last week, the Eagles operated with a pass-heavy bent. Tanner McKee dropped back to throw 48 times, and while some of that was due to game script and some of it due to Barkley's absence, it's worth noting that he had previously made two Week 18 starts and dropped back to pass an average of 44 times in those games as well. The Eagles can't use the quarterback run game with McKee under center like they can with Hurts, and the rest of their run-game efficiency is likely to suffer as a result of not presenting that threat to the defense. It's somewhat reasonable to expect them to be pass-heavier than we're used to here.
That may not be the case if Barkley returns to the lineup, but it is at least somewhat difficult to parse what the Eagles would prefer to do in that situation. Barkley has actually averaged 5.5 yards per carry in each of the two games he's made it through healthy this season. The problem is that the rest of the backs have been extremely inefficient in his absence and he wasn't efficient before leaving the other two games due to injury, either. He fully practiced on Friday for the first time since his hamstring injury, but the team may not want to load him up with too many touches in his first game back in the fold.
Every team that is humanly capable of running the football (i.e., not the Texans or Packers) has done so at will against the Cowboys this season, with Dallas' other five opponents each piling up at least 165 yards on the ground. Opponents have clipped the Cowboys for 4.7 yards per carry, with running backs and quarterbacks alike able to find considerable room to run against a disappointingly friendly Dallas front. If the Eagles can get Barkley (or Dameon Pierce ) going early, they might be able to lean on the Cowboys and prevent the game from turning into the kind of track meet that Dallas' offense would prefer.
Opponents have also generally been able to throw all over the Cowboys, though it will obviously be difficult for the Eagles to do so while down their top two receivers and multiple of their expected starting offensive linemen. It'll be Makai Lemon , Darius Cooper and Dallas Goedert as McKee's top targets here. It'll be interesting to see if the Cowboys send Joey Porter Jr . to follow one of Cooper (who plays outside) or Lemon (usually in the slot, where he would match up more often with Caleb Downs ), as well as how they align their secondary now that Cobie Durant is set to return and potentially push the struggling (to say it kindly) Daron Bland to the bench.
If the Cowboys can put any semblance of pressure on McKee, he could struggle badly. He's just 16 of 45 for 179 scoreless yards in his career when under duress, with a 15.1% sack rate as well. The Cowboys don't rush the passer particularly well, but with the current state of Philly's offensive line, that could change on Monday night.
I just don't think the Cowboys should be favored by more than a field goal against anybody right now, given how they're playing on both sides of the ball. I'll take Dallas to win given the state of the Eagles' offense, but I can't see the Cowboys blowing anyone out in their current state.
Prediction: Cowboys 24, Eagles 20

title: NFL trade rumors: 4 potential landing spots for Maxx Crosby if Raiders decide to sell at deadline
summary: As the Raiders stumble to 3-4 ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline, contenders like the Bears and Bills could pursue the star pass rusher to fuel a playoff push
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders have now gone from 3-0 to 3-4. Just a few weeks ago, they were one of the biggest surprises in the NFL , but have since become a losing team that could be making a quarterback change in the near future. Their swift fall from undefeated to losing record could also change how the organization approaches the upcoming trade deadline.
It's again time to debate if the Raiders should trade one of their best players, pass rusher Maxx Crosby . We listed him as a player we would like to see get a change of scenery recently, but it remains to be seen if that's in the cards for Vegas. Crosby was traded to the Baltimore Ravens this offseason for two first-round picks. However, the Ravens backed out of the deal when their staff discovered something worrisome during the in-person physical.
ESPN's Adam Schefter mentioned recently that it's unknown if Crosby is pushing for a trade behind closed doors, as he was several months ago. Maybe he viewed the canceled trade with Baltimore as divine intervention signaling he was meant to be a Raider for life. Plus, what would Vegas want for him at this point? It's hard to imagine the Raiders fetching two first-round picks again.
With that said, senior NFL writer Pete Prisco argued on CBS Sports HQ this past Sunday that the Raiders should trade Crosby and pick up further draft capital to help in the rebuild they are currently in. Those picks, he said, could be used when Fernando Mendoza eventually takes over.
Should the Raiders try to trade Maxx Crosby before the NFL Trade Deadline? 🤔 @PriscoCBS says it should be heavily considered. #NFLPostgame pic.twitter.com/azjOOezxuD
Maybe Crosby only fetches a first-round pick and a fourth-round pick this time around. Is that good enough for Raiders' GM John Spytek to consider? Crosby is one of the best defensive ends in the NFL. Not only does he get after quarterbacks, having recorded four double-digit sack seasons, but no player has recorded more tackles for loss (136) since Crosby entered the league in 2019. His 25 pressures this season rank second in the NFL behind Greg Rousseau .
The Raiders trading Crosby prior to the Nov. 10 deadline would be a bit surprising. If they decided to part ways with a star talent, where could Crosby land? Let's take a look at four potential landing spots.
The Chicago Bears were deemed the prime regression candidate in the NFC this year following their magical 11-6 campaign in 2025, when they registered an NFL-record seven wins when trailing in the final two minutes of the fourth quarter, including playoffs. But with Caleb Williams under center, who says Chicago has to regress? The Bears do have some tough games coming up against the Seattle Seahawks , Detroit Lions , Jacksonville Jaguars and Buffalo Bills , but through seven weeks, Chicago is sitting pretty at 5-2.
The Bears' pass rush could be improved. It's pretty unbelievable that cornerback Kyler Gordon has played in just two games this season and is tied with Austin Booker for the team lead with four sacks. Chicago also just saw Montez Sweat get suspended two games for violating the NFL's performance-enhancing drugs policy, while Dayo Odeyingbo is currently out with a quadriceps injury. The Bears make sense for Crosby if he's moved.
There's another team in the NFC North where Crosby could potentially be a fit, and it's the team he grew up rooting for. The Lions are actually tied for the league lead in sacks this season with 21, but the defense still ranks dead last with 391.0 yards allowed per game.
I think it's possible Kelvin Sheppard's unit is on the upswing. Not only did they hold Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers to 17 points on Sunday, but Brian Branch is back in the lineup, and Kerby Joseph could be back soon as well. Imagine if the Lions added Crosby to rush the passer opposite of Aidan Hutchinson ? Maybe this is more wishful thinking, but the Lions could become the new favorite in the NFC North if they made this deal.
Some people, like myself, thought the Dallas Cowboys defense was going to be much improved in 2026. That has not been the case, as they rank third-worst in total yards allowed per game (382.5) entering their Monday night matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles .
The Cowboys took a swing on former Pittsburgh Steelers corner Joey Porter Jr. , and they could make another deal in acquiring a pass rusher to help boost a unit that is tied for fourth-worst in sacks with eight. This would be an aggressive and controversial swing of the bat from Jerry Jones.
Let's get a little wild. The Bills made it clear they were " Super Bowl or bust" when they fired Sean McDermott last year, but this Jim Leonhard defense needs some work. Buffalo has won four games this year, and all four victories came in matchups where the Bills allowed 30+ points! The rest of the NFL was 8-42 through Week 6 in games where defenses allowed at least 30 points. The Bills ranked first in points per drive (3.13) and last in points per drive allowed (2.76) after Week 6.
Imagine pairing Greg Rousseau and Deone Walker with a talent like Crosby, and what that could do for this defense and team at large.

title: NFL trade deadline matchmaker: Vikings add Jonathan Taylor to boost offense, Chiefs nab WR
summary: Moves for several contenders who could look to buy
full_text:
For much of October, reports will tell of teams that could be willing to buy or sell waiting to see how the next few weeks will go. A potential seller wins a few games, and all of a sudden, maybe that team wants to keep more key players than originally thought. A couple of losses from a potential buyer could mean that team isn't so keen on making a win-now move. A lot can and does change in the NFL every week.
But now the end of October has arrived, and the trade deadline is two weeks away. Phone lines are buzzing, and Week 7 revealed some more notable concerns for potential buyers. Does that mean sellers will take advantage sooner rather than later? With big names such as Jonathan Taylor and Saquon Barkley being floated as potential trade targets this trade season, we play matchmaker for several top teams looking to patch up their rosters for the stretch run of the regular season and beyond.
The need: Help on offense The solution: RB Jonathan Taylor
The NFL's only undefeated team, Minnesota, moved to 6-0 with a 16-10 win over the Colts . That sort of score has been the norm. The Vikings have 10 touchdowns this season, the fewest by any 6-0 team since the 1934 Lions . 1934!
The Kyler Murray experience has been a rough one. He'll produce a big play or two with his legs or his arm, but the down-to-down consistency hasn't been close to good enough. He is 27th in sack rate, 29th in passing success rate and 31st in touchdown rate.
Surprisingly, the Vikings score on 41.5% of their drives, 12th in the NFL, but that's been a lot of Will Reichard field goals. Taylor, meanwhile, is a scoring machine, and he'd provide explosiveness to the running game, too. The Vikings saw it up close and personal Sunday, with Taylor totaling 110 yards from scrimmage and a touchdown. Aaron Jones has been playing through a knee injury, which he aggravated Sunday. The Vikings can't risk wasting their Super Bowl-caliber defense. Taylor is the solution.
The need: Running back The solution: RB Saquon Barkley
The Bengals are up to 4-2 on the young season after a beatdown of the Ravens . Joe Burrow and co. don't particularly like running the ball, and perhaps the reason why is that the offense only averages 3.6 yards per carry.
It's been a disappointing year for Chase Brown . His -0.6 yards per attempt over expected is among the worst in the NFL, and it seemingly isn't clicking for him. Enter Barkley, who is actually producing 1.15 yards per rush over expected despite pretty much everything around him falling apart. Only four players — Kenneth Walker III , Jaylen Warren , Bijan Robinson and Kyle Monangai — have a higher rate. The Bengals made a blockbuster move for Dexter Lawrence this year despite concerns about his age and productivity, and it has been hugely successful so far. Barkley could be a similar spark, especially with defenses devoting so much attention to Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins .
The need: Another disruptor up front The solution: DL Jeffery Simmons
Even with big leaps from defensive tackle Deone Walker and EDGE Greg Rousseau , the Bills are 24th in defensive rushing success rate, and with Ed Oliver's injury issues, Buffalo has been iffy up front outside of Walker. Buffalo has long maintained the status quo at the deadline, but this is the year to change that in a big way.
Simmons is a superstar — one of the best defenders on the planet, regardless of position. Could you imagine combining him with Walker? Legitimately terrifying. It would also help a leaky secondary. When opposing quarterbacks aren't pressured, the Bills are getting shredded: 30th in defensive EPA per play and dead last in defensive success rate. That has to change.
The need: Downfield passing The solution: WR Adonai Mitchell
The Chiefs fell from the ranks of the undefeated with a humbling 20-3 loss to the Seahawks that exposed multiple issues. One of the biggest was the complete lack of a downfield passing attack. Patrick Mahomes attempted three passes 20+ yards downfield and connected on zero of them. It was his most such attempts without a completion since Week 16, 2024.
Kansas City's downfield passing game has gone out the window ever since Tyquan Thornton's injury. Mahomes didn't even attempt a pass 20+ yards downfield last week against the Chargers , just the second time that's happened in his entire career. Thornton still has more than half of Mahomes' completions 20+ yards downfield this year (4) despite not having played since Week 4. No other Chiefs pass catcher has more than one.
As fun as it would be to send George Pickens to Kansas City, the Cowboys seem dead set on trying to win this year. Mitchell was actually off to a strong start this season before a finger injury. Omar Cooper Jr . has shined the past two weeks, and when Mitchell returned in Week 7, he only played 44% of the offensive snaps.
The need: Interior defensive linemen The solution: DL DeForest Buckner
Buckner made it clear last week he wants to play for a winner, and the Colts don't look like a winner any time soon. The Packers , meanwhile, are 4-3 and look like they could be a legitimate contender, especially when Micah Parsons returns. The defense has rounded into shape without him, and that's even with significant injuries on the interior of the line. Buckner has been a very good — and at times dominant — player this year. The Packers are down some draft capital after the Parsons trade last year, but Buckner, at 32 and in the last year of his contract, wouldn't be prohibitively expensive.
The need: Secondary help The solution: CB Tariq Woolen
Woolen came to Philadelphia on a one-year deal to fill the hole at outside cornerback opposite Quinyon Mitchell , and he has done a decent job. Opponents are completing under half of their passes and averaging just 6.2 yards per attempt when Woolen is the primary defender this season. The Lions were in on Joey Porter Jr . before he ultimately ended up on the Cowboys. This could be another solid option for much, much cheaper. The Eagles figure to be sellers given the disastrous run of injuries on the offensive side of the ball.
The need: Help up front The solution: EDGE Khalil Mack
Not all reunions make sense. This one does. The Bears actually rank seventh in pressure rate and third in sack rate this season, but they could still use some pass rush juice on the edge. Chicago is 18th in pressure rate when not bringing a blitzer from pass coverage. The Chargers are obvious sellers, and Mack is still effective: three sacks and seven quick pressures, which is more than any current Bears EDGE.
The need: More push up front The solution: DL Daron Payne
The 49ers rank 29th in percentage of opponent plays that go for zero or negative yards. Enter the stout Payne, who not only remains a solid player himself, but would free things up for offseason acquisition Osa Odighizuwa on the interior. Payne's counting numbers aren't anything special, but he ranks 21st in PFF's run defense grade among 136 interior defensive linemen. Payne is in the final year of his deal, and Commanders GM Adam Peters used to be in San Francisco's front office. There's a deal to be made here.
The need: Offensive line reinforcements The solution: OL Kevin Zeitler
A longtime stalwart who was playing solidly as recently as last year, Zeitler signed with the Packers less than a month ago amid major offensive line issues in Green Bay. But he is yet to play an offensive snap and was a healthy scratch in Week 7. It just might not be working out, and if that's the case, Green Bay could be eager to recoup any draft capital for him.
New England, with injuries up and down the offensive line, could make sense as a buy-low candidate. Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) is on IR, and Ben Brown (knee) missed Week 7. Mike Onwenu (ankle) is out for most, if not all, of the rest of the season. Onwenu's replacement, Greg Van Roten (thigh), is also on IR.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Garrett Wilson trade destinations: Chiefs, 49ers among three potential landing spots for Jets star
summary: Kansas City needs another weapon for Patrick Mahomes, but two other teams should also consider calling New York
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is fast approaching. As the league gears up for the Nov. 10 deadline, there will be several star players who'll have their names thrown into the rumor mill . One of those names could end up being Jets star wideout Garrett Wilson , especially as his frustrations with the offense appeared to boil over on the sideline during Sunday's loss to the Dolphins .
Wilson could be seen yelling in a huddle that consisted of Geno Smith and passing-game coordinator Seth Ryan. The 26-year-old said his anger wasn't directed at Smith and that he was frustrated with the red-zone play-calling. Whatever the reason for the outburst, it does show some possible cracks in Wilson's relationship with the team, which comes in the thick of trade rumor season.
Last year, the Jets had a fire sale, shipping away the likes of Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams for future draft capital. Wilson was notably not among the players shopped, as the Jets viewed him as part of their future, but what if that changes in a year? In the event that New York decides to move off of Wilson this time around, here's a look at three teams that would be more than happy to take him off their hands.
NFL on CBS analyst and former Super Bowl champion Russell Wilson was the first to float the possibility of the Chiefs pursuing Wilson on a previous edition of "Set Hut!" and it's hard to disagree with him. If New York does put Wilson on the block, Kansas City makes a ton of sense as a potential destination. The team has been hit with injuries to its receiver room, with Tyquan Thornton on injured reserve and Rashee Rice (hamstring) sidelined. In the Week 7 loss to Seattle, the offense mustered just three points, and the Chiefs wide receivers combined for six catches for 39 yards.
Garrett Wilson to Chiefs? @DangeRussWilson thinks the Chiefs should trade for Garrett Wilson pic.twitter.com/PRHRrVVLpq
Sure, Rice will be back at some point, but Kansas City could use another top-tier weapon as they gear up for another Super Bowl run. More than just what Wilson can do for the Chiefs in 2026, he'd also be a long-term option for the organization that doesn't have a clear go-to option for Patrick Mahomes in the passing game whenever Travis Kelce decides to retire. Wilson would fill those shoes perfectly.
The Niners are another team currently starved for wide receiver help. During Sunday's loss to the Falcons , they barely had any healthy bodies at the receiver position, with Jordan Watkins , Jacob Cowing , and Brandin Cooks seeing the bulk of the snaps. That's because injuries have hit the position group, as Deebo Samuel Jr. and Mike Evans have been sidelined. Given that the team is entering the bye in Week 8, that should be enough time to get one or both back, but they could still stand to deepen the room.
Wilson would come in and immediately rival for some high-value targets from Brock Purdy and send what has already been a high-powered San Francisco offense to another stratosphere. The 49ers are 6-1 and have a two-game cushion in the NFC West. They're firmly in a Super Bowl window, and Wilson is just the type of midseason addition that could help put them over the top.
The Raiders ' current four-game losing skid doesn't exactly scream "buyers" at the deadline, but a talent like Wilson doesn't come around very often. While Las Vegas wants to be competitive in 2026, they are a rebuilding team that will, at some point, turn the keys over to Fernando Mendoza , the first overall pick at the 2026 NFL Draft . When they do, they'll want to ensure that he's in the best possible situation to succeed. Giving him a true No. 1 wideout like Wilson to complement the likes of tight end Brock Bowers and running back Ashton Jeanty would go a long way toward him hitting the ground running.
Remember, Wilson is still only 26 years old and signed through 2030. This is an ascending player who is just stepping into his prime, which makes him an ideal target for a Raiders team that doesn't have any household names at receiver. Currently, Tre Tucker , Jalen Nailor , and Cody White headline the receiver room. Wilson would arrive and immediately sit atop the depth chart.
