title: Garrett Wilson explains heated Jets sideline moment, says frustration wasn't directed at Geno Smith
summary: The star receiver acknowledged that he was unhappy with New York's red-zone play calls during an animated conversation
full_text:
The New York Jets hit a potential rock bottom Sunday after falling to the previously winless Miami Dolphins , dropping the franchise to 2-5 on the year. Amid that divisional upset at home, patience had seemingly started to wear thin, specifically when it comes to wideout Garrett Wilson .
During the broadcast, CBS cameras captured the Jets star pass catcher having an animated conversation on the sideline. From the looks of things, Wilson appears to be yelling towards a huddle of Geno Smith and passing-game coordinator Seth Ryan. When asked about it postgame, Wilson said he was not directing his frustrations at Smith and acknowledged he was upset with the red-zone play calls.
"We were collaborating," said Wilson, via ESPN . "I don't even think I was talking to Geno. I think we were both heated, but not at each other at all. We were just disappointed with how we were playing up to that point and wanted to be a little more aggressive. That's what that was."
For his part, Smith also didn't think Wilson was directing anything towards him.
"He might have been yelling, but I don't think he was yelling at me," he said.
Jets WR Garrett Wilson appeared frustrated on the sidelines during the team's loss vs. the Dolphins. (📺 CBS) pic.twitter.com/tMhvk78oC2
In the loss, Wilson -- the highest-paid player on the team -- saw only three targets, catching two passes for 26 yards. That said, Smith was able to find some success through the air via different pass-catching outlets like rookie wideout Omar Cooper Jr . (five catches, 115 yards receiving and a touchdown) and tight end Mason Taylor (five catches, 62 yards receiving and two touchdowns). Still, the offense is at its best when Wilson is involved.
"I think we can all do a better job of finding ways to get him more targets and more touches," Smith said. "But the ball has to go where it goes based on coverage."
Through seven games, Wilson has caught 37 of his team-high 51 targets for 444 receiving yards and three receiving touchdowns. Over the last two games, he's seen nine targets. Smith and Wilson were reportedly seen in the locker room having a conversation after coming out of the shower and walking to their lockers. Wilson said the talk was focused on finding a resolution.
"Just trying to figure out how we can fix where we're at right now, wanting to get it in our hands and make a difference and try to win these games that we feel like we're a better team -- and we're not," he said.
"Like I've said before, I want it in my hands to try and make an impact. So that's all we were talking about, just putting it in our hands and how we can make that happen, being aggressive throughout and keeping ourselves out of those situations so we can win these games."
The Jets have lost two straight and will look to stop the skid and get Wilson back on track next week as they host a Las Vegas Raiders team that has surrendered 35.8 points per game over their current four-game losing streak.
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: Colts' Shane Steichen has 'not thought' about QB change despite Daniel Jones' struggles
summary: Anthony Richardson and Riley Leonard offer little evidence that either would represent an upgrade
full_text:
Quarterback Daniel Jones was a primary reason why the Indianapolis Colts opened the 2025 season on a hot streak, but he is now a key factor in the team's dreadful start to 2026. Jones ranks among the NFL's least efficient passers through Week 7 and struggled mightily in the Colts' latest loss: A 16-10 rock fight with the Minnesota Vikings . Despite his rough first two months of the campaign, though, coach Shane Steichen said he has no plans to make a quarterback change.
That leaves Jones entrenched in the lineup for a 2-5 team that ranks 25th in total offense per game.
"I have not thought about a quarterback change," Steichen said after the loss to Minnesota . "I've got a ton of faith in Daniel. The game plan today was to go in and run the football. Obviously, at the end, he had the interception. That happens in football."
The interception in question was a game-sealer. Indianapolis had possession with 1:39 to play on Sunday and needed a touchdown to take a late and potentially decisive lead. Two plays into the Colts' final drive of the game, Jones threw a devastating pick to Vikings safety Harrison Smith . He finished the contest 13-for-22 for 108 yards and took four sacks.
Few quarterbacks have been able to move the ball with any kind of consistency against the ferocious Vikings defense, to be fair. But Jones was a uniquely favorable matchup for Minnesota, considering he has been one of the NFL's worst quarterbacks under pressure this season. The Vikings are the league's most proficient team at pressuring the signal-caller, and coordinator Brian Flores uncorked the pass rush to a historic extent in Week 7 by blitzing Jones on 85.2% of his dropbacks. That was the highest blitz rate by any defense in a game in the Next Gen Stats era (since 2016).
Jones said it "means a lot" to have his coach's confidence after such a rough showing.
"It's my job to play well, to put the team in position to win games," Jones said . "I gotta do a better job of that. I certainly understand that. We all gotta go back to work. I gotta go back to work, see where I can be better."
Among 33 qualified passers
The unfortunate reality for the Colts is that they might be better off with this version of Jones than with either Anthony Richardson or Riley Leonard as their starter. Richardson remains the backup in his fourth NFL season, while the Colts have been designating Leonard as inactive but keeping him available as the emergency third quarterback. Neither backup has any track record of productivity, and both have lower ceilings than Jones displayed in his breakout start to last season.
Indianapolis declined Richardson's fifth-year option but could give him another look in the final year of his rookie contract. Anything the Colts get out of the former No. 4 overall pick would be a bonus at this point, because he is no longer part of the team's long-term plans following a massively disappointing start to his career in which he made just 15 starts over three years and threw more interceptions (13) than touchdowns (11) while completing only 50.6% of his throws. Richardson never developed as a passer and remains only a highly athletic rushing weapon.
Leonard, in his second year as a former sixth-round pick, might not offer much more in the way of passing ability. He made five appearances and one start as a rookie and went 39-for-67 for 415 yards with two touchdowns and three interceptions. While he is also a running threat, the fact that he did not beat Richardson for the No. 2 job indicates the Notre Dame product is even less of an option.
One of the final significant moves of Chris Ballard's tenure as general manager before the Colts fired him this month was to extend Jones on a two-year deal. It was a questionable signing in March, considering Jones was coming off a torn Achilles, and so far it has not paid off. Even worse, it ties Indianapolis to Jones through 2027 at a high price.
Jones earns an average annual salary of $44 million and is guaranteed $60 million over the life of the two-year contract. He will carry a $46.8 million salary cap hit next season, so the Colts are likely committed to him as the starter for another year. The hope, of course, is that he will return to the form he showed at the start of 2025 as he becomes further removed from his Achilles tear. But if he does not, then he will be immensely expensive for what he is: One of the league's least productive starting quarterbacks.
Richardson will likely be out of the picture next year, and Leonard is expendable with an annual salary of $1.1 million and effectively no dead cap hit should the Colts release him. Indianapolis could entirely retool the quarterback room behind Jones.
If Indianapolis is not confident in Jones' ability to rebound next year, it could target a quarterback in the draft. This is where the Colts feel the ramifications of the poorly aged Sauce Gardner trade, because that deal leaves them without a first-round pick in 2027.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Packers blast officiating after loss to Lions: 'It's bulls---' and 'f---ing up the games'
summary: Safety Xavier McKinney unloaded on the referees following a 20-17 defeat, calling out phantom penalties that kept key drives alive for Detroit and that drew criticism from Tom Brady
full_text:
The Green Bay Packers had their three-game win streak snapped on Sunday, as Jared Goff and the rival Detroit Lions defeated them, 20-17. While Packers kicker Trey Smack missed a 35-yard field goal with 3:25 remaining in the fourth quarter, setting the stage for a Lions' game-winning drive, there were several questionable officiating calls that played into Detroit's favor as well.
In all, Green Bay was penalized eight times for 81 yards. Many of those calls, though, were called into question and outright blasted by the Packers. Safety Xavier McKinney felt it was necessary to make it clear how disgusted he was with the calls on Sunday, calling them "bullshit" after the game.
"I don't know how the NFL's going to treat it, but I'm not a big fan of the refs right now," McKinney said . "I don't think it's great officiating, if I'm being completely honest. I think it's bullshit a lot of the times."
One of the most controversial calls was a roughing-the-passer penalty on Karl Brooks with 2:45 remaining in the fourth quarter, adding 15 yards to an 18-yard gain by Sam LaPorta . Even Fox commentator and legendary quarterback Tom Brady couldn't hide his disgust. "What is that? There's no way," Brady said. "That's definitely not roughing the passer."
pic.twitter.com/l2ggK8Lq2I
Many of the questionable calls involved personal foul penalties that either seemed like a stretch or were completely unclear. Earlier in the third quarter, the Lions were given an automatic first down when Brenton Cox Jr . was called for roughing the passer after attempting to catch himself while fighting through a block. He did put his hands on Goff, but did not extend or make any illegal action that could have qualified as roughing the passer. At least, that's what Brady and rules analyst Dean Blandino believe.
Very questionable roughing the passer call against the #Packers that everyone on the telecast disagreed with, including Tom Brady, who said: “I don’t like it either.” 🤷🏻‍♂️ pic.twitter.com/40PiMm91Ri
"I don't know," Cox said about his penalty, per ESPN . "I'm trying to give you a good answer, but it's disappointing that these are veteran guys -- I'm not trying to go after the refs -- well-informed guys, and I feel like you've got to know the difference between what's intentional and what's not."
In the third quarter, Devonte Wyatt was flagged for unnecessary roughness after he took down Amon-Ra St. Brown , who got up with the ball and tried to run as if the play was still alive. Wyatt slung St. Brown down, who accidentally cleated an official in the gut. The ref threw the flag from his back.
Fighting breaking out between the Packers and the Lions and the ref takes a cleat straight to the gut pic.twitter.com/H18GgBCUZH
"There was no whistle blown, and the guy continued to run, and our guy didn't hear a whistle -- he continued to play too, and then we get called for a penalty," said Packers head coach Matt LaFleur after the game. "So I don't know. They were trying to tell me the play was obviously dead. I'm like, 'How do you know if you don't hear a whistle?' So I don't know if you guys heard a whistle. I did not hear a whistle."
Overall, LaFleur didn't want to address the penalties. He knew he would be subject to fines if he lashed out for the officials' rough afternoon.
"I don't even want to comment on any of the penalties," LaFleur said. "I just -- it is what it is. You got to play above it, and I thought there were some tough calls, but it is what it is."
McKinney, who said he didn't care about being fined by the NFL for complaining about the officiating, argued the phantom penalties killed momentum for the Packers, and that the calls simply don't make sense.
"It's annoying even talking about it because these are critical drives throughout the game, and we might have a drive where we're getting stops but you're calling penalties, and it's like, this is not a penalty," McKinney said. "To me, it just don't really make any sense, and it's killing our momentum, it's killing our drives, and it's kind of f---ing up the games, if I'm being honest.
"I would rather get fined and try to help my team out because I see what's going on, and it's killing us."
Packers cornerback Keisean Nixon also sounded off on the officiating, saying he felt the calls were clearly one-sided. Calls that went against the Packers could have also easily gone against the Lions, he thought.
"We can't really leave it in the refs' hands, it can always go both ways, they clearly don't like Jordan Love . They don't throw nothing on him ever," Nixon said, via WLUK-TV Fox 11 .
On the first play of the fourth quarter, Love was called for intentional grounding despite tight end Tucker Kraft clearly being the intended target. Referee Alex Moore told PFWA pool reporter Ben Raven that it was called since the pass did not reach the line of scrimmage, but Brady flat-out said this was "definitely not grounding" on the telecast.
This has to be the LATEST grounding penalty I have ever seen. Love called for grounding while targeting Tucker Kraft pic.twitter.com/pQEQq4XsiE
In what is good news for the Packers, they will have to shift their focus to Week 8 quickly, as they host the Carolina Panthers on "Thursday Night Football."
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Cowboys announce halftime show artist for Thanksgiving game vs. Eagles
summary: Miranda Lambert is the 30th Red Kettle Kickoff halftime performer
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys have a long history of playing on Thanksgiving, and this year they will host the Philadelphia Eagles in an NFC East clash. The tradition of playing on Turkey Day also includes a special halftime show performance.
This year, Miranda Lambert will take the AT&T Stadium stage between the football action on Thursday, Nov. 26, the Cowboys announced on Sunday. The game and halftime show will be broadcast on Fox, with fans at home able to enjoy the music as well. Kickoff is set for 4:30 p.m. ET.
JUST ANNOUNCED: @mirandalambert will take the stage for The Salvation Army's 30th Red Kettle Kickoff Halftime Show at our Thanksgiving Day game on FOX ⭐️ pic.twitter.com/W9jlR9czWn
This marks the 30th consecutive Red Kettle Kickoff halftime performance, which marks the start of The Salvation Army's annual Red Kettle Campaign. The campaign encourages fans to give back and support local programs to help those in need.
"There's something special about how music brings people together, especially when it's to spread joy and hope to families who need it most," Lambert said in the press release. "The Salvation Army and the Dallas Cowboys have built an incredible tradition with the Red Kettle Kickoff, and I can't wait to be back home in Texas this Thanksgiving to help carry it forward."
Lambert is a successful country artist and songwriter, with 31 Grammy nominations, three Grammy wins, 40 Academy of Country Music Awards and 14 Country Music Association Awards. She is the most-awarded artist in the Academy of Country Music's history. The singer released her most recent album, "Crisco," earlier this month, continuing her streak of 11 consecutive top 10 country albums.
Her resume also includes being a New York Times bestselling author and a non-profit co-founder. Her MuttNation Foundation has raised over $15 million, encouraging shelter pet adoption, supporting rescue organizations across the nation and helping shelters after natural disasters.
The Cowboys have played on Thanksgiving since 1966, with the exception of 1975 and 1977, when the St. Louis Cardinals were given the holiday game. Last year, the Cowboys beat the Kansas City Chiefs 31-28 on Thanksgiving. The last time they lost on the holiday was in 2021, an overtime defeat against the Las Vegas Raiders .
The Cowboys currently sit at 2-4 and are in third place in the NFC East. They play on Monday night in a divisional game against the 2-4 Philadelphia Eagles.
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: Raiders considering 'everything' amid losing streak, including potential Fernando Mendoza turn
summary: Las Vegas has dropped four consecutive games after a 3-0 start, potentially moving the franchise closer to Mendoza
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders have slammed back down to earth after initially being one of the surprise teams of September. Following a 3-0 start, the team has endured a four-game losing streak, with Sunday's 35-21 home loss to the Los Angeles Rams dropping them below .500 for the first time in 2026.
Now with a losing record, it's fair to wonder whether the organization's approach may shift with more of an eye towards 2027, which could result in a change under center.  At some point, the Raiders are going to turn the keys of the franchise over to No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza , and that date may be getting closer, especially if the losses persist.
"I think we have to go watch the film," coach Klint Kubiak said Sunday when asked if it's time to start thinking about the future and potentially turning to Mendoza. "I think at this point, we're thinking about everything. How to fix our problems, how to fix our issues in the red zone, in the third quarter, personnel, scheme. We've got to talk about all of it."
Mendoza has already tasted playing time, making his debut back in Week 5 in garbage time during a loss to the Patriots . Kubiak said Sunday that there was no thought of putting Mendoza in over the course of the second half on Sunday.
Kirk Cousins hasn't been the entire problem for Las Vegas, but the veteran quarterback has also regressed from his 3-0 start to begin the season. Over this four-game losing streak, he's completing 60% of his passes compared to the 67.4% completion rate he had during the first three weeks of the year.
"It's really the same every day that it was in March or April," Cousins said postgame when asked about eventually being unseated by Mendoza. "I mean, nothing changes in the sense that if I'm not the best option then I don't want to be out there, either. I want our football team to have the best chance to win games, and if the first OTA if that had become apparent, I would have been the first one to say, 'Yeah, you can't play me.'
"So nothing changes, you know, and the organization will do what they feel is best. I feel that, you know, Fernando's done a great job and has a bright future ahead, and I'm going to try to go out there and play as well as I possibly can and help us win and give him a great example to learn from, until he does go out there eventually."
Again, while some of those numbers are down, it's not like Cousins has been bad enough to warrant a benching on his own, but the circumstances could create a perfect storm where it happens anyway.
The biggest reason for the Raiders' return to Earth has been the regression on defense, as they've faced some of the game's elite quarterbacks, including Patrick Mahomes , Josh Allen , Drake Maye and Matthew Stafford . During the losing streak, the defense has allowed opponents to average 35.8 points per game with 11 total passing touchdowns allowed.
That poor play on the defensive side of the ball should factor into any decision Kubiak makes at quarterback. With the unit playing this poorly, does it make sense to throw Mendoza in and ask him to repeatedly try to keep his team in the game? Those poor game scripts could prevent Mendoza from building the best foundation moving forward.
The Raiders will be on the road for four of their next five games before hitting the Week 13 bye. If these losses continue to mount, Mendoza will be thrust in under center at some point to try to give this 2026 team a spark as well as build towards 2027 and beyond.
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: Chiefs may have a Harrison Butker problem: Andy Reid says KC kicker 'gotta fix it'
summary: Butker missed two field goals during Kansas City's Week 7 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs may have a kicking problem on their hands. Longtime placekicker Harrison Butker hasn't been as sharp as he has been at times during his tenure with KC, and the warts were all too apparent in the team's 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday night.
Butker failed to connect on two of his three field goal attempts, with each of those misses proving to be massive gut punches and momentum killers. The first came just before halftime. While it was a sluggish start for the Kansas City offense as it faced a lethal Seattle defense, it had an opportunity to cut into the 10-0 deficit just before the break thanks to a 65-yard interception return by corner Nohl Williams .
After a 4-yard gain by Kenneth Walker inched them a little closer, Butker trotted out for a 58-yard attempt, but it didn't have the leg.
FG attempt is short and the Seahawks maintain their 10-point lead. KCvsSEA on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/vnhaC6WufL
While Butker connected on a 50-yard field goal in the third quarter, he again failed to come up in the clutch for the Chiefs later in the second half. With just under nine minutes to play in regulation, Butker came out for a 45-yard attempt, which would've brought the Chiefs within a touchdown (and extra point) of tying the game. Instead, it was wide right, with an emphasis on wide.
harrison butker noooo good pic.twitter.com/1pBD7hX7rD
"He's been one of the most consistent kickers in football," head coach Andy Reid said of Butker postgame. "He's off a bit, so gotta fix it."
Mostly, Butker's struggles have come from long range. This season, he's connecting on just 33.3% of kicks from 50-plus yards (2-of-6). Since the start of last season, Butker is 7-of-15 from 50-plus yards (50%).
While the long-range issues have been a big chunk of the problem, Butler has also missed five PATs since the start of last season. Combined with 10 missed field goals, Butler's 15 missed kicks since the start of last season are the most in the NFL , per CBS Sports Research. That's 35 points the Chiefs have lost because of Butker's misses during that time span.
As Reid cautioned, Butker has to fix these issues and be a more reliable option in the kicking game for Kansas City, especially as it pushes toward getting back into the playoffs. Because KC missed the postseason last year, Butker's kicking problems haven't reached that make-or-break portion of the calendar. Over his past two playoff runs (2023 and 2024), Butker has been perfect, netting all 15 of his field goals (two from 50-plus) and all 13 of his extra points.
That predates these recent struggles, however, and if they persist this time around, it could very well be the difference between the Chiefs getting back to the Super Bowl and ultimately hoisting another Lombardi Trophy or not.
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: Giants among NFL's biggest Week 7 winners; today's rare Sports Equinox with World Series, MNF, WNBA Finals
summary: Plus highlights from UFC 333, another chaotic weekend of college football and blockbuster NHL trade
full_text:
This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here .
The featherweight championship bout between Alexander Volkanovski and Movsar Evloev was the main event at UFC 333 and was an excellent fight in its own right with Volkanovski retaining his title via second-round TKO . But the most entertaining bout of the night came in the prelims when Petr Yan defended his bantamweight championship against Merab Dvashvili . Yan won by unanimous decision in a thriller our Brent Brookhouse said might go down as the Fight of the Year. The win was one that only Yan could have pulled off , said Brian Campbell.
Earlier in the night, Aaron Pico scored a brutal knockout of Losene Keita and called out ranked fighters for avoiding him , and Lone'er Kavanagh bounced back from a loss with a knockout of Ramazan Temirov .
In the wake of these results, our experts would like to see the following fights scheduled , among others:
And while we're looking ahead, the UFC 336 card is taking shape. The promotion announced a championship doubleheader as its co-main event for the Jan. 30 event in Toronto, which will be the first numbered event of 2027. Notably absent from the interim welterweight title fight is Islam Makhachev , and Dana White explained why he picked Carlos Prates and Michael Morales over him.
The NBA season is not even a week old, yet injuries have already begun to impact the championship hunt. Multiple big-name players came out of the weekend with health concerns. None are more devastating than the gruesome leg injury Jalen Williams sustained Sunday night . The Thunder star appears destined to miss the remainder of the season after he was taken off the court on a stretcher.
Our Jack Maloney explained how significant this could be to Oklahoma City as it aims to lift a trophy at season's end.
The Magic are also the victims of brutal injury luck. Just minutes after Williams' awful leg issue occurred, Jalen Suggs went down with a scary-looking injury of his own as his knee buckled from underneath him on a layup. That followed Paolo Banchero 's high-ankle sprain, which made us wonder whether Orlando is cursed .
And on Friday, reigning NBA Rookie of the Year Cooper Flagg sprained his shoulder when he found himself on the receiving end of a flagrant foul. He will be reevaluated in the coming days.
The last time there were only three undefeated teams remaining in college football through Oct. 24 was in 1977. Congratulations are in order for Miami , Utah and UCLA as the only three teams to survive the chaos of this historically unpredictable season. The Hurricanes are off to the best start of that trio as the clear-cut No. 1 team in the country and week after week prove that "The U" is very much back .
One storied program that cannot seem to revive its glory days, though, is USC . The Trojans (and more specifically, Lincoln Riley ) are among the biggest losers of Week 8 . 17 was the not-so-magic number for the Trojans, who lost by 17 points to Wisconsin and posted -17 rushing yards in an embarrassing defeat. It was the largest loss of Riley's career and one that amplifies the questions about his long-term future in Los Angeles. Our Brad Crawford says it's time for USC to scrap together a cool $70 million and pay Riley's buyout.
Saturday delivered the full Texas experience. The Longhorns looked like championship contenders when they built a 24-3 lead over Ole Miss , then they showed their flaws when Arch Manning and the offense turned the ball over three times and let the Rebels back into the game . They held on for a seven-point win, but we were left less than enthusiastic by their performance and gave them a "B" on our report card . Losing star left tackle Trevor Goosby for the season with a knee injury does not inspire confidence in them, either.

title: Peyton Manning for Colts GM after Chris Ballard's firing? Why timing isn't right for Hall of Fame QB
summary: The franchise legend spent 14 seasons in Indianapolis, winning Super Bowl XLI with the Colts
full_text:
Following the Indianapolis Colts' firing of general manager Chris Ballard this month, one name that immediately surfaced as a potential call was former quarterback Peyton Manning, who spent 14 seasons with the franchise and won a championship as a four-time MVP.
However, ESPN's Adam Schefter reports that Manning is not interested in a front office role at the NFL level at the moment, nor is Indianapolis expected to kick the tires on someone synonymous with Colts greatness and beloved by the organization
"The Colts have not approached Manning about their vacant GM job nor would the Hall of Fame quarterback be expected to be interested in the position, sources said," Schefter reported Sunday prior to the team's loss to Minnesota. "Manning has not trained or aspired to become an NFL general manager, not with all that he has going on in his life. The timing to become an NFL general manager, which requires day-to-day attention, would not be right, according to sources."
In disarray at 2-5 overall this season with three straight losses, Indianapolis moved on from Ballard last week after modest on-field results during his decade-long tenure as GM. Colts owner and CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon said a change was a "deliberate" decision given the team's struggles.
"Waiting would only delay the important work that needs to begin now," Irsay-Gordon wrote in a statement. "We will conduct a thorough search for our next general manager and take the time necessary to identify the right leader for the future of this organization.
"I also want to be clear: this decision does not change our goals for the season. We have a lot of football in front of us, and I expect us to compete, improve, and win football games."
Since 2021, Manning and his brother, Eli, have hosted Manningcast, an alternative broadcast of "Monday Night Football." Manning, that same year, expressed interest in an ownership role with the Denver Broncos — his other former team —but nothing materialized.
"I actually like what I'm doing now. I get to stay close to the game," Manning said about his broadcasting job at the time.
With the Colts, Manning took Indianapolis to the playoffs 11 times, winning a championship in 2006. He is the franchise's all-time leader in passing yards, passing touchdowns, completions and passing attempts.
For now, Indianapolis has been transparent with other teams on the trade market that the franchise is interested in shopping talent ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline , including star running back Jonathan Taylor.
New personnel director Ed Dodds is reportedly working closely with Irsay-Gordon and other decision-makers to determine trades and what moves would best benefit the franchise moving forward.
Edge rusher DeForest Buckner, defensive tackle Grover Stewart and offensive guard Quenton Nelson are considered the Colts' most attractive pieces in the market beyond Taylor. All three are on expiring contracts with the Colts, along with wideout Keenan Allen, who has 29 receptions for 258 yards and a score this season.
According to NFL insider Tom Pelissero , no player is expected to be off-limits if Irsay-Gordon decides the Colts are "sellers" at the deadline. It is believed to depend on how Indianapolis fares in its next two games against Jacksonville and Dallas.
Irsay-Gordon's strongly worded statement following Ballard's firing suggests she believes all goals are still out in front of this team this fall, but Sunday's loss to the Vikings may have altered that confidence a bit.
author: Brad Crawford

title: Cover 32: There is a very clear Jonathan Taylor trade destination, plus game balls, biggest gaffes from Week 7
summary: Why Cincinnati should make a blockbuster offer for Jonathan Taylor, plus Week 7 game balls for Joe Burrow and Malik Willis
full_text:
Like an object in your rearview mirror, the NFL trade deadline is closer than it appears. Tuesday will mark two weeks before the Nov. 10 deadline, and there will be a tsunami of rumors and reports about the comings and goings of players between now and then. Key among them will be All-Pro running back Jonathan Taylor , arguably the biggest prize of this cycle.
The Indianapolis Colts are a clear seller as the deadline approaches. Before Week 7, the club fired general manager Chris Ballard. Then, a loss to the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday has since dropped the franchise to 2-5 on the year and has them on a three-game losing skid. They have two more games before the deadline, traveling to Jacksonville next week to face the Jaguars , who are 4-2 and will be coming off their bye week. In Week 9, they'll host the Dallas Cowboys .
On the lookahead lines, Indy is a 7.5-point underdog to Jacksonville and a 1.5-point underdog at home to Dallas, so the oddsmakers have them favored to go 0-2 over that stretch. That'd bring them to 2-7 on the season as they reach the deadline, which would only further embolden them to sell off major pieces as they look to refill the cupboard to better jumpstart their rebuild.
So, who should target Taylor and pull the trigger on a blockbuster to bring him to town? Isn't it obvious?
The Cincinnati Bengals should be pushing their chips into the middle of the table to try and land Taylor. The back is the missing piece that could help take Joe Burrow back to the Super Bowl and, this time, win it.
On Sunday, Cincinnati pulled off a comeback victory over the Baltimore Ravens thanks to a second-half explosion from the offense. Burrow threw for four touchdowns over the final two quarters as part of a 35-0 run to move them to 4-2 on the season and put them firmly in the mix in the AFC North race.
Burrow's touchdown barrage and 249 passing yards in the second half were awe-inspiring. It's also unsustainable.
What was missing from Cincinnati's victory was a running game, and that's been a common theme for the team throughout the first half of the regular season. As a team, the Bengals are averaging 82.9 rushing yards per game, which ranks in the bottom third in the NFL. Their 3.6 yards per carry average is also lackluster. Moreover, Cincinnati has just 44 rushes that have gone for five-plus yards and a league-low five explosive rushes (12-plus yards).
The combination of Chase Brown and Samaje Perine isn't giving the Bengals a rushing attack that opposing defenses need to worry about. Brown is averaging a career-low 3.5 yards per carry, while Perine's 4.1 yards per carry is his lowest since 2022.
For a team in a Super Bowl-or-bust window, this is a clear area of need, and there is a clear answer currently on the trade market in Taylor. So far, Taylor has 11 explosive rushes, and his 2.89 yards per carry after contact is better than the 2.46 yards per carry after contact the Bengals are averaging.
Taylor could be Cincinnati's version of the trade the San Francisco 49ers made leading up to the 2022 deadline when they landed star running back Christian McCaffrey . He proved to be the central engine of the Niners' second half as they reached the NFC Championship, and that has remained the case over the last handful of years, including a Super Bowl LVIII appearance.  Taylor is every bit as capable of making that type of impact on the Bengals, and Cincinnati is at the precise moment in the franchise's history to go all-in and outbid the rest of the league for the star back.
How Game Balls work: Six are awarded to standout players from the slate of teams that won their contests, and only one player on a team can get a game ball.
After not registering a single touch last week, Skattebo emerged from John Harbaugh's doghouse and redeemed himself in Week 7 as the Giants took down the Texans in overtime. The second-year back was at the center of the winning effort, including a 42-yard rush in overtime that helped springboard New York. His 124 rushing yards are a career high.
The longest run of Cam Skattebo's career puts the @Giants in striking distance in OT... NYGvsHOU on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/VslWlQGb0V
The Miami Dolphins are finally in the win column. The Dolphins enjoyed their first win of the Jeff Hafley era, going into MetLife Stadium and taking down the Jets , 28-25. Willis did damage with both his arm and his legs in the winning effort and is the second quarterback in franchise history with a passing touchdown and a rushing touchdown in consecutive games.
Malik Willis lowers his shoulder for the touchdown MIAvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/TVRwL1sULm
The Vikings linebacker was all over the place in Sunday's 16-10 win over the Colts to keep Minnesota undefeated on the year at 6-0. Cashman's 4.5 sacks on the season are already tied for his career high, while the Vikings defense is allowing just 12.3 points per game so far this season (fewest in the NFL).
"This is a group that honestly no matter how well we've played this season, we aren't satisfied." @EvanWashburn catches up with Blake Cashman after the Vikings defense seals the game to improve to 6-0 pic.twitter.com/BpeQIPTZNc
The Browns ' first-round rookie had his coming-out party in Week 7, tallying career highs across the board. In the 27-34 win over Tennessee to move Cleveland to 5-2 on the season, Concepcion was a central figure in the offense. His 10 targets were a season-high, as were his 129 receiving yards. Todd Monken even got him going in the ground game as he carried the ball three times for 23 yards, another season high.
KC Concepcion showing off his speed 🏃 CLEvsTEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/qZVlUdpPyU
Burrow was perfect in the second half of Cincinnati's win over the Ravens on Sunday. He orchestrated a 35-0 run over the final two quarters to erase a 13-0 halftime deficit. In the second half, Burrow completed 16 of 18 throws for 249 yards and four touchdowns, giving him a perfect 158.3 passer rating over that stretch.
Burrow dropped that one right in the bucket for Tee CINvsBAL on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/0cTT0jvKqS
Bates was one of the main faces of a strong defensive effort by the Falcons as they handed the 49ers its first loss of the season. Both of his turnovers came in the second half, with the interception preventing a scoring opportunity as he approached the Atlanta 10-yard line. Then, his forced fumble on George Kittle effectively ended the game. This was Bates' sixth career game with an interception and a forced fumble, tied for the second-most in the NFL over the past 40 seasons and trailing only Rod Woodson (7).
This interception by Jessie Bates III is UNREAL. SFvsATL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/R4UDkkfGcb
One of the big momentum shifts, as the Ravens allowed 35 unanswered second-half points to the Bengals, came in the opening seconds of the fourth quarter. At the time, Baltimore was trailing Cincinnati 14-13, but had the ball on the Bengals 12-yard line. That led to a decision for coach Jesse Minter, facing a fourth-and-2. He could either opt to keep the offense on the field in hopes of moving the sticks and eventually finding the end zone. Either that, or he could kick it to retake the lead and make it a 16-14 game.
While keeping the offense on the field (which is what he ended up doing) can be argued, the play call was ... puzzling. The Ravens called a passing play on the fourth-down attempt, and Tyler Huntley , who was filling in for the injured Lamar Jackson , failed to connect with rookie tight end Josh Cuevas and turned the ball over on downs. Cincinnati took possession and scored six plays later to extend its lead.
Ravens decide to go for it on 4th & 2 and can't convert. pic.twitter.com/OAARWnsV2d
This is a scenario where the obvious answer is the right one—just give the ball to Derrick Henry . That is why you have a back of his caliber,…
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: NFL Week 8 early odds: Undefeated Vikings gain respect, Chiefs-Broncos line flips
summary: Minnesota is gaining ground ahead of its NFC North showdown with Detroit, while the Chiefs-Broncos and Eagles-Commanders lines have flipped
full_text:
It took seven weeks for a lone undefeated team to emerge in the NFL . The Vikings are the last unbeaten standing after taking down the Colts to move to 6-0, while both Kansas City and San Francisco fell on Sunday.
Minnesota's strong start to the year is now being reflected in the betting odds, as they are getting respect as a true NFC contender. For instance, the Lions opened as a 4.5-point favorite at home against the Vikings for Week 8, but that has started to move towards Kevin O'Connell's club. Now, Detroit is a 3-point favorite.
That is just one of the many swings that we're seeing in the Week 8 odds now that the final chapters are being written in Week 7. As we gear up for a new week in the NFL, let's take a look at the early odds for the slate and see who the oddsmakers have coming out on top.
Note : New Orleans, New York ( Giants ), San Francisco, and Houston are on the bye in Week 8.
All lines via DraftKings ; all games on Sunday unless noted
Panthers at Packers (Thursday)
Panthers +170, Packers -205
Cardinals +240, Cowboys -298
Falcons +105, Buccaneers -125
Browns +160, Steelers -192
Patriots -380, Dolphins +300
Eagles +154, Commanders -185
Bears at Seahawks (Monday)
Green Bay is a 4.5-point favorite at home and looking to improve its 2-1 ATS record at Lambeau Field. Carolina is coming off a demoralizing loss to the Buccaneers on Sunday, where they surrendered 43 points. The Panthers are 2-1 ATS on the road this season, but that loss has shaken the confidence of bettors. The line opened at Packers -3, but it has since jumped up a point and a half. The total has also held at 47.5. In Packers games this season, the Under is 5-2, which includes a 2-1 record at home. The Under is 3-0 in Panthers road games.
Dallas initially opened as a 10.5-point home favorite, but that line has dipped below the touchdown threshold to -6.5. That could be due to questions about the Cowboys' defense and Arizona's ability to sneak through the back door. Dallas will also be playing on a short week after facing the Eagles on Monday night in Philly. The Cowboys are 1-1 ATS at home this season, while the Cardinals is 3-1 ATS on the road. The total for this game jumped up to 51.5 after opening at 49.5. Between these two clubs, the Over is 8-5.
Buffalo is coming off its bye, so it'll have a rest advantage over Baltimore. However, the Ravens are slated to get Lamar Jackson back in the fold after missing the previous three games. That's likely why this line is at -3.5 in favor of the Bills. Josh Allen's team is 4-2 ATS this season, which includes a 2-1 ATS record at home. Baltimore is 2-1 ATS on the road. Given Jackson's return, the Over will likely be a popular play, even at 52.5. This season, the Over is 5-1 in Bills games.

title: Can the Vikings actually win the Super Bowl with this offense? You're telling me there's a chance
summary: Minnesota has one of the NFL's worst offenses and a defense playing at a historically dominant level -- the 2015 Broncos provide a blueprint, but there are reasons to be skeptical
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings are 6-0, which is remarkable for one very obvious reason: their offense, by any objective measure, is anemic. They've scored all of 10 touchdowns this season. Their kicker, Will Reichard , has 63 points. Everybody else on the roster? Sixty-two.
Sunday against the Colts offered more of the same. Kyler Murray threw for 150 yards, the offense scored a lone touchdown, and Minnesota won anyway, 16-10. Indianapolis quarterback Daniel Jones managed 108 passing yards, threw an interception and was sacked four times. The Vikings have now won 11 straight games dating to last season, despite scoring just 21 touchdowns during that stretch, the fewest in an 11-game winning streak in NFL history.
At this point, there's no debating whether Brian Flores is an elite defensive coordinator. But here's a question worth considering: Is he so good that his defense can drag this offense all the way to a Super Bowl ? I know, this sounds ridiculous – even for the terminally online, where hyperbole, hype and mock outrage are the fuel that keeps the internet running.
But this is not that. Just ask the 2015 Denver Broncos .
Eleven years ago, Denver started 6-0 with a 39-year-old Peyton Manning who looked nothing like the quarterback who'd won five MVP awards. His arm strength had diminished, injuries had taken their toll, and a makeshift offensive line wasn't helping. Manning threw nine touchdowns and 17 interceptions in 10 games before a foot injury opened the door for Brock Osweiler .
Denver's defense, led by Von Miller , DeMarcus Ware and a loaded secondary, made up for the offense's shortcomings. The Broncos finished 25th in offensive EPA per play but beat the Steelers , Patriots and Panthers on their way to winning Super Bowl 50.
But here's the fine print: Minnesota's offense ranks 31st in EPA per play, and its minus-0.148 mark is considerably worse than Denver's minus-0.063 in 2015. The Vikings aren't just struggling offensively. They're playing at a historically bad level.
Still, the Broncos established that winning a championship without consistently good quarterback play isn't impossible. And Minnesota's defense is performing at a level worthy of the comparison.
Since 2011, only two defenses have completed a season with better EPA/play than Minnesota's current plus-0.195: the 2019 Patriots and 2020 Rams . That's 480 completed team-seasons, and the Vikings' six-game performance? It would rank No. 3. Overall.
Historically dominant defenses, 2011–2026
Flores has taken an already aggressive approach to another level. Minnesota blitzes on 71.8% of dropbacks, nearly 28 percentage points more frequently than the next-closest team this season. Its 47.1% pressure rate ranks among the NFL's best, and opponents are averaging just 12.3 points per game.
Against the Colts, Flores blitzed on 85.2% of dropbacks, the highest single-game rate since 2013. Indianapolis managed 48 yards in the second half.
And the Vikings don't need to blitz to dominate. They lead the NFL in defensive EPA per play when rushing four or fewer defenders. But there's a difference between making life miserable for opposing quarterbacks and being asked to singlehandedly win games every week. That's effectively what Minnesota's defense has done through six games.
The 2026 Vikings rank 31st in offensive EPA/play, 29th in passing yards per game and 31st in touchdown rate per drive. And that minus-0.148 EPA/play? It would rank 22nd-worst among those same 480 team seasons going back to 2011.
And this isn't just a Kyler Murray problem. The 2025 Vikings finished at minus-0.111 EPA/play, and the offense has become even less efficient in 2026. Murray didn't inherit the Kirk Cousins offenses that ranked fifth and sixth in EPA/play in 2019 and 2020. He inherited a mess. And so far, it's somehow worse.
The run game has been respectable, ranking 12th in yards per game. The passing game? Not so much. Murray is averaging just 162.3 passing yards per game, and Minnesota scores touchdowns on only 13.8% of its possessions, 31st in the NFL.
So how long can a defense keep winning games when its offense contributes so little? Three teams from the last decade faced similar challenges, and their seasons ended in three very different ways.
How far can an elite defense carry a bad offense?
The 2019 Steelers are the cautionary tale. Ben Roethlisberger suffered a season-ending elbow injury in Week 2, leaving Pittsburgh with Mason Rudolph and undrafted rookie Duck Hodges (!) at quarterback. Injuries elsewhere on offense compounded the problems. The Steelers' defense, featuring TJ Watt and Minkah Fitzpatrick , kept them competitive, but Pittsburgh finished 8-8 and missed the playoffs. Their offense ranked 31st in EPA per play, the same as Minnesota's this season. I know we now joke about Mike Tomlin never having a losing season, but I was serious when I said he should've won Coach of the Year after willing this team to eight wins.
The 2023 Browns provide a more encouraging comparison. Cleveland lost Nick Chubb , Deshaun Watson and key offensive linemen to injuries, eventually cycling through five starting quarterbacks. Joe Flacco provided an unlikely off-the-couch, late-season spark, while Jim Schwartz's defense helped the Browns finish 11-6. Cleveland's minus-0.145 offensive EPA/play is the closest historical comparison to Minnesota's, and its defense was lights out. But the Browns' wild ride didn't last long once they reached the postseason; the Texans beat them 45-14 in the wild-card round.
Three teams. Three outcomes. And proof that even an elite defense can't guarantee much if the offense consistently struggles.
There's another reason not to dismiss the Vikings' Super Bowl chances: They're already 6-0.
Of the 14 teams that opened a season with six consecutive wins going back to 2013, all 14 reached the playoffs. Seven made the Super Bowl, though only the 2015 Broncos won it all.
Not surprisingly, Minnesota has outperformed expectations, but not by a wildly outrageous margin, at least according to something called Pythagorean expected wins. The formula uses points scored and allowed to estimate how many games a team should have won . Based on their 125 points scored and 74 allowed, the Vikings have an expected 4.7 wins, compared with their actual 6-0 record. That's a better mark than the 2015 Broncos, who also started 6-0 but had just 4.1 expected wins through six games. And, as we've established, Denver went on to win the whole thing.
How far did these 6-0 teams go?
At 6-0, the Vikings have already given themselves plenty of breathing room. Even a 5-6 finish would leave them at 11-6, and there's little reason to believe the wheels are about to fall off Flores' defense.
But getting to the playoffs and winning three or four games against the NFC's best teams are two different conversations. And that brings us back to the original question: Forget about making the playoffs – that feels almost inevitable at this point. Let's get nuts: Can these Vikings actually win the Super Bowl?
The Broncos proved it's possible. The Steelers and Browns showed how quickly things can go sideways. Minnesota's defense is playing well enough to make a championship run – no doubt about it – but its offense is asking even more of Flores than Denver asked of its defense a decade ago.
The good news for Minnesota? At 6-0, there's time to figure it out. And with Flores making life miserable for opposing quarterbacks, O'Connell and Murray don't need to turn this into a top-five offense. They just need to make it replacement-level.
Because right now, the Vikings look like a Super Bowl contender on one side of the ball and a team headed for a top-five draft pick on the other. Something's got to give.

title: Cardinals receiver out for the season
summary: It always happens. You have an abundance of one thing, list one or two on Facebook Marketplace, make some new money, and then all of sudden something breaks, you are robbed and three others are stolen, and you drop the last one and break it. Yeah. The life of being involved with the Arizona Cardinals. […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - OCTOBER 25: Jalen Brooks #86 of the Arizona Cardinals drives with the football after a reception against Kris Abrams-Draine #31 of the Denver Broncos during the fourth quarter of the game at State Farm Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images It always happens. You have an abundance of one thing, list one or two on Facebook Marketplace, make some new money, and then all of sudden something breaks, you are robbed and three others are stolen, and you drop the last one and break it. Yeah. The life of being involved with the Arizona Cardinals. After trading away WR Marv Harrison in a crowded receiver room, word now comes that WR Jalen Brooks had surgery to repair an injured wrist. RELATED: BEAKS & GEEKS WEEK 7 Brooks posted on his Instagram: “Have to get an emergency surgery on my wrist. I don’t need any phone calls. Just Prayer. I’ll be done for the season. God is in control of my next steps. Much love.” Wide receiver Jalen Brooks posts on Instagram that he is done for the season. A massive blow to the #AZCardinals wide receiver room and for Brooks who finally earned playing time. pic.twitter.com/2hFLJlVxiq — Zach Gershman (@ZachAZCards) October 26, 2026 Against the Denver Broncos, with 2:09 remaining in the game, Brooks caught a short pass and rumbled for 35 yards to Denver’s one-yard line. As he was being tackled, he extended the ball in an attempt to break the plane for a touchdown. He was hit and stopped just short at the Broncos’ 1-yard line. After the game, he was visibly uncomfortable in the locker room. Brooks sprained or fractured his wrist. It must have been a severe injury because he had surgery on Monday. Brooks, age 26, was the darling of this year’s preseason, and one of the reasons viewed by the Cardinals coaching staff as a reason they could move on from Harrison, who didn’t seem to fit this new offense. Along with WR Kendrick Bourne, Brooks was expected to garner more of the workload. This season, Brooks played in all seven games with zero starts. He had 17 targets with five receptions for 81 yards, an average of 16.2 yards per catch, 26 YAC, converted three first downs, and had 1 drop. But his targets increased once Harrison left. Receiver Simi Fehoko, who has mostly gotten snaps on special teams, will now fill Brooks’ role on the offense. The other receivers on the roster are rookie Reggie Virgil and kick returner Devin Duvernay. Listed on the practice squad are Harrison Wallace and Shedrick Jackson.

title: NFC South Week 7 Review: Upsets close the gap in the division
summary: The Buccaneers took down the Panthers, while the Falcons held off the 49ers, turning the tide in this division race. The Saints went marching into France and marched out with a loss. Here’s the Week 7 NFC South Review. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (2-5) Week 7 Result: Buccaneers 43 – Panthers 13Week 8 Opponent:  Atlanta Falcons […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NC - OCTOBER 25: Tampa Bay Buccaneers Bucky Irving (7) begins the celebration after scoring a touchdown during an NFL football game between the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the Carolina Panthers on October 25, 2026 at Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte, N.C. (Photo by John Byrum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Buccaneers took down the Panthers, while the Falcons held off the 49ers, turning the tide in this division race. The Saints went marching into France and marched out with a loss. Here’s the Week 7 NFC South Review. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (2-5) Week 7 Result: Buccaneers 43 – Panthers 13 Week 8 Opponent: Atlanta Falcons The Buccaneers steamrolled the Panthers and spooked Dave Canales so badly that the head coach could barely process what happened. Baker Mayfield was back, but the Buccaneers didn’t really need him; their defense and run game stole the show. Tampa Bay ran for 258 yards and three rushing touchdowns, while the defense forced four turnovers and added a touchdown of their own. It was an impressive win against the division leaders, and the Buccaneers will face another division rival as they prepare to host the Falcons. Buccaneers pouring it ON vs. the Panthers (via @NFL ) pic.twitter.com/Il95ilGs3Q — Sports Illustrated (@SInow) October 25, 2026 Carolina Panthers (3-3) Week 7 Result: Panthers 13 – Buccaneers 43 Week 8 Opponent: Green Bay Packers The Panthers gave up 33 points in the first half and never recovered. Bryce Young turned in his worst performance of the year; the quarterback had two interceptions and a fumble returned for a touchdown. The Panthers defense was no better. The Buccaneers ran wild, allowing them to protect Mayfield in his return and dominate the time of possession. If all that wasn’t bad enough, the offense also lost OT Taylor Moton for the year to a fractured fibula. This loss felt like a punch to the gut, and Carolina has to rebound quickly on Thursday against the Packers. New Orleans Saints (2-5) Week 7 Result: Saints 10 – Steelers 16 Week 8 Opponent: Bye Week The French expedition proved fruitless as Kellen Moore’s team keeps disappointing. The Saints defense finally showed up, but their offense disappeared. Tyler Shough threw a costly interception in the 3rd quarter that swung momentum back to the Steelers , but it’s fair to say Shough didn’t get much during the game. He led the team in rushing yards with seven, as the Saints running backs combined for 14 carries and 11 yards. This season has gone off the rails, and Moore could be coaching for his job if things continue. The bye week has arrived just in time because this team needs a hard reset. title: Falcons – 49ers recap: Victory, sweet and pure
summary: It was going to take a stellar effort to beat the San Francisco 49ers. They were undefeated and had shrugged off challenges and injuries all season long, with Kyle Shanahan’s offense humming and Raheem Morris’s defense rolling. After back-to-back weeks where penalties, poor special teams, and simple execution errors doomed the Falcons, it was hard […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 25: Head coach Kevin Stefanski of the Atlanta Falcons reacts after an interception against the San Francisco 49ers during the third quarter at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images It was going to take a stellar effort to beat the San Francisco 49ers. They were undefeated and had shrugged off challenges and injuries all season long, with Kyle Shanahan’s offense humming and Raheem Morris’s defense rolling. After back-to-back weeks where penalties, poor special teams, and simple execution errors doomed the Falcons, it was hard to do more than hope against hope that they had that kind of effort in them. They did, though. The Falcons were in a hole early—they went down 14-3 at one point—but this team climbed out of it with aplomb, outscoring San Francisco 26-6 the rest of the way. The passing game was terrific, with Michael Penix Jr. slinging it well and throwing three touchdowns, and the ground game was solid enough to get the job done. Special teams finally lumbered to life, with Nick Folk missing an extra point but nailing multiple field goals, and the offense getting a major assist from two nice returns from Zachariah Branch and Khalil Herbert. More than anything else, the defense was spectacular , rallying after their early struggles to force four turnovers, limit the 49ers to just six points after halftime, and close the game out late. It was a whole team effort that delivered a badly needed win, and suddenly these Falcons are very much in the NFC South race again. We shouldn’t overlook just how spectacular this effort was. I wrote last week that the Falcons were dimming our hopes and playing deeply frustrating football, and those kinds of skids are not always easy to climb out of. In this game, the 49ers sold out to stop the Falcons from running the ball and largely bottled up Bijan Robinson, while the Falcons had a couple of tough misses from Penix and unbelievable drops by Jahan Dotson and Drake London. Those errors, paired with the missed Folk extra point, felt like plays that would surely haunt Atlanta, yet the Falcons proved to be ready and willing to ghostbust their recent past. The fact that Shanahan and Morris have been doing stellar work with this team and pressed all the right buttons early meant the Falcons would have to be sharp and adjust on the fly, and they did just that. That required stellar days from coaches and players alike. We’ve now seen this team do truly impressive work in three games, passable work en route to losses in two games, and poor work in two more. That’s not enough to build a case for this team to be good, bad, or indifferent, really, and evaluating this team’s trajectory on a weekly basis has been a fool’s errand thus far. What matters to me is that this game was the best evidence yet that there’s something more here than mediocrity to work with, and evidence of the uneven but critical progress I wanted in 2026 . We’re likely in for more ups and downs, but if the Falcons can start to truly find their footing and string together these kinds of efforts, there may just be something here. I would like that very much. If nothing else, that was a great way to spend a Sunday afternoon. Let’s dive in to the full recap. The Good Zachariah Branch badly wanted a big play after his rough two-fumble performance last week, and the electric rookie got it. On his first kickoff return of the game, he got a lane with some nice blocking and flew downfield, picking up 61 yards and setting up the Falcons with excellent field position. He was once again only a small factor on offense, but that was great to see after the Bears game. Michael Penix Jr. missed a couple of throws along the way, but I was struck by how comfortable he looked in this game. Pressure—which came less frequently, thank you offensive line—didn’t seem to rattle him as much as in weeks past, and he made multiple great throws on the move in this game. Unlike last week, where Penix fumbled twice and threw multiple turnover-worthy balls that luckily did not turn into interceptions, he was also quite careful with the ball and threw plenty of shorter passes. The result was a fairly pedestrian stat line—25/34 for 213 yards—but also critically three very well-thrown touchdowns and zero turnovers. He’s now thrown three touchdowns in back-to-back games, becoming just one of nine Falcons quarterbacks to do so. Bijan Robinson had one productive run called back, but this was a real grind-it-out game for a player who came into this one as the obvious focal point for the 49ers defense. It’s a credit to Bijan that he turned a rough matchup against a team that knew where he was on every single play into a strong day, with just 3.1 yards per carry on the ground (and 63 yards on 20 carries) but another 59 yards on five catches. He remains the most dangerous player the Falcons bring to bear, and occupies attention that creates opportunities for others even on a “quiet” sort of day. Khalil Herbert has long been a player I liked more than the NFL did, given his limited opportunities past his early years in Chicago. I think he showed why I like him on Sunday, when he nearly dropped a kickoff but still returned it for close to 40 yards, and on a great catch and run early in the game where he nearly scored a touchdown. If the Falcons have to lean on him for a couple of weeks, I think he’s very much up to the task. The inability to turn Kyle Pitts, who has sticky hands, excellent speed, and difficult-to-defend size, into a real red zone threat in years prior was one of the most baffling subplots in a sea of such subplots for the Falcons from 2021-2025. It appears Tommy Rees and Michael Penix Jr. are on their way to solving that particular conundrum, as Pitts has now caught four touchdowns in the past three games and is just one score away from matching his career high for a single season. While Pitts had a relatively quiet day, he had a few important short grabs, none more than the touchdown. Drake London spent Sunday battling, too, including a brief exit to be checked for a concussion after a helmet-to-helmet hit. He finished with seven catches for 66 yards—both marks led the team, of course—and his first touchdown grab of 2026. He’s on track to break his single season receiving yardage mark this year, and that connection with Penix is the stuff of legends. The line wasn’t perfect, especially against the run, but the Falcons got much better pass protection out of this group today from top to bottom and supplemented it with a healthy dose of tight ends staying in to block, resulting in Penix taking zero hits on the day. This team needed to find an answer for pressure given how shaky Penix has been when he’s on his back foot, and to the line’s credit and Tommy Rees’ credit, they found one. Maason Smith chained together a couple of great plays in the first quarter. After the 49ers picked up a dispiriting first down on a pass to George Kittle, Smith shed his blocker and took a chip from Kaleon Black and still got to Brock Purdy quickly for a sack. On the very next play, he got his hand up and deflected Purdy’s pass, which fell harmlessly for an incompletion. The less heralded member of Atlanta’s formidable defensive front, Smith has been effective much of the year but didn’t have the big plays. That worked, and he followed it up by helping to force a Kaleon Black fumble in the second quarter. Za’Darius Smith is just a fun player. He’s had a couple of costly penalties in recent weeks, which I do find frustrating given his limited snaps, but Smith also is just a very effective pass rusher. After putting up just 1.5 sacks a year ago, he’s at 4.5 sacks already in 2026 following a Purdy takedown. Kendal Daniels is a player I have a lot of belief in, but I wasn’t expecting greatness coming into this one given that he was carted off the field just a week ago. Yet greatness is what we got, as…

Head coach Jesse Minter was noncommittal about Jackson’s status during his Monday presser, effectively indicating that the […]
full_text: Sep 7, 2025; Orchard Park, New York, USA; Buffalo Bills running back Ty Johnson (26) is pushed out of bounds by Baltimore Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton (14) in the first quarter at Highmark Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark Konezny-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect *sigh* Another week of Lamar Jackson Ankle Watch in Baltimore. The Ravens badly need their star quarterback back on the field for their upcoming visit to Buffalo, but his high ankle sprain could sideline him for another week. Head coach Jesse Minter was noncommittal about Jackson’s status during his Monday presser, effectively indicating that the ninth-year passer remains day-to-day. His return to practice last Wednesday was an encouraging sign, but he will likely need to be upgrade to full participation for at least one day this week. Unfortunately, there is reason to believe that Jackson will miss another week. He revealed last week that he was dealing with a high ankle sprain, an injury that typically takes at least four weeks to heal. The two-time MVP indicated that he can play at less than 100%, but he still has yet to reach his minimum standard to take the field. Jackson also said that his attempts to play through injuries last year were “dumb, a little bit,” indicating he could take a cautious approach to his return. There are some similarities between his current injury situation and last year’s. Jackson missed three weeks with a hamstring injury, returned to practice in a limited capacity, and did not start the next game, due in part to a short turnaround before a Thursday night matchup the following week. This year, the Ravens are hosting the Jaguars just four days after their trip to Buffalo, which could give the team another reason to rule Jackson out for one more game in the hopes of a strong return in Week 9. Betting markets, however, have a sunnier outlook of Jackson’s availability in Week 8. The Ravens opened as 3.5-point underdogs against the Bills ( via FanDuel Sportsbook ), but another Tyler Huntley start would be much more of an uphill battle. title: Ravens sign former Browns, Steelers safety Rayshawn Jenkins
summary: The Baltimore Ravens signed veteran safety Rayshawn Jenkins to their practice squad on Monday, per the NFL’s daily personnel notice. Jenkins, 32, is a 10-year veteran who appeared in the Steelers’ first six games this season. He served as the No. 3 safety in his first two games, started in Week 3, and saw his […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - NOVEMBER 23: Rayshawn Jenkins #5 of the Cleveland Browns looks on before a game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium on November 23, 2025 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens signed veteran safety Rayshawn Jenkins to their practice squad on Monday, per the NFL’s daily personnel notice. Jenkins, 32, is a 10-year veteran who appeared in the Steelers’ first six games this season. He served as the No. 3 safety in his first two games, started in Week 3, and saw his snap count collapse in the following contest. Jenkins was relegated to special teams duties in Weeks 5 and 6 before his release last week, which corresponded with former Raven DeShon Elliot’s return from injured reserve. Baltimore needed some safety depth with Jaylinn Hawkins dealing with a knee injury. He did not practice last week and missed Sunday’s game against the Bengals, elevating K’Von Wallace and Keondre Jackson into their first significant defensive snaps of the season. Wallace delivered some mighty hits, but both were exposed in coverage during Cincinnati’s second-half onslaught. Jenkins adds some experienced depth to the safety room as well as Anthony Levine’s special teams units. He has spent time with a variety of defensive coordinators during his decade in the NFL, including 13 appearances (nine starts) on Mike Macdonald’s Seahawks in 2024. That should help him quickly learn Jesse Minter’s defense. The Ravens will likely roll with Wallace and Jackson as their rotational safeties on game day for another week, but if the secondary’s struggles continue, Jenkins could get an opportunity. He has primarily lined up as a free safety and in the box in his career with a decent track record as a blitzer. If Minter wants to deply Hamilton at free safety more often, Jenkins could take on some of his box snaps and pass-rushing duties, though he certainly cannot fill Hamilton’s diverse, one-of-one role. Originally a Chargers fourth-round pick in 2017, Jenkins earned a starting job in his third season. He led the defense with five interceptions over the next two years and ranked second with 84 tackles in 2020. His performance earned him a four-year, $35 million deal from the Jaguars in free agency in 2021. Jenkins started for three years in Jacksonville before moving to Seattle. Last year, he appeared in every game for the Browns with three starts and played 26% of the their defensive snaps and 51% of their special teams snaps.

title: Ravens Snap Count Analysis, Week 7: Collapse on both sides of the ball in second half
summary: Offense The Ravens played 67 offensive snaps and again did not receive a full showing from their starting offensive line because of injuries. Vega Ioane was replaced by Emery Jones Jr. after he suffered a knee injury and did not return to the game. Jones played the final 51 snaps at right guard next to […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - OCTOBER 25: Nate Wiggins #2 of the Baltimore Ravens breaks up a pass intended for Ja'marr Chase #1 of the Cincinnati Bengals during the third quarter at M&T Bank Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Todd Olszewski/Getty Images) | Getty Images Offense QB: Tyler Huntley 67 RB: Derrick Henry 34, Justice Hill 31, Rasheen Ali 4 WR: Zay Flowers 57, Rashod Bateman 49, Ja’Kobi Lane 46, Devontez Walker 20, LaJohntay Wester 1 TE: Mark Andrews 38, Matthew Hibner 26, Josh Cuevas 15, Nick Vannett 14 OL: Ronnie Stanley 67, John Simpson 67, Cam Jurgens 67, Vega Ioane 16, Emery Jones Jr. 51 The Ravens played 67 offensive snaps and again did not receive a full showing from their starting offensive line because of injuries. Vega Ioane was replaced by Emery Jones Jr. after he suffered a knee injury and did not return to the game. Jones played the final 51 snaps at right guard next to Cam Jurgens, who started at center for the first time since being traded to the Ravens. Jurgens played the entire game. In the backfield, it was a near-evens split between Derrick Henry and Justice Hill. Unfortunately, the Ravens were ineffective running the ball again. Henry averaged less than 3.0 yards per carry on 17 attempts and with the team trailing big late in the game, Rasheen Ali played four snaps and had four carries. Matthew Hibner returned from injury at tight end and reassumed his No. 2 role in the pecking order. He was not targeted in the passing game, however. Josh Cuevas had 35 receiving yards on two catches in 15 snaps, while fourth-stringer Nick Vannett played 14 snaps as a blocker. Mark Andrews was quiet with only three receptions for minimal yardage in 38 snaps. The only offensive bright spot was, once again, Zay Flowers. In 57 snaps, Flowers had eight catches for 137 yards with a long touchdown. This was the first game in which Flowers, Rashod Bateman and Ja’Kobi Lane all played together for four quarters. Bateman slightly out-snapped Lane (49 to 46), with Devontez Walker sliding down into a clear No. 4 role with 20 snaps. Defense DL: Nnamdi Madubuike 40, Travis Jones 32, Calais Campbell 24, John Jenkins 15, Aeneas Peebles 6 EDGE: Mike Green 36, Trey Hendrickson 32, Zion Young 21, Ethan Burke 17 ILB: Roquan Smith 46, Trenton Simpson 40, Teddye Buchanan 11 CB: Nate Wiggins 53, Marlon Humphrey 53, Keyon Martin 14, Chidobe Awuzie 2 S: Malaki Starks 53, Kyle Hamilton 50, Keondre Jackson 21, K’Von Wallace 17 The Ravens were on the field for 53 defensive snaps, most of which came in the second half as they gave up five consecutive touchdown drives. Nnamdi Madubuike’s streak of playing 40+ snaps continued, with Travis Jones and Calais Campbell again behind him in order. John Jenkins and Aeneas Peebles combined for 21 snaps. In the first game without Tavius Robinson, Mike Green played the most edge rusher snaps (36). He was closely followed by Trey Hendrickson with 32. Zion Young (21 snaps) and Ethan Burke (17 snaps) continue to be pretty close to each other in snap count. This is a position group that is definitely subject to change moving forward after Robinson’s season-ending injury, and the Ravens need more consistent pass rush. Roquan Smith exited the game briefly with a leg injury but quickly returned, finishing with 46 snaps. Trenton Simpson’s 40 snaps were far ahead of Teddye Buchanan (11 snaps) once again. Simpson has been the team’s most impactful linebacker this season on a week-to-week basis. In the secondary, Nate Wiggins and Marlon Humphrey both played all 53 snaps and struggled to slow down Cincinnati’s wideouts in the second half. Keyon Martin (14 snaps) saw a decrease in snaps from last week and Chidobe Awuzie was again a minimal factor in the cornerback rotation, playing only two snaps. Jaylinn Hawkins’ absence at safety opened the door for both Keondre Jackson and K’Von Wallace to get defensive reps. They combined for 38 snaps. Malaki Starks played the entire game and Kyle Hamilton played 50 snaps.
