The Chiefs did not reach the red zone or the end zone against Seattle. Since 2016, that's happened to teams 56 times. It had never happened to a Patrick Mahomes-led team before tonight. — SūmerSports (@SumerSports) October 26, 2026 Mahomes finished with 165 yards on 19 of 33 passing, posting the fifth-lowest marks of his career for passing yards per attempt (5) and passer rating (58.3). It was only the second time Kansas City has scored three or fewer points with Mahomes at quarterback. The other game was also in Week 7, in 2021, a 27-3 loss to the Tennessee Titans . According to NFL Researcher on X , the Chiefs totaled the fewest yards and first downs of any game started by Mahomes. It was a frustrating night for the two-time MVP, who played without two of his top wideouts — Rashee Rice (hamstring) and Tyquan Thornton (dislocated ankle) — and his starting right tackle, Jaylon Moore (concussion). Still, Mahomes and the Chiefs’ offense have produced more in similarly tough spots before. It was a failure from start to finish in Seattle. Head coach Andy Reid pointed to one key factor in the abysmal performance after the game in his post-game press conference. “You got to keep yourself out of third-and-long situations,” Reid said at the podium. “You’ve got to do better on first and second down. We can do better. We had some penalties in there also that got us going in the wrong direction. Got to take care of those.” On Kansas City’s opening drive, the Chiefs moved the chains on third-and-7, but the officials called an illegal shift on tight end Travis Kelce, wiping away any offensive momentum. Late in the first half, two incompletions opened a drive, and the Chiefs failed to convert on third-and-10 with a screen pass to running back Emmett Johnson. Those possessions put the Chiefs in a hole, and Mahomes couldn’t dig him and the unit out of it. He threw an interception on a second-down pass in Seattle territory that could’ve been avoided. He also fumbled on a third-down play when he didn’t feel the pressure, ending a promising possession. Mahomes reflected on the game at the podium in Seattle. “In order to have success in this league, you got to be able to sustain drives, and we weren’t able to do that,” Mahomes acknowledged. “And obviously they contained the explosive plays. So it’s stuff we have to continue to get better at. You can’t have those mistakes versus this defense.” At one point in the first half, Mahomes was 7/14 with an interception and just 63 yards. He had five straight incompletions in the second quarter, including the interception. “Especially early in the game, I thought my feet were kind of getting me into trouble, where I could have maybe sat in the pocket and made some of the throws down the field,” Mahomes admitted. “I got better a little bit later in the game. But at the same time, when you play a team like that, you can’t let them get ahead and get into a game they want to play.” You don’t often see Patrick Mahomes show frustration like this. But after Xavier Worthy’s drop…. the QB was upset. pic.twitter.com/1TpbgZs5cW — Henry McKenna (@henrycmckenna) October 26, 2026 As the gunslinger settled into primetime, his receivers couldn’t step up with him, and the absence of Thornton was felt as heavily as it has since he was injured. When the offense found a rhythm in the second half, a drop by wide receiver Xavier Worthy had many in Chiefs Kingdom — including Mahomes — wanting to pull their hair out. These feelings are part of a blowout loss, and the Chiefs quarterback knows it’s important to embrace them to move forward. “The biggest thing is you got to feel it. This sucks,” Mahomes said. “You don’t want to perform like this in primetime on a big moment like this. You got to feel it on that plane ride home and understand that it sucks, but then how can you build off it?” Whatever the solution is, it needs to happen for the offense to keep humming as it did in Weeks 1-4. Running back Kenneth Walker was held to just 36 rushing yards, which is simply not a winning formula. “We have to help [Walker],” Mahomes said. “When they put so many eggs in that basket of stopping the run game, we have to have the play-action game and the movement game to be able to throw the ball. And if we’re not proving that, they’re going to continue to put those guys at the line of scrimmage, and that is hard for the run game.”

title: Chiefs Week 7 snap count analysis: L’Jarius Sneed has less playing time
summary: Welcome to Arrowhead Pride’s weekly snap-count analysis! Let’s take a closer look at the Kansas City Chiefs’ snap counts in the 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks in Week 7. The starting lineups are courtesy of NFL Game Stats and Information, and the snap-count data comes from Pro Football Focus’ premium stats. Starters (offensive): LT Kahlil Benson, […]
full_text: (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to Arrowhead Pride’s weekly snap-count analysis! Let’s take a closer look at the Kansas City Chiefs ’ snap counts in the 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks in Week 7. The starting lineups are courtesy of NFL Game Stats and Information, and the snap-count data comes from Pro Football Focus’ premium stats. Starters (offensive): LT Kahlil Benson, LG Kingsley Suamataia, C Creed Humphrey, RG Trey Smith, RT Joshua Ezeudu, QB Patrick Mahomes, WR Jalen Royals, WR Xavier Worthy, RB Kenneth Walker, TE Travis Kelce and TE Noah Gray Starters (defensive): DE George Karlaftis, DT Chris Jones, DT Khyiris Tonga, DE Felix Anudike-Uzomah, LB Nick Bolton, LB Drue Tranquill, LB Jack Cochrane, CB Mansoor Delane, CB Nohl Williams, S Alohi Gilman and S Chamarri Conner Did not play: QB Justin Fields, OT Diego Pounds Inactive: QB Garrett Nussmeier (Emergency third QB), DB Jadon Canady, FB Ben VanSumeren, DE Jack Pyburn, WR Rashee Rice (Hamstring) and OT Jaylon Moore (concussion) The big takeaway: L’Jarius Sneed plays a season-low 14 snaps Early and often, the Seahawks offense attacked Chiefs’ slot cornerback L’Jarius Sneed by throwing over the middle to wide receivers Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Cooper Kupp. Pro Football Focus says Sneed allowed five catches for 83 yards and four first downs. Anecdotally, it felt like the Chiefs adjusted the lineup to exclude Sneed as the game went on, and the snap counts back that up. Sneed played just 14 snaps (11 coverage snaps), just 20% of the defense’s total snap volume. Safety Chris Roland-Wallace (31 snaps) led the team in reps at slot cornerback, lining up there seven more times than Sneed. Roland-Wallace allowed three catches for 15 yards on three targets. It was the least playing time Sneed has had in a single game this season. The matchup was tough for Kansas City’s secondary, but Sneed especially struggled against the slot. The next time the Chiefs face high-end slot receiving talent like Seattle’s, the plan may look different. The Offensive takeaway: Cyrus Allen leads wideouts in production The Chiefs’ wideouts combined for 39 receiving yards on 13 targets. Xavier Worthy (46 snaps): 11 yards on 6 targets Jalen Royals (36 snaps): 0 yards on 2 targets Andrew Armstrong (31 snaps): 3 yards on 2 targets Cyrus Allen (16 snaps): 18 yards on 2 targets Justin Watson (5 snaps): 7 yards on 1 target The fifth-round rookie Allen, who saw the field for just 11 pass plays in Seattle, outproduced the rest of the room with one catch. The Seahawks’ defense suffocated the Chiefs’ passing attack, and quarterback Patrick Mahomes offered little relief, missing a handful of throws, but it’s the second time this season Kansas City’s wide receiver corps got basically shut out. In Week 1, the Chiefs ran to victory over the Denver Broncos , but the pass game needed to step up this week and didn’t. The Defensive takeaway: R Mason Thomas’ playing time decreases After rookie defensive end R Mason Thomas played as many as 50 snaps at times this season, he played just 20 of the defense’s reps against Seattle, a season-low mark for the second-round pick. He was on the field for 15 pass plays, dropping into coverage on three. Thomas was on the field for just five run plays, which matches the four times he played against the run against the Los Angeles Chargers last week. Since the bye week, Thomas’ usage has shifted more toward pass downs than in Weeks 3 and 4. Against the Seahawks, Thomas registered four pressures, including a quarterback hit, coming off of five against the Chargers. The first-year edge rusher may be settling into a more pass-down-only role while defensive ends Felix Anudike-Uzomah (19 run snaps) and Ashton Gillotte (28 run snaps) handle most of the every-down duties. title: 5 things we learned from the Chiefs’ first loss of the season
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs were outmatched in every phase of the game. They kept it close for most of the night, but there was never a time when you felt like they were the better team on the field. The Seattle Seahawks came out determined to shut down Kenneth Walker III, and did just that. […]
full_text: (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs were outmatched in every phase of the game. They kept it close for most of the night, but there was never a time when you felt like they were the better team on the field. The Seattle Seahawks came out determined to shut down Kenneth Walker III, and did just that. As a result, the Chiefs offense turned into a pumpkin as the Seahawks dealt Kansas City their first loss of the season, beating Patrick Mahomes and company 20-3. Here are five things we learned from the Chiefs getting humbled in Washington. 1. K9 is mortal He is still the best running back in the NFL. But Seattle came into this game with one job in mind: don’t let this turn into a revenge game. Their No. 1 priority was to shut Kenneth Walker III down. With Seattle playing so many heavy boxes, you would think it would open up downfield passing for the Chiefs, but that wasn’t the case. With Kenneth Walker kept in check, the Chiefs did not have an answer as to how to move the ball down the field. Walker’s 36 rushing yards were his lowest output of the season, and this game was the worst offensive performance in the Patrick Mahomes era. I thought #Chiefs Kenneth Walker had no ill towards the #Seahawks ? But I guess he does? Weird. Go shake hands man. Video credit: SM Highlights pic.twitter.com/UaAQIviGey — HawkMania (@hawkmania4) October 26, 2026 2. Harrison Butker looks cooked I mentioned last week that it didn’t matter if Harrison Butker can kick 70 yards if he can’t kick it straight. Well, now it appears that he can’t even kick it 58 anymore. Butker missed another field goal from beyond 50 yards, as well as one from 45 yards out. Whether he has the yips and it is temporary, or this marks the beginning of Butker’s physical decline and the end of his best days. Regardless, the Chiefs can’t keep leaving points out on the field, especially in a hard-fought game like this, where points are a premium. If Butker keeps missing these kicks, the Chiefs need to start bringing in available kickers for tryouts. Harrison Butker's 15 missed kicks (10 FGs, 5 PATs) since start of last season are the most in NFL. — Josh Dubow (@JoshDubowAP) October 26, 2026 3. Pass rush continues to be a problem Last week, when the Chiefs played against the Los Angeles Chargers , I wrote that a bad team can make your mediocre pass rush look awesome. Now I’m writing the flip side of that equation—a good team can make your mediocre pass rush look horrible. The Chiefs did a good job early in this game getting Seattle into unfavorable downs and distances, but then someone overpursued the quarterback, and Sam Darnold pulled the ball down and ran for the first down, or found a receiver downfield. If you can’t get to the quarterback, you at least have to contain him. 4. Chiefs need to make a move for a wide receiver at the deadline With Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton both out with injuries, the wide receiver position remains a concern. Heck, even with Rice back, this receiving group just isn’t good enough. The Chiefs need a legit wide receiver who can give them even a fraction of what Jaxon Smith-Njigba offers the Seahawks. Even if it’s half of what he offers, it’s light-years better than what we have now. We need a wide receiver who can get open, not one we scheme open. 5. Spags’ game plan was flawed The Seahawks picked on cornerback L’Jarius Sneed early in this game—moving Jaxon Smith-Njigba around until he found himself lined up across from Sneed. Smith-Njigba then dismantled Sneed on multiple consecutive snaps. Now listen, Smith-Njigba is the best receiver in the NFL. He made two amazing plays against Manoor Delane, including one of the better touchdown catches of the season. My question is: if Smith-Njigba is basically their only offensive weapon, why weren’t you bracketing him from the get-go? Second, if you aren’t going to double-team him, why weren’t you at least having your best cornerback shadow him? I love Sneed, but like Chris Jones, at this point in his career, he’s just not the same guy he once was. Jaxon Smith-Njigba continues his ridiculous 2026 season with another huge performance against the unbeaten Chiefs. 9 REC, 150 REC YDS, 2 CAR, 13 RUYDS, 1 TD vs Chiefs Can the reigning Offensive Player of the Year go back to back? pic.twitter.com/FreW19rwa3 https://t.co/W9EOMOTE7i — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) October 26, 2026

title: Chiefs News: Travis Kelce has record-setting night despite loss
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs suffered the first loss of the season against the Seattle Seahawks on “Sunday Night Football.” The only positive storyline for the Chiefs coming out of the game centered on tight end Travis Kelce, who caught four passes for 44 yards and moved up the career receiving list. He’s now Top 5 all-time […]
full_text: (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs suffered the first loss of the season against the Seattle Seahawks on “Sunday Night Football.” The only positive storyline for the Chiefs coming out of the game centered on tight end Travis Kelce, who caught four passes for 44 yards and moved up the career receiving list. He’s now Top 5 all-time in NFL career receptions, but that wasn’t the only significant milestone passed on Sunday. Chiefs Kingdom, bring the noise to the SB Nation app! Join fellow Chiefs fans to react to every explosive play and game-changing moment in real time. Chat live throughout the game Browse with fewer ads Easily jump between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Download the SB Nation app on your mobile device! For Apple devices, click here . For Android devices, click here . The latest Kansas City Chiefs news Chiefs’ Travis Kelce passes Tony Gonzalez for NFL TE receiving record | USA T0day The Kansas City Chiefs tight end has topped another former Chief, Tony Gonzalez, by setting a new record for most receiving yards by a tight end in NFL history – including the playoffs. And he did it on the big stage of “Sunday Night Football” against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 7. Kelce broke the record on his third reception of the game, which occurred in the fourth quarter of Sunday’s contest. Harrison Butker addresses kicking issues after Chiefs’ loss to Seahawks | The Kansas City Star “The 58-yarder, just short,” he said. “Otherwise it was middle. Obviously, you want to make it, but it was short. And then the 40-yarder at the end, you just got to make it. Just pushed it.” Butker made a 69-yard field goal during the preseason in Tampa, demonstrating he still has the leg strength to connect from 58 yards. Of course, cooler conditions in Seattle can affect a ball’s carry, and Butker thought that might have made the difference on his short attempt to end the first half. “I think I’m at my best when I’m smooth and not overswinging,” Butker said. “Going into that game, our range was the 37-yard line, so that was a 55-yard field goal. And for the 58, I didn’t want to change anything. I just wanted to keep it smooth, and unfortunately it was a little short. Chiefs struggle on 3rd down offensively, defensively in lopsided loss to Seahawks | KSHB 41 “Third downs on both sides of the ball, we can do a better job on those,” Chiefs coach Andy Reid said. Darnold finished 7 of 10 for 110 yards with a touchdown and picked up two first downs, gaining a yard more than he needed both times and finishing with two carries for 17 yards as Seattle converted 11 of 16 third downs. “I think we’ve got to do a better job as a D-line as in closing the pocket, filling those voids to make sure he doesn’t have an escape lane,” Jones said. “That’s something we can look at film and we can correct. A few more stops on third down that we let slip on us.” Seahawks shut down Kenneth Walker, hand Chiefs first loss in battle of NFL heavyweights | The Athletic Walker played his first game in Seattle since he was named MVP of Super Bowl 60 in February. But his old team frustrated him and the Chiefs, holding the NFL’s second-leading rusher to 36 yards on 14 carries. The Seahawks’ defense had that Super Bowl look on Sunday night, holding Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes to 3 points for the second time in his career and first since Oct. 24, 2021, against the Tennessee Titans. Mahomes struggled from the start, completing only 19 of 33 passes for 165 yards, no touchdowns and an interception. Kansas City never reached the red zone. Asked to describe the Chiefs’ effort, Walker simply said: “Terrible.” Jaxon Smith-Njigba, stifling defense help Seahawks hand Chiefs first loss | ESPN Trend to watch: Brett Veach, the Chiefs’ general manager, should continue to be interested in acquiring another wide receiver ahead of the trade deadline on Nov. 10 after the lack of production from the position. Without Rice, who missed Sunday’s game with a strained right hamstring, and Thornton, who is on the injured reserve list after having surgery to repair his dislocated left ankle, the Chiefs’ collection of wideouts — Xavier Worthy, rookie Cyrus Allen, Justin Watson, Andrew Armstrong and Jalen Royals — produced just six receptions for 39 yards. – Nate Taylor Around the NF L Nick Emmanwori: Seahawks’ defense was motivated to stop Kenneth Walker | Pro Football Talk “I ain’t gonna lie, I did,” Emmanwori said. “I’m not gonna sit here and lie. I definitely did want to hold him under 100. I don’t really listen to all the media noise but that was my motivation. I know a lot of dudes on defense, that was their motivation, too, to stop him under 100 and play lights out on defense and I think we did that.” The Seahawks did more than just hold Walker under 100 yards. They held him to 36 yards on 14 carries, by far his worst game of this season and almost 100 yards below his average heading into Sunday night of 133 yards per game. Christian McCaffrey injury: 49ers’ RB says leg ‘just died’ on him during loss to Falcons | CBS Sports After the game, the four-time Pro Bowler gave an update and explained what happened with his leg. “I have no idea. It sucks, because I feel like I was going on a run there, and my leg just died on me,” CMC said. “I was trying to get it going for the whole rest of the game, but it just sucks trying to play like that.” He added some reassurance on his health, saying, “I know I’ll be alright, but it’s just really frustrating.” Raiders’ Klint Kubiak on Fernando Mendoza potentially replacing Kirk Cousins: ‘We’re thinking about everything’ | NFL.com Following the 35-21 loss to the Los Angeles Rams, Raiders coach Klint Kubiak wasn’t ready to make any definitive statements about Kirk Cousins, Mendoza or the rest of his squad. “We have to go watch the film,” Kubiak said, via ESPN. “I think at this point, we’re thinking about everything to fix our problems, how to fix our issues in the red zone, in the third quarter, personnel [and] scheme. We’ve got to talk about all of it.” Cousins struggled mightily in the first half before the Raiders made a game of it in the second half. Vegas trailed 28-6 at halftime, with the offense putting up 128 yards and two field goals. Cousins finished 26-of-44 passing for 295 yards and two touchdowns. If not for two third-quarter turnovers-on-downs, the Raiders might have made it even more interesting late. In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Chiefs-Seahawks: 4 instant takeaways from deflating loss in Seattle Tight ends Travis Kelce and Noah Gray combined for seven catches for 88 yards. The backs and tight ends were Mahomes’ only outlets in Seattle; the Chiefs’ wide receivers combined for 39 yards on 13 targets. We’ll see whether a matchup with the Denver Broncos’ pass defense is more fruitful for the team’s receivers, or whether general manager Brett Veach will be active before the trade deadline on November 10th. title: Myles Garrett’s latest injury update doesn’t help Rams
summary: Myles Garrett has not played for the Los Angeles Rams since Week 1 and the team still is not sure if the edge rusher will return to the field any time soon. Sean McVay was asked about Garrett returning for the Los Angeles Chargers game on Sunday, and the head coach said that he wasn’t […]
full_text: Myles Garrett has not played for the Los Angeles Rams since Week 1 and the team still is not sure if the edge rusher will return to the field any time soon. Sean McVay was asked about Garrett returning for the Los Angeles Chargers game on Sunday, and the head coach said that he wasn’t sure if L.A.‘s superstar offseason acquisition would practice this week or not. McVay said he needs to meet with Reggie Scott, the Rams’ Senior Vice President of Sports Medicine and Performance, before he makes any type of determination. The Rams have not made a determination yet on whether or not to open the practice windows for Myles Garrett or Terrance Ferguson, per Sean McVay. — Nate Atkins (@NateAtkins_) October 26, 2026 McVay was asked about both Garrett and tight end Terrance Ferguson potentially making a return to practice this week, but answered that he wasn’t prepared to answer yet. “I’m not sure yet. I’m not decided on those things.” A follow-up question was asked with regard to when McVay would know whether or not either player would practice this week. McVay only offers further that he’ll meet with the medical team and go from there. McVay doesn’t offer any insight to how he thinks that meeting will go, just that he needs to meet with them before making a decision. “Once I get with Reggie and talk about the approach for the week. Then we’ll just kinda follow their guidance based on where he’s at and how he’s feeling.” It could be gamesmanship, it could be McVay wanted to have genuine deniability for this presser about whether Garrett will play this week or not, but at some point the team will need to make a decision on Garrett. And hopefully soon because the team invested a lot into him as an addition for a defense that is lacking serious firepower upfront this season. The Rams traded a first-round pick, Jared Verse, and more to to get Garrett . He hasn’t played in a game since Week 1, as the 2025 sack leader has yet to notch one single sack or tackle for his new team. The longer Garrett doesn’t suit up, the harder it will be for the Rams to stay afloat in a tough 2026 season where the Rams need to go on a run to make Garrett’s return worth it from a playoff perspective. By the time Garrett is ready, if he’s ready, will there be a point to playing this season? Or, will it better to wait for 2027? As McVay might say, “I’m not sure yet. I’m not decided on those things.”

title: How far can the Rams go without a viable number 2 receiver?
summary: While the Los Angeles Rams did show some offensive sparks in a 35-21 win over the Las Vegas Raiders, a lack of production from the wide receiver corps could threaten to smother the embers before they ignite into flames. Sunday’s win, satisfying as it was, offered no clarity as to who will stake a claim […]
full_text: While the Los Angeles Rams did show some offensive sparks in a 35-21 win over the Las Vegas Raiders, a lack of production from the wide receiver corps could threaten to smother the embers before they ignite into flames. Sunday’s win, satisfying as it was, offered no clarity as to who will stake a claim for LA’s WR2 role. A grand total of two targets were shared amongst the L.A. receiver unit not named Puka Nacua. Both of those targets went to Konata Mumpfield (31 snaps vs L.V.), with one catch for 15 yards. Over his 24 regular season game Rams tenure, Mumpfield has 584 snaps with 42 targets and 19 receptions, a catch rate of 45%. Over that same time frame, Tutu Atwell (25 snaps vs L.V.) has logged 275 snaps, pulling down nine of 19 targets (47%) and Jordan Whittington (15 snaps vs L.V.) has hauled in 20 of 28, a 71 percent catch rate. The three in-house candidates for WR#2 have been targeted 89 times out of 879 L.A. pass attempts for a paltry 10 percent target rate. Having a deep threat, or threats, is critical to explosive plays. There is a correlation between explosive and scoring/winning. Drives that contain big chunk plays score at a far higher rate than without them. The Rams offense is middle of the NFL pack this season in explosives and has been trending down slightly over the past couple of games. On Sunday, they had two plays over 15 yards, both running plays. L.A.’s multiple tight end usage is all well and good and leaning on the run game more often is a welcome occurrence, but to vie for playoff contention and win against better teams, the Rams will have to show that they can press the ball downfield with the pass. They need a viable WR#2. Here’s a review of the snap counts from Sunday. Players, their snap counts and percentage of play time in bold. Quarterback Matthew Stafford ( 72, 100%) Stafford was very efficient in an underneath passing game plan. As was the case last week, he was under five air yards per attempt. He identified the open areas in the coverage, got the ball out quickly, and was accurate. It appeared that the pass blocking was good enough to allow a few more shots down field, but the short game was there and Staff took advantage of it. Running back Kyren Williams ( 37, 51%) Blake Corum ( 32, 44%) The Rams were expected to run freely through the Raiders and the consistently did throughout the game, piling up 199 yards on 38 attempts and two scores. Corum had 50 yards and two touchdowns called back by penalties. Williams ran well, but had another fumble, the 12th of his career. Blake Corum had 17 carries for 93 yards and a TD in the victory. His highest touches total in his career. 2 TDs were called back on penalties. One of them, this 43 yards scamper was explosive. I think we all know it’s only a matter of time until he explodes for another! pic.twitter.com/qiTnZrnyfu — RAMS ON FILM (@RamsOnFilm) October 26, 2026 Wide receiver Puka Nacua ( 65, 81%) Konata Mumpfield ( 31, 43%) Tutu Atwell ( 25, 31%) Jordan Whittington ( 15, 21%) Alex Bachman ( 3, 4%) CJ Daniels ( 3, 4%) It is imperative that the Rams can develop a another receiving threat. The reasons are threefold. L.A.’s pass offense seems to have a sense that it’s built around Nacua breaking tackles for big gains, they seldom target him deep. With his “bull in a china shop” play style, he’s constantly playing banged up, another injury would be devastating to the pass game. And finally, while even good defensive teams will struggle to completely stop him, simply limiting Nacua will cause major problems to the offense overall. Bachman and Daniels got to mop up the final reps in victory formation. Tight end Tyler Higbee ( 53, 74%) Davis Allen ( 50, 69%) Colby Parkinson ( 50, 69%) With 10 minutes left, the Rams were floundering a bit and the Raiders surging, Higbee stretched his full frame to pull in a high third down pass. It was a needed, clutch conversion. Allen came out of college profiled as a vacuum cleaner receiver and has really improved his inline blocking. Nice to see him get a few touches and find the end zone. He is always in the mix down near goal line. Even though he’s been banged up, Parkinson really played a physical game. In the future, the Rams offense will need him powering over defenders for extra yardage. What a throw by Matthew Stafford and catch by Tyler Higbee 🔥 LARvsLV on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/6p15WoLfO0 — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 Offensive line Coleman Shelton, Warren McClendon ( 72, 100%) Alaric Jackson, Steve Avila, Kevin Dotson ( 69, 96%) Beaux Limmer, David Quessenberry, Dylan McMahon ( 3, 4%) Strong outing for big uglies. The Rams used man blocking, hat on a hat, for almost 70 percent of rush attempts (24 of 35). A couple of loops caused some pass pressure early in the game, but generally, the line offered solid pass protection. Special teams Although the coverage units are still a sieve and the Rams former special teams coordinator thumbed his nose at his former bosses with a successful fake punt, it’s nice to report the that the special teams did not put the Rams behind the eight ball. Defensive line Aaron Donald ( 50, 74%) Braden Fiske ( 43, 63%) Tyler Davis ( 28, 41%) Ty Hamilton ( 18, 26%) Larrell Murchison ( 17, 25%) I’m pretty sure I saw the Rams some of their old 5-2 fronts. It was quite a menagerie of pre-snap looks L.A. threw at the Raiders. Donald is beginning to look like his old self, penetrating and blowing up offensive plans. Fiske got the only official Rams sack. Hamilton should have had his first pro sack, but the Raiders QB intentionally grounded the ball. Braden Fiske, shuffle step or kind of up, jab step inside and gets his right armed cocked, right arm clubs/swipes hands of g and he closes the initial stutter gets G off balanced, his head gets over his skis and you can see him in an awkward position and Fiske's hustle does the… pic.twitter.com/qLN4lSLy6b — Jim Youngblood 53 (@53_jim70721) October 26, 2026 Edge Byron Young ( 54, 87%) Josaiah Stewart ( 47, 69%) Wesley Bailey ( 29, 43%) Desjuan Johnson ( 6, 9%) Darryl Peterson ( 5, 7%) Young has blossomed as a solid defender against the run, rushing the passer, and dropping into coverage. Bailey continues to play hard, but has yet to show that he’s more than only there because of Myles Garrett’s injury. Johnson is still not seeing much action. Lake had a nice breakup, but was also flagged for a pair of 15 yard penalties. Curl and McCollough gave up big plays when tasked with deep coverage. title: What Matthew Stafford loves about Rams’ offense this season
summary: Los Angeles Rams’ quarterback Matthew Stafford has been in the NFL for almost two decades, but he believes that this season he has the best running back room behind him that he’s ever had in his career. The combination of Kyren Williams and Blake Corum could surpass any duo he’s ever had in the backfield […]
full_text: Los Angeles Rams’ quarterback Matthew Stafford has been in the NFL for almost two decades, but he believes that this season he has the best running back room behind him that he’s ever had in his career. The combination of Kyren Williams and Blake Corum could surpass any duo he’s ever had in the backfield before and that was apparent during the Rams’ 35-21 win over the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. Williams and Corum rushed for 192 yards on 33 carries against the Raiders. That’s the type of offensive attack that Sean McVay will need moving forward in the absence of Davante Adams for the next two months. Blake Corum had 17 carries for 93 yards and a TD in the victory. His highest touches total in his career. 2 TDs were called back on penalties. One of them, this 43 yards scamper was explosive. I think we all know it’s only a matter of time until he explodes for another! pic.twitter.com/qiTnZrnyfu — RAMS ON FILM (@RamsOnFilm) October 26, 2026 Stafford told Pat McAfee on Monday that he’s perhaps never had a running back duo quite like this, where both backs are so interchangeable play-in and play-out. “It’s a whole lot of fun…I haven’t had a tandem like this where they both can do everything, Right? Usually you have one big guy, one small guy. Big slow gut that can run over people and a small fast guy that can run around people…this is a really unique instance in which we can call our entire offense with both those guys in the game and not bat an eye. Sometimes I get in the huddle and I don’t know which one of ‘em is in the damn game; they look so alike anyways. So, hey, we just go out there and play ball and those guys do what they do.” Stafford has competed with some solid, if not great, running backs like Reggie Bush, Joique Bell, Theo Riddick, D’Andre Swift, Cam Akers, and Darrell Henderson. By comparison, Stafford feels that Williams and Corum offer a “unique” difference as they both can sub in for each other without missing a beat. “I haven’t had a tandem like this where they both can do everything.” —Matthew Stafford on the unique versatility of Kyren Williams and Blake Corum in the Rams' backfield 💪 (via @PatMcAfeeShow ) pic.twitter.com/AXpRA2aLq5 — NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) October 26, 2026 To hear Stafford tell it, they don’t have separate packages for each back. The playbook stays the same regardless of which back is in there, and that’s a huge boost for L.A.‘s offense, while being tricky on opposing defenses. It’s a feature Stafford doesn’t believe he’s had before in his career. "Corum is the runner built for volume, since Williams plays so much in pass protection and the receiving game. He can save Nacua from having to amass so many catches that he risks getting hurt again. He can provide the explosive plays missing without Ferguson." https://t.co/QPGI6RxaMr — 32BeatWriters (@32BeatWriters) October 26, 2026 The Rams offense was clicking in Week 6 as L.A.‘s run game put up 199 yards to complement Stafford’s 187 passing yards and three touchdowns. It was perhaps the first time the Rams showed a “balanced” attack all season in terms of runs vs. passes. It worked. On the season, Williams has 96 carries to Corum’s 64. Williams, to his credit, has also been a demon in the passing game with 32 catches to Corum’s 10 . The stats say Williams is the lead back, and he is, but watch for the Rams to give more carries/touches to Corum as long he keeps producing . The Rams will likely need both backs to continue to be effective beyond Week 6 to truly stamp themselves in the playoff race, and re-establish themselves as a Super Bowl contender . Having two running backs you can lean on seems better than only having one, and to hear Stafford tell it, he doesn’t care whether it’s Williams or Corum getting the work, he just wants to keep working with them. Both of them.
author: Danny Stone

title: Brian Thomas Jr sweepstakes favor Rams, not 49ers
summary: The Los Angeles Rams could have the upper hand over the San Francisco 49ers if the Jacksonville Jaguars decide to trade wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. While both NFC West rivals could use additional help at wide receiver, several factors suggest the Rams are better positioned to land the former first-round pick. From their front-office […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FL - SEPTEMBER 13: Brian Thomas Jr. #7 of the Jacksonville Jaguars reacts after a play during the game between the Jacksonville Jaguars and the Cleveland Browns on September 13, 2026 at EverBank Stadium in Jacksonville, Fl. (Photo by David Rosenblum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams could have the upper hand over the San Francisco 49ers if the Jacksonville Jaguars decide to trade wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. While both NFC West rivals could use additional help at wide receiver, several factors suggest the Rams are better positioned to land the former first-round pick. From their front-office connections to their projected draft capital, the Rams have multiple advantages that could make Los Angeles a more appealing trade partner for Jacksonville. 🚨🚨The #Rams have been linked to #Jaguars Brian Thomas Jr. Both organizations' front offices are very familiar with each other. pic.twitter.com/UWn3Fn6Jyw — NFL Rumors (@nflrums) October 24, 2026 Factor #1: James Gladstone connection The first factor is Jaguars general manager James Gladstone, who previously served as the Director of Scouting with the Rams. Gladstone spent years working alongside Los Angeles’ front office before taking over in Jacksonville, giving the Rams a connection that San Francisco cannot match. Gladstone is not obligated to favor his former organization, but familiarity between the two front offices could help facilitate trade discussions. He may also be less inclined to strengthen a division rival that has spent years competing against Los Angeles for NFC West supremacy. If Jacksonville decides Thomas is available, Gladstone could be more comfortable negotiating with the Rams than helping San Francisco improve its roster. Factor #2: 49ers have alternatives at wide receiver San Francisco’s injuries at wide receiver could create a need for reinforcements, but the 49ers might not need to make a significant investment in Thomas. Their injured receivers could return in the coming weeks, potentially reducing the urgency to pursue a trade. Additionally, San Francisco already has established offensive weapons in Mike Evans and George Kittle. Depending on the health of its receiving corps, the 49ers could prioritize bringing back Jauan Jennings rather than surrendering valuable draft capital for Thomas. The Rams, meanwhile, have a compelling reason to explore the market for another receiver. Adding a young, explosive playmaker would give their offense another option capable of creating separation and stretching defenses vertically. Factor #3: Rams could offer Jacksonville better draft capital Perhaps the most important factor is the draft compensation Los Angeles could offer. Following a 3-4 start, the Rams are currently positioned to select 14th overall in the 2027 NFL Draft. If those projections hold, their second-round selection would be 45th overall. San Francisco’s second-round pick is projected to fall at No. 62, giving Jacksonville a potentially less attractive option if both teams offer comparable packages. A difference of 17 selections in the second round could matter to a rebuilding team seeking to maximize its return on a young receiver. Ultimately, the Rams have the front-office connection, the positional need and potentially the better draft pick to make a compelling offer. San Francisco remains a possible suitor, but if the Jaguars entertain trade discussions, Los Angeles could have the advantage in the Brian Thomas Jr. sweepstakes.

title: Rams PFF grades: Blake Corum sparks offense in win over Raiders
summary: The Los Angeles Rams scored a much-needed 35-21 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. The offense posted their highest scoring total on the season so far. The running game helped their unit course correct. Blake Corum and Kyren Williams took over the game. It’s encouraging to see the offense back on track. One […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - OCTOBER 25: Blake Corum #24 of the Los Angeles Rams is tackled by Treydan Stukes #31 of the Las Vegas Raiders during the fourth quarter at Allegiant Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams scored a much-needed 35-21 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. The offense posted their highest scoring total on the season so far. The running game helped their unit course correct. Blake Corum and Kyren Williams took over the game. It’s encouraging to see the offense back on track. One win isn’t enough to say the Rams have turned things around. There is certainly more work to be done in order to take a playoff berth seriously. These are the grades and advanced metrics from Sunday’s win from Pro Football Focus (PFF): Top five grades on offense 1 – Blake Corum, RB: 87.4 Let’s take Corum and Williams together. Corum: 17 rushes for 93 yards, 1 TD Williams: 16 rushes for 99 yards, 1 TD, 1 fumble lost That’s the box score. Williams probably had the more impressive day outside of his lost fumble that helped Las Vegas gain momentum. Corum: 2.74 yards before contact, 47 yards after contact, 2 forced missed tackles Williams: 1.89 yards before contact, 69 yards after contact, 8 forced missed tackles The Rams offense needed a spark. Corum contributed two rushes over 15 yards and totaled 32 breakaway yards. Creating explosives on the ground helped an offense that is struggling to create chunk gains. Blake Corum: really good at football pic.twitter.com/NH2qHvjL4D — Sosa Kremenjas (@QBsMVP) October 26, 2026 2 – Puka Nacua, WR: 86.8 It was no surprise to see Nacua handle a heavy workload with Davante Adams injured. Nacua caught eight of 10 targets for 68 yards with a touchdown. 47 of his yards came after the catch point, so he was creating in addition to what the offense designed for him. 3 – Warren McClendon, RT: 75.2 The offensive line only allowed two pressures in pass protection, of which both were attributed to McClendon. The right tackle was handed a touch matchup in Maxx Crosby, and he prevented the star pass rusher from wrecking the game. While McClendon was not LA’s best blocker in the run or pass games, he fared the best of the group across the boards. He was consistent in both phases. 4 – Kyren Williams, RB: 72.3 5 – Matthew Stafford, QB: 70.5 Stafford’s grade in this game was roughly the same as his performance in Buffalo. His best outing on the year was still Week 2 against the New York Giants. He’s at 66.5 on the season. Stafford did not make a big-time throw against the Raiders. He also played mistake-free football—no turnover-worthy plays—despite throwing an interception. This was efficient quarterback play that stuck to the script . That’s still better than the level we’ve seen from Stafford so far this year. On the season Stafford has nine big-time throws and 12 turnover-worthy plays. Other notes on offense It’s worth keeping an eye on the receiver rotation as the Rams look to replace Adams. These are the snap counts from the game: Konata Mumpfield: 31 Tutu Atwell: 25 Jordan Whittington: 15 Alex Bachman: 3 CJ Daniels: 3 Mumpfield was the only player of this group that was targeted. He caught one of two targets for 15 yards. The Rams WR's put on a blocking display against the Raiders. Puka, Whittington & Mumpfield getting after it on just about every big run. That is evidence of a really good culture. Unselfish. — Daniel Jeremiah (@MoveTheSticks) October 26, 2026 Top five grades on defense 1 – Jaylen Watson, CB: 90.5 Watson allowed just two catches on eight targets for 17 yards. He forced more pass breakups with three than he allowed completions. That’s an elite game. Watson did his best work against Tre Tucker where he was targeted five times and allowed just one catch for 13 yards. Jaylen Watson allowed just 2 receptions on 10 targets in coverage against the Raiders, recording 4 passes defensed. The only other player to allow 2 or fewer receptions & 4+ passes defensed in a game this season is teammate Trent McDuffie (Week 2 vs NYG). #LARvsLV | #RamsHouse — Next Gen Stats (@NextGenStats) October 25, 2026 2 – Shaun Dolac, MLB: 84.3 3 – Omar Speights, MLB: 82.6 Omar Speights and Shaun Dolac led the defense in run grade at 84.2 and 78.3, respectively. Speights’ grade was lower because he missed two tackles. Dolac graded better in pass coverage, where he allowed only a single reception for four yards. Nate Landman missed the game because of a stint in the NFL’s concussion protocol. His replacements stepped up in a big-time way for LA. 4 – Josh Wallace, CB: 78.5 Similar to Watson, Wallace was also targeted often. He allowed four receptions on eight targets for 22 yards, with 12 coming after the catch point. The former UDFA has played well over the last few weeks as Watson and Trent McDuffie have battled injury. The secondary is performing at a high level. 5 – Ty Hamilton, DT: 76.2 The defensive line rotation is a work in progress after learning that Poona Ford will miss the remainder of the season and Kobie Turner will be out an extended period of time. Hamilton made his case for more snaps against the Raiders with strong grades against the run and pass. With 18 snaps in Las Vegas, will Hamilton’s workload continue to increase? This was his best performance in a long while. Other notes on defense While the secondary is performing very well, the defensive line is another story. LA was stingy in run defense. The Raiders are not a good rushing team. The pass rush was another story. LA pressured Kirk Cousins 16 times, which is a positive. They finished with two sacks. This was accomplished in the aggregate as opposed to an individual player stepping up: Byron Young: 3 pressures Omar Speights: 2 Wesley Bailey: 2 Braden Fiske: 2 Josaiah Stewart: 2 Quentin Lake: 2 Ty Hamilton, Aaron Donald, Kamren Curl: 1

title: Did Rams sense Jared Verse was turning into a 1st round bust?
summary: Jared Verse’s lack of pass-rush development through 2+ seasons is becoming a concerning storyline, raising rumors about whether the Los Angeles Rams saw warning signs before Verse’s career took an unexpected turn via trade. Through seven games with the Cleveland Browns, Verse has recorded zero sacks, a disappointing start for a former first-round pick expected […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NJ - OCTOBER 11: Jared Verse #8 of the Cleveland Browns rushes during the game against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on October 11, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Rich Graessle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Jared Verse’s lack of pass-rush development through 2+ seasons is becoming a concerning storyline, raising rumors about whether the Los Angeles Rams saw warning signs before Verse’s career took an unexpected turn via trade . Through seven games with the Cleveland Browns, Verse has recorded zero sacks, a disappointing start for a former first-round pick expected to become a disruptive force off the edge – not to mention entering Year 3 – a year where players are suppose to breakout. While sacks do not tell the entire story of a pass rusher, the lack of production becomes more concerning when paired with questions about his development as a technician. The Verse third down rush looks a little different than his predecessor pic.twitter.com/0BMgFILYXq — Anthony Lima (@SportsBoyTony) October 18, 2026 Verse has continued to rely heavily on his bull rush, attempting to overpower offensive tackles rather than consistently winning with a diverse collection of pass-rush moves. That approach can work against certain opponents, particularly when a defender possesses the strength and explosiveness to collapse the pocket. However, NFL offensive tackles are talented enough to adjust when they know what is coming. Without a reliable secondary move, Verse risks becoming a predictable pass rusher. Developing a counter move, such as a rip, swipe or spin, can help defenders capitalize when offensive tackles anticipate the initial power rush. Until Verse demonstrates that ability consistently, opposing blockers can focus on absorbing his bull rush without worrying about a sudden change of direction. The question now is whether the Rams recognized these limitations before moving on from the former first-round selection. Los Angeles invested significant draft capital in Verse, expecting his physical tools to translate into consistent production at the highest level. Of course, seven games without a sack do not automatically make a player a bust. Quarterback pressure, run defense and the circumstances surrounding a player’s new team all matter when evaluating performance. Still, the combination of zero sacks and an apparently limited pass-rush arsenal creates legitimate reasons for concern. When Myles Garrett returns, the Rams will likely be reassured that they made the right decision paying Jared Verse and a first round draft pick for the defending Defensive Player of the Year. Had they not, the Rams would have been facing a tough decision as to whether they should or should not offer a handsome contract extension to Verse. With edge rushers commanding money $45.0+ AAV, the Rams could have been stuck with a sizable payday for a player that has shown inability to evolve into anything more than just a slightly above average bull rusher. It seems like Les Snead made the right call once again.
author: Steven Ridings

title: Rams have 2 must-win games left before trade deadline
summary: The Los Angeles Rams looked better during this week’s 35-21 win over the Las Vegas Raiders than they did in the previous game’s loss to the Arizona Cardinals, but one victory against a team on a four-game losing streak isn’t enough to prove that Sean McVay and Matthew Stafford are all the way back. The […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams looked better during this week’s 35-21 win over the Las Vegas Raiders than they did in the previous game’s loss to the Arizona Cardinals, but one victory against a team on a four-game losing streak isn’t enough to prove that Sean McVay and Matthew Stafford are all the way back. The Rams are entering a three-game stretch on their schedule in which their next three opponents have a combined record of 3-15-1, and L.A. needs to sweep them — 0-6 Chargers, 1-4-1 Commanders, 2-5 Cardinals — if they want any chance of making a strong playoff push after their bye week. Should the L.A. Rams lose to either the Chargers or Commanders before the November 10 trade deadline however, then Les Snead must consider if his roster is better served as a fire sale to recoup 2027 draft picks than as a contender hoping to sneak into the playoffs as a wild card. The schedule gets significantly harder after November, so if the Rams can’t beat the Chargers and Commanders, who can they beat? Rams playoff standings The Rams are 3-4 and just one game behind the 4-3 Packers for the final spot in the NFC playoffs standings as of Monday. L.A. is also behind the Seattle Seahawks (beat the Chiefs) and Atlanta Falcons (beat the 49ers) in the standings, both of whom are 4-3. So the climb isn’t just one up, it’s climbing over other teams too. The Rams will have their direct chance at beating the Seahawks in Week 16 and Week 18, but both teams have to still be in the playoff hunt by then, which isn’t necessarily something that’s clearly going to be the case. And if the Rams lose to the 0-6 Chargers this week, what business do they have projecting themselves as Super Bowl contenders? It’s not just being 3-5 that would hurt, it’s the fact that L.A. has also lost to a team like Arizona already. Even in beating the Raiders, the Rams proved that they have work left to do defensively. The Raiders have three wins, but those came against the Dolphins, Chargers, and Saints; Three teams with a combined record of 3-16. Now the last thing that McVay needs on his record is being the first team that loses to the Chargers this season. Especially at a stadium that the other team pays $1 in rent to the Rams to play in. The other L.A. team is so desperate for a win that they’ll do just about anything to upset the Rams this week, and the Chargers are coming off of their bye week, giving them an extra week to prepare and rest for what may as well be their “Super Bowl” of 2026. Both teams really need this win The Rams can’t afford a loss to the Chargers, otherwise they should seriously consider putting all of their stars on the trade block and hoping to recoup the first-round pick they gave up for Myles Garrett, and more. If the Rams drop to 3-5 by losing to a winless team, is it rational to think that they can go 8-1 or 9-0 the rest of the way against that remaining schedule for the respectable record they need? Or should they be looking at Stafford, Puka Nacua, even Garrett himself, and say “We should try to get first-round picks for next year”? Many people on the Chargers can’t afford to lose either. Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel has been largely blamed for L.A.’s offensive woes and could be fired after this week if the Chargers lose to the Rams. Justin Herbert is spinning out with eight interceptions this season already. Jim Harbaugh’s entire reputation as a good head coach is being questioned. General manager Joe Hortiz knows he could be the next GM fired after seeing what happened to Chris Ballard. A win over the Rams would do a lot for everyone on the Chargers, especially now that they know how badly the Rams also need it. So it may seem like 3-4 vs. 0-6, but to these teams it may as well be 6-0 vs 6-0. It’s a must-win matchup for both sides…but still only the first of many must-win matchups for the Rams.
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: Who has thrown more touchdowns for the Rams than Matthew Stafford?
summary: No one has thrown more touchdowns for the Los Angeles Rams than Matthew Stafford. Yes, the headline was a bit of a trick question as the answer is in the question because on Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders, Stafford threw three touchdowns and became the Rams franchise leader in passing scores. Stafford passed Roman […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - OCTOBER 25: Matthew Stafford #9 of the Los Angeles Rams passes the ball against the Las Vegas Raiders during the first quarter at Allegiant Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images No one has thrown more touchdowns for the Los Angeles Rams than Matthew Stafford. Yes, the headline was a bit of a trick question as the answer is in the question because on Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders, Stafford threw three touchdowns and became the Rams franchise leader in passing scores. Stafford passed Roman Gabriel to take the record. Stafford also leads the Detroit Lions in passing touchdowns, making him the only quarterback to lead two separate franchises in throwing scores. Not bad. Stafford has broken and or matched records before, and he did it again on Sunday, but his team won the game too. The best of both worlds. Stafford can enjoy his record setting ways this week, and enjoy his win before the Rams try to do it all again and try to notch another win in Week 8. Rams beat Raiders as Matthew Stafford sets franchise TD record (cbssports) “Stafford has 155 touchdown passes in a Rams uniform, one more than previous team record holder Roman Gabriel. The reigning MVP also became the first player to accomplish that for two teams; Stafford’s 282 touchdown passes is Detroit’s record.” Rams’ Matthew Stafford Gets Strong Words Amid Major Career News (sports.yahoo) “This is Stafford’s second time achieving such a feat, doing so with the Detroit Lions. “Matthew Stafford is the first quarterback in NFL history to lead two different franchises in passing touchdowns,” Rams PR posted. “Congratulations Matthew; ALL TIME PASSING TD LEADER!” Rams legend Jim Everett said in a post on X , tagging the team.“ Puka Nacua addresses reinjury fears after MRI reveals calf injury details (sports.yahoo) “”Just trying to run, and deceleration after, guys, it kind of tapped off on the play. I just planted, and just felt something in my lower calf,” he said. The Rams star also confirmed that the MRI had not revealed anything significant, although he was unsure which specific muscle had been affected. Nacua admitted that avoiding the fear of reinjury was part of his preparation before facing the Raiders. “I try to mentally prepare and say that I’m full focus and being able to play in the game and kind of letting some of those worries and fears go,” he explained.“ Kyren Williams and Blake Corum combine for feat last accomplished in 2001 (sports.yahoo) “Corum eclipsed Williams in carries, 17 to 16, picking up 93 yards and a touchdown. Williams had 99 yards and a touchdown. This actually has happened since Faulk and Canidate, but it was in the playoffs. During the Rams’ divisional round win over the Dallas Cowboys on January 12, 2019, both Todd Gurley and C.J. Anderson rushed for over 100 yards and a touchdown, combining for 238 rushing yards and three scores in the 30-22 win. That was the last NFL playoff game that was played at the Los Angeles Coliseum.“ After losing their identity on offense, the Rams may have just found it (ramswire) “ In a 35-21 win over the Raiders , the Rams handed it off to their running backs 33 times. Kyren Williams rushed for 99 yards and a touchdown on 16 carries. Blake Corum had 93 yards and a touchdown on 17 carries. They combined for 192 yards rushing and 30 yards receiving, running exceptionally well all afternoon. It could’ve been much more, too, because Corum had a 43-yard touchdown run called back by a penalty.“ Matthew Stafford sets Rams TD pass record as Los Angeles rolls past Raiders 35-21 (espn.com) “ Matthew Stafford threw for 195 yards and three touchdowns to become the Rams’ career leader in passing TDs, and Los Angeles resembled the team previously favored to win the Super Bowl, beating the Las Vegas Raiders 35-21 on Sunday. The Rams (3-4) still have a ways to go to overcome their slow start and numerous injuries, but this victory improves their chances to be a factor in the playoff race. Since the NFL playoffs expanded from 12 to 14 teams in 2020, 10 of 41 clubs have made the postseason after opening 3-4, with just 4 of 33 making it after going 2-5.“ Rams open as heavy favorites vs. winless Chargers in Week 8 (ramswire) “The Chargers are the only winless team left in the NFL and coming off a bye, they’ll surely be motivated. The Rams, though, will be equally fired up after starting the season 3-4. According to BetMGM, the Rams are heavily favored in this matchup, opening as 7-point favorites over the Chargers. The over/under is set at 43.5 points, with the Rams being -325 to win straight-up on the moneyline (bet $325 to win $100).“ Is Blake Corum overtaking Kyren Williams as Rams’ top RB? (ramswire) “ Against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday , there may have been a shift in the Rams’ backfield. Williams once again got the start, as he has every week that he’s been available since Week 2 of the 2023 season. However, it was Corum who got the first carry of the day. After throwing three straight passes on the opening three-and-out with Williams on the field, Corum took over at running back on the second drive. And so when the Rams decided to run the ball for the first time, he was the one taking the handoff.“ Hobbled Nacua has 68 yards, TD vs. LV (nbcsports) “Nacua, dealing with a calf injury, didn’t appear to be 100 percent but still got by just fine against a beatable Vegas secondary. He caught one of Matthew Stafford’s three touchdowns and led the Rams offense with ten targets. Nacua has a good chance of leading the NFL in targets for the remainder of the season with Davante Adams (hamstring) out indefinitely. His role in the LA offense makes Nacua one of the most dangerous fantasy options in the game. He gets the Chargers secondary in Week 8.” Rams Winners and Losers: Blake Corum Makes His Case for Bigger Role Against Raiders (sports.yahoo) “After last week’s loss to the Arizona Cardinals, in a moment of frustration, Williams said that the offense lacked energy because he wasn’t on the field. It may have been a nothingburger, but Sunday was a reminder that Williams needs to focus on his game and the rest will follow. In the third quarter, Williams let the Raiders back in the game with his second fumble of the season. Williams sucked the energy out of the offense. The fumbling issues continue to be his Achilles heel. He finished one yard shy of 100 yards, but the turnovers matter. Winner: LB Shaun Dolac/Omar Speights The Rams were without Nate Landman on Sunday and Speights filled in nicely in a full-time role. Speights was great against the run, finishing with six tackles, including two tackles for loss. Shaun Dolac deserves more opportunities on defense after adding three tackles of his own. Nate Landman is a captain and has a knack for forcing turnovers, but the Rams looked good at linebacker against the Raiders.“ Comment of the Day: “We learned that the sky isn’t falling and that the sun will rise again tomorrow. Seriously…I’m so proud of the effort in a make or break game. The team I watched today can play with anybody. With backups. I’m not saying it’s still Super Bowl or bust but we won the line of scrimmage. Again, with lots of reserves. Think about what this does for team confidence. It’s only one game, but it’s a big one.” -Sunsetstripped Feed post of the day:
author: Danny Stone

title: Geno Smith gets earful from Garrett Wilson in New York Jets loss to Miami Dolphins ahead of Las Vegas Raiders matchup
summary: Point blank, Week 7 sucked for the Las Vegas Raiders, as they got blown out by a very injured Los Angeles Rams team. But let’s see how the weekend fared for a few old friends: Geno Smith, Jermaine Eluemunor and Geno Smith Score: 28-25 Jets lose Stats: 23/30 (76.7%), 287 yards, 3 TDs, 1 INT […]
full_text: (Photo by Jordan Bank/Getty Images) | Getty Images Point blank, Week 7 sucked for the Las Vegas Raiders , as they got blown out by a very injured Los Angeles Rams team . But let’s see how the weekend fared for a few old friends: Geno Smith, Jermaine Eluemunor and Geno Smith Score: 28-25 Jets lose Stats: 23/30 (76.7%), 287 yards, 3 TDs, 1 INT We’re a week away from Smith’s revenge game as the Raiders head to New York next week. Both teams desperately need a win if they have any hopes of keeping their slim playoff chances alive, especially after both clubs lost on Sunday. However, the bigger story was Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson giving Smith an earful on the sidelines with the team down four points in the fourth quarter. What’s interesting is that the quarterback had a decent game, but Wilson could have been frustrated with only getting three targets. That, plus losing to a winless Dolphins team, will do that. The wideout tried to brush off the situation, saying he and Smith were “collaborating” (h/t SNY Jets ). Jets WR Garrett Wilson appeared frustrated on the sidelines during the team's loss vs. the Dolphins. (📺 CBS) pic.twitter.com/tMhvk78oC2 — NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) October 25, 2026 Jermaine Eluemunor Score: 27-21 Giants win in OT Truth be told, Eluemunor’s spotlight is less about Week 7 and more about the post/tweet from Pro Football Focus below. Heading into the weekend, the offensive tackle has the highest pass-block win rate (96.7%) of his entire position. However, PFF’s preliminary grading (which is subject to change after review) has him on the hook for a couple of pressures against the Houston Texans . So, Eluemunor’s pass protection standing could be changing a bit, but he’s still playing well, and the Giants have a decent command of the NFC East at 4-2-1, while the 2-4 Philadelphia Eagles and 2-4 Dallas Cowboys battle it out for second place on Monday Night Football . These young men are protecting their QBs pic.twitter.com/GRrDR47WGA — PFF (@PFF) October 22, 2026 Josh Jacobs Score: 20-17 Packers lose Stats: 11 carries, 36 yards (3.3), 5 catches, 55 yards, 1 receiving TD This was Jacobs’ first game back since being removed from the Commissioner’s exempt list after being charged with a misdemeanor for a domestic incident this offseason. A couple of weeks ago, he took a plea deal for two misdemeanor charges, and his case is still under review by the NFL for a potential suspension. On the field, the running back didn’t find much success on the ground, but he did have an impressive 25-yard touchdown catch, tightroping the sideline for a score. However, Jacobs did have a costly drop in the end zone that would have given the Green Bay Packers a six- or seven-point lead with about 3:30 left on the clock. Instead, the Packers’ kicker missed a field goal, and the Lions’ kicker nailed a walk-off. title: Kirk Cousins remaining Raiders’ starting quarterback
summary: Sunday night, Las Vegas Raiders coach Klint Kubiak opened the door to a potential starting quarterback change when he said the team needs to look at everything in an attempt to snap a four-game losing streak. Monday afternoon, however, Kubiak made a point to put the end of any speculation that that the team could […]
full_text: (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images Sunday night, Las Vegas Raiders coach Klint Kubiak opened the door to a potential starting quarterback change when he said the team needs to look at everything in an attempt to snap a four-game losing streak. Monday afternoon, however, Kubiak made a point to put the end of any speculation that that the team could replace veteran Kirk Cousins with rookie Fernando Mendoza. Kubiak began his press briefing by stating Cousins is the starter. “There is no controversy here,” Kubiak said Kubiak said that Cousins is playing well and the team needs to run the ball better to help the offense. He said Mendoza, the No. 1 overall draft pick, will “eventually” play but the time is not now. He said the 3-4 Raiders are still in the playoff hunt and winning is the priority. Thus, Cousins will remain the starter. It is my read that Kubiak was never really going to consider a quarterback change this week, but his big-picture way of answering the question Sunday night fueled the speculation. That’s why he made it clear Monday that a change will not be happening. Meanwhile, Kubiak said wide receiver Jack Bech is expected to begin practicing this week. He’s been on he injured reserve for the past four weeks with a broken forearm. He will have three weeks to ramp up. The team has until Wednesday to either activate Dont’e Thornton or keep him on the injured reserve all season.
