title: Quay Walker’s coverage woes continue to haunt Las Vegas Raiders in Week 7 loss to Los Angeles Rams
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders have wiped away just about any momentum the team had with a 3-0 start, dropping their fourth straight contest with the Week 7 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. Despite the Rams being heavily injured heading into the game, Los Angeles managed to outclass Las Vegas, leading 28-6 heading into the […]
full_text: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders have wiped away just about any momentum the team had with a 3-0 start, dropping their fourth straight contest with the Week 7 loss to the Los Angeles Rams . Despite the Rams being heavily injured heading into the game, Los Angeles managed to outclass Las Vegas , leading 28-6 heading into the fourth quarter before a few garbage-time scores made the scoreboard look prettier at 35-21. That doesn’t leave much room for winners in this week’s winners and losers column. LOSER: Quay Walker To be fair, Walker did have a couple of good stops against the run to give the defense a handful of quality plays. However, he continues to be a liability in coverage, allowing six catches on six targets for 51 yards and a touchdown, according to Pro Football Focus , while also drawing a flag. All of those figures were team highs, and it’s the third week in a row that he’s given up a perfect completion percentage to go along with at least five catches and 50 yards when targeted. The story of the former Green Bay Packer’s career is that he lacks awareness and instincts in coverage. That’s continued in Las Vegas, as opposing offenses are picking on him by giving him eye candy when playing zone or taking advantage of his aggressiveness against the run via play-action passes to open up the middle of the field. On top of that, Walker has had issues against scramble drills, failing to plaster to his man. In other words, the free-agent signing hasn’t improved on his biggest weakness. LOSER: Tonka Hemingway It’s no secret that the Raiders have a massive need at defensive tackle. Meanwhile, Hemingway drew plenty of praise during training camp but hasn’t done much during the regular season, including on Sunday. While he did register his first sack of the season, that was the result of Nakobe Dean setting a great pick on a stunt rather than the defensive tackle winning on his own. Also, the second-year pro had just one other pressure throughout the game and was part of the Raiders’ run defense issues, posting a 41.6 PFF run defense grade . Granted, this was Hemingway’s first game since suffering a concussion a couple of weeks ago, and he participated in 21 snaps against the Rams. However, these issues go beyond this past weekend, with a 39.9 run defense mark and just seven pressures in six games. WINNER: Dylan Laube While Laube didn’t receive any offensive snaps (outside of the fake punt), he had a pair of notable kick returns that gave the Silver and Black’s offense short fields. He returned the opening kickoff for 36 yards to give the Raiders the ball at the 38-yard line, and returned the next one for 42 to cut the field in half. The problem was that those returns resulted in just three points, but the kick returner held up his end of the bargain. For the season, Laube has 435 kick return yards (tied for 13th in the NFL) and leads all returners who have at least seven kick returns with a 31.1-yard average . LOSER: Caleb Rogers The coaching staff’s decision to bench Jackson Powers-Johnson for Rogers hasn’t made any difference in the offense’s running game over the last two weeks. The Raiders managed just 65 yards and 3.3 yards per carry as a team against the Bills and had just 48 yards and 2.8 ypc against the Rams, while Rogers logged 51.8 and 28.6 PFF run-blocking grades in those contests. To be fair, Powers-Johnson wasn’t getting the job done either, with a 43.6 mark in his four outings. But week-by-week, it’s becoming clearer that Las Vegas didn’t do enough at guard during the offseason and will have to address the position again this spring. LOSER: Klint Kubiak Speaking of the guard issue, Kubiak is clearly too tied to Spencer Burford. Those two have a history together, but Buford’s play continues to be uneven where every other game is a bad outing. This past week was a down performance, giving up a sack and posting a 43.5 PFF pass-protection grade to go along with a 52.6 mark in the ground game. It’s time for the head coach to put aside his allegiance and give someone else a try at left guard. Additionally, Kubiak showed more signs of being a rookie head coach on Sunday. After scoring a touchdown to cut the Rams’ lead to 16 at the beginning of the fourth quarter, he opted for the two-point conversion instead of making it a 15-point game. That forced the Raiders to go for it again after scoring on the next possession, only for the try to fail again and allow Los Angeles to maintain a two-possession lead. Using the kicker both times would have made it an eight-point lead with over 13 minutes left on the clock, and failing on two fourth downs in field goal range during both of the team’s third-quarter possessions looms large. The latter brings up another point: the offense is struggling mightily in the red zone, which the offensive play-caller contributes to. Again, these are the results of a first-time head coach, and Kubiak can get better with more experience. But that starts with pointing out and adjusting to the mistakes. LOSER: Kirk Cousins While Cousins has certainly had more good games than bad ones, Sunday was arguably his worst performance of the year. Dropping back for 48 passes and airing the ball out down 28-6 to begin the second half led to a prettier box score, but the book is out on the 38-year-old. Per PFF , the Rams blitzed on 27.1 percent of his dropbacks, resulting in a 46.2 completion percentage (6/13), as his lack of arm strength and mobility really show up when under pressure. But the biggest reason Cousins lands in this week’s losers column is that the calls for Fernando Mendoza to take over are only getting louder. Again, the veteran quarterback isn’t playing poorly this season by any means. But the Raiders are no longer winning with him behind center, and that should start to shift the focus to the future for the rest of the 2026 season. LOSER: Tommy Eichenberg According to Sumer Sports , the Rams were in 13 personnel for 50 percent of their offensive snaps on Sunday, over 41 percent higher than the league average. That led to a season-low 29 snaps for nickelback Taron Johnson and a season-high 43 snaps for Eichenberg , as Rob Leonard countered Sean McVay’s strategy with more base personnel to help stop the run. Seeing as Los Angeles racked up over 200 rushing yards and 5.8 yards per carry before Matthew Stafford’s three kneel-downs, Leonard’s strategy didn’t work. The linebacker was part of the problem, posting a season-low 48.4 PFF run defense grade on 30 snaps as a run defender. That’s a big lost opportunity since Eichenberg got his number called and failed to rise to the occasion.
author: Matt Holder

title: Rams 13-personnel batter Raiders defense
summary: Las Vegas Raiders came into Sunday’s game against the Los Angeles Rams with something to prove against a team that was reeling. Rob Leonard had a great start to the season, but once the big boys of the league showed up, the clock struck midnight on his defensive prowess. His defense has turned back into […]
full_text: (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images Las Vegas Raiders came into Sunday’s game against the Los Angeles Rams with something to prove against a team that was reeling. Rob Leonard had a great start to the season, but once the big boys of the league showed up, the clock struck midnight on his defensive prowess. His defense has turned back into a pumpkin over the last four games, with all the magic beaten out of it. The Rams run 13 personnel (one running back and three tight ends) more than anyone in the league and it was obvious from the second possession that neither Leonard nor the Raiders’ defense had anything for it. Lining up eight men in the box on offense negated everything Leonard had at his disposal. Displaying how little of a push the undersized defensive line really gets on a play-to-play basis. Committing an extra linebacker to the field didn’t help. The cornerbacks were too small to make an impact and constantly got outmuscled. Zone coverage conceded too much space to pass catchers; blitzing players couldn’t outnumber the line and man coverage was getting barbequed by play-action passes. There was hardly any pressure: one sack and only four quarterback hits on Matt Stafford, who set the Rams franchise record for touchdown passes (155). Defense got ran through Marshawn Lynch once said, “if you just run through somebody face a lot of people aint gonna be able to take over and over … run through a mf face and you won’t have to worry about them anymore.” That is exactly what opposing teams have been doing to the Raiders during the four-game losing streak. When the clock read 0:00, the Raiders had surrendered: 35 points, 99 yards rushing to Kyren Williams and 93 yards rushing to Blake Corum, with both scoring rushing touchdowns. As a team, the Rams rushed 38 times for 199 yards and two touchdowns. Tonka Hemingway got a sack on third down of the first drive to force a three-and-out. It would be the only thing that went well for the defense in the first 30 minutes of football. In the first half, the Rams totaled over a hundred yards on the ground and 243 yards tota offense. Going 4/5 on red zone opportunities, scoring four touchdowns without a turnover and with only one punt. Backup tight end Davis Allen caught two touchdown passes in the red zone, and Puka Nacua added one as well. Nacua, the game-time decision, did whatever he felt like as he ran around virtually uncovered and through anyone who dreamed of attempting to tackle him. Tackling continues to be an issue for the Raiders’ defense. The Rams’ ball carriers had no problems lowering their shoulders and driving through them. Stiff-arming guys practically to the ground all while running downhill through holes big enough to drive trucks through. Making something happen To be fair, in the second half, the Raiders’ defense forced two turnovers. Nakobe Dean added a tipped pass interception to his collection of turnovers, his fourth turnover of the season. Jeremy Chinn recovered a fumble for the defense as turnovers came in bunches at the end of the third quarter. At one point helping cut a 25-point lead down to 10 (28-18), making the game interesting for a moment and showing some degree of pride. It was short-lived as the Rams resumed success with their 13 personnel and immediately drove back down the field and scored again boosting the total to 35 points. It was the fourth straight week the Raiders defense has given up 30+ points in a game. With a showdown against the New York Jets, next week on the road with a 10am PST start time, Leonard and the Raiders defense better get their stuff together and do it fast. .
author: Philip Robinson

title: Raiders’ rancid start gives way to a battering by Rams in 35-21 loss
summary: Just how lopsided was the effort to start the contest between the visiting Los Angeles Rams and host Las Vegas Raiders this past Sunday? Puka Nacua showcased more physicality than the entire Raiders team as he ran through tackle attempts showcasing both power and sheer will — all the while the Rams wide receiver was […]
full_text: (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images Just how lopsided was the effort to start the contest between the visiting Los Angeles Rams and host Las Vegas Raiders this past Sunday? Puka Nacua showcased more physicality than the entire Raiders team as he ran through tackle attempts showcasing both power and sheer will — all the while the Rams wide receiver was questionable to play in the Week 7 matchup due to a calf injury. Nacua paced the Rams aerial attack with eight receptions for 68 yards and a touchdown while quarterback Matthew Stafford finished 23 of 29 for 195 yards and three touchdowns and one interception as L.A. rolled into Allegiant Stadium and battered Las Vegas for a 35-21 win, and now both teams sport 3-4 overall records seven games into the respective 2026 campaigns. The Rams came out with a sense of urgency and will to win — the Raiders did not — dropping an avalanche of offense on the Silver & Black for a commanding 28-6 lead just before halftime. “Obviously, not a winning performance. Didn’t start the game well enough at all. Didn’t give ourselves a chance,” Raiders rookie head coach Klint Kubiak said to start his postgame press conference. “Started the game way too slow. Guys fought in the second half, but for us to put ourselves in that big of a hole versus a really good team, well-coached team, you don’t give yourself a chance.” Sean McVay’s Rams offense and Chris Schula’s Rams defense manhandled their Raiders counterparts in Kubiak and defensive coordinator Rob Leonard and did almost whatever they wanted in a dominant first half. Stafford had 148 yards passing and his trio of touchdown throws all in the first half and the Rams’ ground game racked up 103 of it’s total 199 rushing yards in that same timespan. “They’re moving the ball on us way too well. I’ve got to go look at the tape,” was all Kubiak could say when broached with his team’s run defense getting carved up. Kyren Williams extends the lead for the Rams 💪 LARvsLV on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/F2PBZOlOQf — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 The distinct difference in desire and execution in the first half was so apparent that even FOX Sports analyst and former NFL linebacker Jonathan Vilma couldn’t help but question the Raiders defense’s effort on a simple toss play by the Rams that saw running back Kyren Williams easily scamper for the 17-yard touchdown on Los Angeles’ possession before halftime (the specific play is above). No matter what Leonard dialed up to combat the Rams, it was to little to no avail early on as coaching, communication, and player execution was amiss. “I feel like we didn’t get in any situation to kind of help ourselves. We started slow, we wanted to start fast. They played with the lead the whole time,” Raiders edge rusher Maxx Crosby, who finished with four total tackles and a stop for loss, said after the game. “They had like zero drop back passes, and we wanted to obviously rush them, and we really didn’t get many opportunities. But it starts with us, we’ve got to be able to stop the run. I’ve got to watch the film, but overall, it wasn’t good enough at all. We couldn’t stop the run, and it’s really disappointing, and we’ve got to learn from it and get better from it real fast.” Las Vegas did finally kick into gear in the third and fourth quarters — even a fleeting moment of complementary football occurred. Kubiak’s offense clicked late in the third stanza with Tre Tucker’s nifty move after a catch resulted in a 37-yard touchdown. That was immediately followed by a diving interception by middle linebacker Nakobe Dean off a ricochet from the hands of Rams tight end Colby Parkinson. And four plays later, Cousins dropped a dime to running back Ashton Jeanty on a well-designed 15-yard touchdown pass and the Raiders’ trimmed the deficit to 28-18. Sensing a momentum shift, however, the Rams went back to serious mode and produced a 12-play, 70-yard scoring drive that ate more than six and half minutes from the clock to surge ahead 35-18 following that and all Las Vegas could muster was three more points. Tipped INT ‼️ Nakobe Dean comes up with it for the Raiders! LARvsLV on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/nAx5msnWFJ — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 Let’s hit the quick slants as fast as the Rams took control of the contest from the Raiders: —Running back Dylan Laube remains a bright spot as the Raiders primary kick returner. The Rams booted it to the shifty tailback twice and Laube produced 78 yards (long of 42) on the two opportunities. Kicker Matt Gay finished 3 of 4 (missed wide left on his first attempt from 51 yards out) while Cole had two punts for 112 yards (a long of 61 and 56 yard average per boot) with one ending up a touchback and another inside the Rams’ 20-yard line. —The Rams’ Williams and Blake Corum paced the running back production with 16 carries for 99 yards and a touchdown and 17 carries for 93 yards and a score, respectively. Flip it to the Raiders and Mike Washington Jr. led the team with six carries for 27 yards while Ashton Jeanty added eight carries for 15 yards. In total, L.A. churned out 199 yards on 38 carries (5.2 yards per carry average) to Las Vegas’ 17 carries and 48 yards (2.8 yards per carry) total production. —Cousins finished 26 of 44 for 295 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions. He was sacked twice and added six yards on three carries scrambling. Las Vegas’ other pass attempt — from punter AJ Cole III — was a thirteen yard gain on the fake punt. Cole finished with a higher rating (118.8) than Cousins (94.4). —Tucker continues his fine 2026 season with five receptions for 103 yards and a score against the Rams. Tight end Brock Bowers was the next most-productive pass catcher with six grabs for 73 yards. He was followed by Jeanty who had more yards receiving (61 on eight receptions and a touchdown) than rushing. —Dean and fellow linebacker Quay Walker finished with 12 total tackles , apiece, to lead all defenders in Sunday’s game. Walker added two stops for loss while Dean had the interception and a pass deflection. Cornerback Darien Porter, safety Jeremy Chinn, and linebacker Tommy Eichenberg each finished with seven total tackles. —Defensive tackle JJ Pegues punched the ball out with Chinn recovering to produce a takeaway for the Raiders defense. But the defense’s performance in the red zone — the Rams went 5-for-5 when they got to Las Vegas’ 20-yard line — remains a brutal Achilles heel. Kubiak’s Raiders offense went 1-for-5 in the red zone. —The Raiders’ overall efficiency against the Rams is truly disconcerting. The Silver & Black went 3-for-14 on third downs and 2-for-5 on fourth downs. Despite running 64 plays for 350 yards (L.A. had 68 plays for 386, in comparison), the Rams dominated time of possession 34:14 to 25:46. Quotes of Note Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak on potentially starting Fernando Mendoza after a 4th loss in a row and why the team seemed to come out flat in a home loss to the Los Angeles Rams. 🎥: By @Sean_Zittel pic.twitter.com/jPBaGxjwwn — Vegas Sports Today (@VegasSportsTD) October 25, 2026 Raiders center Tyler Linderbaum details the struggles of getting the run game going through six weeks & how important it is going to be moving forward to stick together as a team pic.twitter.com/4W1aSm9sQG — Raider Nation Radio (@RNR920AM) October 26, 2026 Up Next The free-falling Raiders hit the road and head East to face the New York Jets (2-5) for a 10 a.m. (Pacific Standard Time) matchup at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey next Sunday. Aaron Glenn’s Jets are on a two-game skid losing back-to-back to AFC East foes in the New England Patriots (26-19) and the previously winless Miami Dolphins (28-25) this past Sunday. The Raiders want to end a four-game losing streak and in order to do so, they’ll need to drop the Jets on the road. The way Las Vegas played on Sunday, however, Week 8 may be a get-right game for current New York quarterback (and former Raider)…

title: Raiders News: Week 7 AFC West Roundup, Denver Broncos inch closer to Kansas City Chiefs
summary: Week 7 saw the Las Vegas Raiders drop their fourth consecutive game as their playoff hopes are quickly fading. On that note, let’s take a look at the AFC West Standings and check in on the Denver Broncos and Kansas City Chiefs, while the Los Angeles Chargers were on a bye. Broncos vs. Cardinals Score: […]
full_text: (Photo by Chris Coduto/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 7 saw the Las Vegas Raiders drop their fourth consecutive game as their playoff hopes are quickly fading. On that note, let’s take a look at the AFC West Standings and check in on the Denver Broncos and Kansas City Chiefs, while the Los Angeles Chargers were on a bye. Broncos vs. Cardinals Score: 30-16 Broncos win Key Stats: QB Bo Nix: 15/29 (51.7%), 222 yards, 1 TD, 0 INTs, 7 rushes, 73 yards, 1 TD RB Jonah Coleman: 9 carries, 54 yards (6.0 ypc) RB RJ Harvey: 3 carries, 6 yards (2.0 ypc), 2 catches, 54 receiving yards, 1 receiving TD LB Alex Singleton: 19 tackles, 1 sack, 2 QB hits CB Ja’Quan McMillian: 5 tackles, 3 PDs This is the type of game Denver needed. Nix wasn’t exactly bombing it down the field, as his 52-yard touchdown pass was a screen to Harvey, and Marvin Mims did a lot of work after the catch on a 47-yarder. However, all of that becomes irrelevant when the quarterback has a 62-yard score on the ground, and the team wins by two possessions for the first time this season. So, the Broncos still have work to do, but they went to Arizona and took care of business to narrow the gap against Kansas City. Next week: vs. Chiefs Chiefs vs. Seahawks Score: 20-3 Chiefs lose Key Stats: QB Patrick Mahomes: 19/33 (57.6%), 165 yards, 0 TDs, 1 INT, 2 carries, 14 yards RB Kenneth Walker III: 14 carries, 36 yards (2.6 ypc), 4 catches, 21 receiving yards TE Travis Kelce: 4 catches, 44 yards CB Nohl Williams: 10 tackles, 1 INT, 1 TFL LB Nick Bolton: 11 tackles, 1 TFL On the opposite end of the spectrum, Kansas City played its worst game and suffered its first loss of the season. The Seattle Seahawks managed to do what no other team had done yet in 2026: bottle up their Super Bowl MVP. Walker’s return to Seattle didn’t go as planned, notching a season-low rushing total with half as many yards as his previous low (70). Also, that was just the third time in six games he’s been kept below triple digits, and Mahomes couldn’t get anything going in the passing game either. Kansas City’s defense had a fine night, but failed to record a sack and only had two quarterback hits, both from George Karlaftis. That sets up an interesting battle in the Mile High City next week. Next week: @ Broncos LAC Next week: @ Rams Standings Kansas City 5-1 (+40 point differential) Denver 5-2 (+3) Las Vegas 3-4 (-14) Los Angeles 0-6 (-61) In Other Raiders’ Links: Updated AFC Playoff picture: The Raiders are clinging to slim playoff hopes and are quickly falling out of the running. What we learned from Rams loss: “Rob Leonard’s unit isn’t getting it done,” S&BP’s Bill Williamson wrote. “The Raiders have allowed 170 points in the past five games. According to the Associated Press, this ties a franchise record for allowing, at least, 27 points in five straight games and they have also allowed, at least, 30 points in four straight games.” Fernando Mendoza’s time coming?: Klint Kubiak was asked about potentially making a quarterback change, and instead of shooting down the question, he said: “I think at this point, we’re thinking about everything,” via the Las Vegas Review-Journal’s Sam Gordon . Maxx Crosby trade talk picking back up: “Maxx Crosby is a wanted commodity,” CBS Sports’ Pete Prisco said. “And they traded Maxx Crosby once, let’s not forget that…I think they should be sitting there saying, ‘You know what, we can get a bunch of assets for a guy that probably isn’t going to be around here when we become something with our young quarterback. Grading Dolphins’ 28-25 victory over the New York Jets – Chris Perkins, South Florida Sun Sentinel The Miami Dolphins got their first victory of the season in Sunday’s 28-25 breakthrough performance against the New York Jets. The Dolphins (1-5) weren’t perfect, but they were pretty darn good in many ways. Miami Dolphins QB Malik Willis grades: Strong play helps beat Jets – Joe Schad, The Palm Beach Post Miami Dolphins’ Malik Willis was seeking his first win of the season Sunday as starting quarterback in a game at the New York Jets. Four Winners And Four Losers From Miami’s First Win Of 2026 – Jake Gibson, Miami Dolphins on SI It took a complete team effort on all sides of the ball for the Dolphins to shock both the Jets and the rest of the NFL. Where Willis ranks after Sunday. And news, notes on Dolphins’ offensive personnel – Barry Jackson, Miami Herald One good game on Sunday wasn’t enough to lift Malik Willis from the bottom tier of statistical measurements for quarterbacks. title: Fins Up, Fins Down | Winners and losers from Miami Dolphins week seven victory
summary: The Miami Dolphins earned their first victory of the season on Sunday, defeating their AFC East division rivals — the New York Jets — by a score of 28-25. It wasn’t a perfect game by any stretch of the imagination, but the Dolphins gave fans something they haven’t had much of lately — a reason […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 25: Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins looks on during the first quarter against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on October 25, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Jordan Bank/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins earned their first victory of the season on Sunday, defeating their AFC East division rivals — the New York Jets — by a score of 28-25. It wasn’t a perfect game by any stretch of the imagination, but the Dolphins gave fans something they haven’t had much of lately — a reason to smile on a Sunday afternoon. Malik Willis turned in his best performance since joining Miami, and as a result, the offense finally showed some signs of life. Unfortunately, the defense apparently decided that a comfortable lead was an invitation to make things interesting. Let’s hand out this week’s Fins Up and Fins Down honors! FINS UP Our Fins Up player of the week is quarterback Malik Willis. Willis finds himself on the positive side of this article for the first time this season — and for good reason. He finished Miami’s win over the New York Jets with three total touchdowns (two passing and one rushing) while not turning the ball over a single time. His 130.7 passer rating was easily the highest of his season so far — a whopping 79.7 points higher than the last time he took the field (51.0 against the Cincinnati Bengals). Perhaps the most encouraging part of Willis’ performance was his ability to take what the defense gave him rather than constantly searching for the home run. Miami’s offense has looked downright painful at times this season, but Willis demonstrated that the unit can move the football when the quarterback makes good decisions and uses his athleticism effectively. FINS DOWN Our Fins Down player is… well, the entire defensive secondary. Yes, I know that rookie safety Michael Taaffe came down with and interception. That’s great. However, the New York Jets and quarterback Geno Smith moved the ball at will in the second half of Sunday’s contest — en route to a final tally of 287 passing yards and three passing touchdowns. Smith completed an eye-popping 76.7% of his passes, and rookie receiver Omar Cooper Jr. enjoyed an afternoon that saw him nab five receptions for 115 yards and a touchdown. Miami allowed New York to score 18 second half points after building a 21-7 halftime lead. The defense repeatedly gave the Jets opportunities to climb back into the game. Against a better offense, those mistakes could easily turn a win into a loss. The Dolphins cannot expect their offense to keep producing enough points to compensate for a secondary that makes opposing receivers look like they’re running routes against air.

title: Looking Back at the Biggest Trades of the Miami Dolphins’ Rebuild
summary: When it comes to team-building, sometimes you just can’t beat a trade. Need to get younger? Make a trade! Need a veteran for a playoff push? Make a trade! Want to desperately catch lightning in a bottle by acquiring a former first-round quarterback bust? Trade your <wince> second-round pick to Arizona! (I see you, Josh […]
full_text: When it comes to team-building, sometimes you just can’t beat a trade. Need to get younger? Make a trade! Need a veteran for a playoff push? Make a trade! Want to desperately catch lightning in a bottle by acquiring a former first-round quarterback bust? Trade your <wince> second-round pick to Arizona! (I see you, Josh Rosen. I wish I didn’t.) Over the past year, the Dolphins have aggressively reshaped their roster, trading away established veterans, former first-round picks and even future Hall of Famer Quinn Ewers in an effort to accelerate the rebuild. With another deadline approaching, let’s revisit the biggest deals of the past 12 months and see how they’re working out so far. November 2025: Jaelan Phillips The Deal Dolphins traded EDGE Jaelan Phillips for the Eagles’ 2026 third-round pick (No. 87), which was used to select TE Will Kacmarek. The Financial Impact After finishing the season with the Eagles, Phillips signed a massive four-year, $120 million contract with the Carolina Panthers this offseason, including $80 million guaranteed. How Phillips Has Performed After nearly five full seasons in South Florida, where he recorded 177 tackles and 26 sacks, Phillips managed just 28 tackles and two sacks in eight games with Philadelphia. So far in 2026, he has 2.5 sacks and 10 tackles, though he does lead the Panthers with 18 pressures. Stop me if you’ve heard this one before, but Phillips has also missed time with an injury, suffering a hamstring injury in Week 4 before re-aggravating it after the bye. How Kacmarek Has Performed Kacmarek, who was drafted primarily for his run-blocking ability, has largely delivered in that role. After a somewhat slow start, he posted PFF grades north of 70 against Kansas City and Minnesota before turning in a more pedestrian performance against Cincinnati. Early Verdict You’ll recall Phillips called being traded to Philadelphia “the best thing that’s ever happened” to him. Rude. Still, most of us agreed at the time that a long-term, big-money extension carried significant risk. Turning a player you weren’t likely to re-sign into a third-round pick was sound business. You can debate whether Miami reached for a blocking tight end at No. 87, but there’s something to be said for building a nasty offensive line, and Kacmarek helps you do that. For now, I’m good with it. March 2026: Minkah Fitzpatrick The Deal Dolphins traded S Minkah Fitzpatrick for the Jets’ 2026 seventh-round pick (No. 238), which was used to select EDGE Max Llewellyn. The Financial Impact Immediately following the trade, Fitzpatrick signed a three-year, $40 million contract with the Jets. How Fitzpatrick Has Performed So far in 2026, Fitzpatrick is doing Fitzpatrick things. He’s recorded 26 tackles, an interception and two passes defended while posting a 73.8 PFF grade. Nine years into his career, the five-time Pro Bowler and three-time All-Pro still looks like one of the better safeties in football. How Llewellyn Has Performed Well, he hasn’t been released yet, and if you’re a seventh-round pick, that’s a good sign. Llewellyn received five snaps against the 49ers, two on defense and three on special teams, and currently resides on the practice squad. Early Verdict Before the trade, I hoped the Dolphins would do with Fitzpatrick what they did with Jordyn Brooks and keep a proven veteran around as part of the rebuild. If you’re looking to build a secondary of Minkahs, it helps to have the real Minkah on the roster to learn from. So while I understand it, I don’t love that Fitzpatrick was traded. I really don’t love that the return was only a seventh-round pick. And I really, really don’t love that he was traded to the Jets. But when a team commits to a rebuild, sometimes even popular veterans become cap casualties. March 2026: Jaylen Waddle The Deal Dolphins traded WR Jaylen Waddle and a 2026 fourth-round pick (No. 111) for the Broncos’ 2026 first-round pick (No. 30), third-round pick (No. 94) and fourth-round pick (No. 130). After subsequent trades involving the 49ers, the transaction ultimately became Waddle and picks No. 90 and No. 111 for CB Chris Johnson, WR Chris Bell, LB Trey Moore and S Kyle Louis. The Financial Impact In May 2024, Waddle signed a three-year, $84.75 million extension that included $76 million guaranteed and kept him under contract through 2028. The Broncos absorbed the entire contract, though the Dolphins incurred a $26.3 million dead-cap charge in 2026 while receiving a $3 million cap credit in 2027. Meanwhile, Johnson, Bell, Moore and Louis are all playing on rookie deals. How Waddle Has Performed Much to the surprise of many, including one fantasy football manager (who shall remain nameless) who selected Bo Nix to lead his team, Denver’s offense has been a complete mess this season, and Waddle’s production has suffered along with it. Through five games, he has 22 receptions for 228 yards and one touchdown. A cynic might point out those are WR1 numbers for the Dolphins, but they’re almost certainly not what Denver envisioned when it acquired him. How Johnson Has Performed Chris Johnson has been every bit as good as Dolphins fans could have hoped. He has a Minkah-esque 31 tackles, two passes defended and a forced fumble. After a slow start against the Raiders and 49ers, he’s been outstanding, highlighted by an 86.9 PFF grade against Minnesota in Week 5. Teammate Jacob Rodriguez may be getting most of the Defensive Rookie of the Year buzz, but Johnson has a legitimate case of his own. How Bell Has Performed Bell was widely viewed as a first-round talent who slid because of injury concerns. The expectation was that he’d miss much of the season while recovering from ACL surgery, yet he’s already appeared in all five games. The numbers (five catches for 92 yards) aren’t eye-popping, but given the injury and his limited time working with Malik Willis, the future still looks bright. How Moore and Louis Have Performed Unfortunately, both are currently on injured reserve. Moore suffered a severe ankle injury during the preseason, while Louis sustained an MCL sprain in Week 1 against the Raiders. Louis’ practice window has opened, and expectations are that both players will return later this season. Early Verdict Even if Waddle’s disappointing production is largely a byproduct of Denver’s dysfunctional offense, this trade looks like an early win for Miami. The Dolphins shed a major financial commitment and turned the return into several intriguing young players. Chris Johnson alone is making this deal look favorable, and if Bell, Louis and Moore become meaningful contributors, the trade could have a lasting impact on the franchise’s trajectory. Of course, Waddle hasn’t suddenly forgotten how to play wide receiver, and this isn’t necessarily a win-or-lose transaction. But from Miami’s perspective, it’s hard not to like the early returns. August 2026: Quinn Ewers The Deal Dolphins traded QB Quinn Ewers for the Jaguars’ 2028 sixth-round pick. The Financial Impact Minimal. Ewers remains on his rookie contract and is not scheduled to become a free agent until 2029. How Ewers Has Performed Ewers currently serves as Trevor Lawrence’s backup in Jacksonville and, like most backup quarterbacks, hasn’t seen meaningful game action. Early Verdict If Ewers eventually develops into a legitimate NFL starter, Miami may look back on this one with some regret. For now, though, turning a seventh-round pick who didn’t appear to have a future on the roster into a future sixth-round pick qualifies as good business. So, Was It Worth It? If nothing else, these trades illustrate just how aggressive Miami has been in reshaping its roster. Established veterans, former stars, fan favorites, draft picks and future cap space have all been put on the table. Whether the Dolphins ultimately move Austin Jackson, Josh Uche, Zach Sieler or someone else before November 10, recent history suggests one thing: Nobody is untouchable if the front office believes the…

title: The Good, Bad & Ugly from the Miami Dolphins Week 7 win over the New York Jets
summary: I guess the Dolphins’ bye week came at just the right time! On Sunday, on the road against the New York Jets, the Miami Dolphins earned their first victory of the year — the first victory of head coach Jeff Hafley’s tenure with the team — by downing their AFC East rivals by a score […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 25: Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins and Caleb Douglas #7 of the Miami Dolphins look on after their win against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on October 25, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Jordan Bank/Getty Images) | Getty Images I guess the Dolphins’ bye week came at just the right time! On Sunday, on the road against the New York Jets, the Miami Dolphins earned their first victory of the year — the first victory of head coach Jeff Hafley’s tenure with the team — by downing their AFC East rivals by a score of 28-25. After a hot start allowed Miami to take a 21-7 halftime lead, the team cooled on both offense and defense in the second half, but held on by the skin of their teeth — sealing the victory with a 4th and 1 tush-push by quarterback Malik Willis with less than two minutes on the clock. No, it wasn’t a perfect game from the Dolphins, but the squad did enough to earn the hard-fought win — and maybe enough to convince a frustrated fanbase that patience is the right approach when it comes to letting Miami’s new regime build a successful organization after being forced to tear it down to the screws this past offseason. GOOD Malik Willis has best game in Dolphins uniform For the first time this season, Dolphins fans have a legitimate reason to feel encouraged about quarterback Malik Willis. Willis completed 14 of 21 passes for 208 yards and two touchdowns without having a turnover. He also added 37 rushing yards and a touchdown with his legs, giving Miami’s offense another dimension that has largely been missing this year. Not a bad afternoon for a guy who entered the game with plenty of fans questioning his ability to lead this offense. Miami scored touchdowns on their first two offensive drives, with Willis connecting with rookie receiver Caleb Douglas for a 7 yard touchdown in the first quarter before the Dolphins extended their lead with a rushing touchdown from Ollie Gordon II on the next drive. Willis then capped a 91 yard scoring drive late in the first half by scrambling into the end zone for a two yard touchdown. Miami’s lone second-half touchdown game on a short throw to Douglas who would make a man miss before taking the rock to the house for a 63 yard score. There is still plenty of work to do, and one good performance against the Jets doesn’t suddenly anoint Willis the organization’s savior at quarterback, but he deserves credit for delivering a win in this one. For a team that has spent the first several weeks looking for something to build on, Willis finally gave Miami a performance worth celebrating. BAD Dolphins pass defense has rough afternoon The Dolphins have enough problems without helping opposing offenses discover their next star receiver. Unfortunately, Miami’s pass defense apparently decided to give Jets’ rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. a helping hand on Sunday. Cooper finished the game with 5 receptions for 115 yards and a touchdown, averaging a whopping 23 yards per catch. That’s the kind of production offensive coordinators dream about from their receivers, and the kind defensive coordinators spend the week trying to prevent. Cooper wasn’t the only New York pass catcher to find success either. Tight end Mason Taylor added 5 receptions for 62 yards and two touchdowns, while their running backs contributed nine catches for 79 yards. Quarterback Geno Smith completed 23 of 30 passes for 287 yards and three touchdowns. Although Smith also threw an interception — good work, Michael Taaffe — his 77% completion rate illustrates just how comfortable New York was moving the football through the air all day long. Miami won the game, so nobody needs to spend the evening writing a eulogy for the entire secondary (fair self-burn), but allowing that kind of production against a subpar offense is concerning. If Miami wants to build on Sunday’s victory, their pass defense needs to do a much better job limiting explosive plays and preventing opposing receivers from turning routine opportunities into game-changing moments. UGLY Poor second-half nearly costs Miami game The Dolphins entered the locker room at halftime with a comfortable two touchdown lead. Then the second half happened. Miami was outscored 18-7 after halftime, allowing the Jets to turn what should have been a relatively stress-free afternoon into a 28-25 nail-biter. New York kept chipping away at the lead, and Miami struggled to maintain the offensive momentum it had established during the opening half of play. Douglas’ 63 yard touchdown reception helped Miami push its advantage to 28-17, but even that explosive play wasn’t enough to make the final minutes peaceful. The Jets continued to fight, and Miami’s inability to put the game away left the door open for a comeback. The box score tells the story of two very different halves. Miami had 231 yards of offense by halftime, but the second-half struggles — just 129 more offensive yards during the final two quarters — prevented the Dolphins from building on that production and putting the game beyond reach. The defense deserves some criticism here too. After allowing just 114 yards to the Jets’ offense in the first-half, Miami gave up 263 second-half yards to Geno Smith and company. No bueno, muchacho. We can credit the Dolphins for hanging on and getting the win. Winning a close game requires making plays when they matter, and Miami did enough to survive. But Sunday’s game was also a reminder that a two touchdown lead isn’t necessarily safe when your offense stops moving the football and your defense starts giving up explosive plays. ___ The Dolphins have plenty of reasons to celebrate their first victory of 2026. They also have plenty of film to review before next week’s game. Still, they are no longer winless on the season, and head coach Jeff Hafley can finally breathe a sigh of relief in that regard. Do you think they can continue to build momentum with a victory against the visiting New England Patriots next week? Let me know in the comments below or on Twitter at @MBrave13 . Fins up !

title: The Vikings sneak past the Colts, 16-10: By the Numbers
summary: The Minnesota Vikings did what they do best on Sunday — win by the skin of their collective teeth. It was far from pretty — though I listened to it on the radio as I drove back from my homeland and cannot attest to how it technically looked — but at the end of the […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - OCTOBER 04: Minnesota Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores looks on before the NFL game between the Miami Dolphins and the Minnesota Vikings on October 4th, 2026, at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings did what they do best on Sunday — win by the skin of their collective teeth. It was far from pretty — though I listened to it on the radio as I drove back from my homeland and cannot attest to how it technically looked — but at the end of the day, they added a tally to the W column. One of my favorite things to do is look at the game’s data and numbers afterward, find some fun trends, and explore avenues others may not have seen or focused on. So let’s give this thing a shot: 6-0 The Vikings are unbeaten through six games for the eighth time in franchise history. They’ve opened 6-0 in 2026, 2009, 2003, 2000, 1998, 1975 and 1973, and also opened the 1976 season 5-0-1. In those seven seasons, the Vikings have missed the playoffs only once — the 2003 team, which Nate Poole and the Arizona Cardinals bounced in the final game of the regular season. In the post-World War II era, only seven teams have started 6-0 and missed the playoffs: 2009 Denver Broncos 2003 Minnesota Vikings 1978 Washington (Redacted)s 1968 Los Angeles Rams 1963 Cleveland Browns 1956 Detroit Lions 1948 San Francisco 49ers Contrarily, 72 teams (of 79) have started 6-0 since 1945 and gone on to make the playoffs (91.1 percent). Alone and unbeaten The Vikings have lost zero times — and are the last team to be able to say this. Minnesota has been in sole possession of the “final unbeaten team” label five previous times in franchise history: 2016: 5-0 2000: 7-0 1976: 6-0-1 1975: 10-0 1973: 9-0 Eleven straight wins Do you remember their last loss? You can be forgiven if you’re memory-holed it, as it was the Max Brosmer-inspired 26-0 loss to the Seahawks in Seattle. As of today, that’s 330 days ago. In case you were wondering, this is the third-longest regular-season streak in Vikings history. From Dec. 1, 1974-Nov. 23, 1975, the Vikings won 13 straight regular-season games, breaking the team’s previous record of 12 straight set during the 1969 campaign (Sept. 28-Dec. 14). Thirteen remains in play, but it won’t be easy if the offense doesn’t fire it up a bit. Five straight wins — all by 10 points or fewer Since beating the Packers 39-22 in Week 1 — mind you, remember all it took to reach that final margin of victory — the last five have come by a total of 34 points. The Vikings have won five straight regular-season games by 10 points or fewer five times in franchise history, including most recently (before now, that is) from Nov. 3-Dec. 1, 2024. The franchise record is seven in a row (Sept. 25-Nov. 13, 2022) and the team also had streaks of six games from 1999-2000 and during the 1997 campaign. 16-25 (.390) Minnesota’s six wins have come against teams with a combined 16-25 record — a .390 winning percentage, the third-easiest so far, ahead of the Chiefs (.375) and Giants (.287). In case you were wondering, a .390 winning percentage comes out to roughly a 7-10 regular-season record. That also gives the Vikings a .390 average strength of victory, which is in the middle of the pack in the NFL (16th). By comparison, Chicago’s five wins have come against teams with a .424 collective winning percentage, while the Packers check in at .407 and the Lions at .357. 41-30-1 (.576) This, on the other hand, is Minnesota’s remaining strength of schedule — the toughest in the NFL. That comes out to roughly a 10-7 record on a full season. The next-toughest schedule belongs to the Bears (.563), with the Lions fourth in the NFL (.561). The Packers are tied with the Ravens for the eighth-toughest (.539), too, so don’t let anyone gaslight you into thinking the Vikings are the only team with a tough upcoming schedule in the NFC North. 200 The Vikings have won four games in which their leading passer has thrown for fewer than 200 yards: Week 1: Carson Wentz (133) Week 2: Wentz (143) Week 3: Kyler Murray (168) Week 7: Murray (150) Prior to this season, the last time the Vikings won at least four of their first six games with their leading passer throwing for under 200 yards was 1973, when they had five such wins. In franchise history, this has only happened three times before this season: 1970, 1971 and 1973. To say the game has changed since then might be a bit of an understatement. Average passing yards per game (teams): 1973 – 140.9 2026 – 221.0 12.3 The Vikings allow an average of 12.3 points per game — the top mark in the NFL by nearly 5.0 points per game (Kansas City is second at 17.2). Unless you’re older than 50, you’ve never seen a better scoring defense through six games in a Vikings season: 1970 – 6.5 PPG 1971 – 8.2 PPG 1976 – 10.0 PPG 1969 – 10.8 PPG 2026 – 12.3 PPG 0 The Vikings had zero giveaways on Sunday — the third time they’d done so this season. They’ve won six straight games when committing zero turnovers, dating back to a 31-9 loss to the Lions on Jan. 5, 2025. Under head coach Kevin O’Connell, the Vikings are 15-2 (.882) when they don’t turn over the football (since 2022). 155.0 The Vikings are allowing just 155.0 passing yards per game this season. The last time they allowed fewer? How about 1977, when they allowed just 112.9. This season’s mark would be the 11th-best in franchise history, but all 10 previous seasons were at least 49 years ago. 3 The Vikings have allowed just three points in the fourth quarter this season. The next lowest is the Dolphins with 27. Last season, the Saints led the NFL by allowing just 58 fourth-quarter points — an average of 3.4 per game. The Vikings are currently allowing an average of 0.5 points per game in the fourth quarter. While this pace is pretty much impossible to maintain, they could still challenge the mark for fewest fourth-quarter points allowed in the era of 16-plus-game seasons. The 1996 Carolina Panthers and 2003 Detroit Lions both set the mark with just 33 fourth-quarter points allowed, while the vaunted 2002 Tampa Bay Buccaneers allowed 41 and the 1993 Bills and 2000 Ravens allowed 42. That comes to between 2.1 and 2.6 points per game — still more than four times what the Vikings have done so far.

summary: The Minnesota Vikings defense shut down the Colts offense on Sunday, leading to a 16-10 victory. We saw the first unsuccessful field goal of the year for the Vikings, so at least that’s out of the way. The offense continues to sputter, but the defense is looking like world beaters. The game was perfectly sealed […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 25: T.J. Hockenson #87 of the Minnesota Vikings scores a receiving touchdown against the Indianapolis Colts during the fourth quarter of the game at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings defense shut down the Colts offense on Sunday, leading to a 16-10 victory. We saw the first unsuccessful field goal of the year for the Vikings, so at least that’s out of the way. The offense continues to sputter, but the defense is looking like world beaters. The game was perfectly sealed by future Hall of Famer Harrison Smith’s interception. Blake Cashman Cashman was everywhere on Sunday. It seemed he was in the backfield and somehow in the secondary at the same time. Nearly intercepted passes that resulted in series ending incompletions, a sack to end the 2nd quarter drive and take away the Colts’ final attempt at the end zone, and another sack to start the 2nd half off right. Harrison Smith Smith recorded his 40th career interception on Sunday. He’s just the 4th player to achieve 40 career interceptions and 20 career sacks. Hall of Famers Larry Wilson, Charles Woodson, and Ronde Barber are the other three. Smith baited Jones into a throw, during the Colts’ final attempted drive. Smith was also credited with 1/2 a sack on a play he and Dallas Turner went unblocked off the edge and took down Daniel Jones. Overall, it’s another win and another reminder that Harrison Smith still knows exactly where the football is going. Will Reichard I am putting this man up there because I saw how bad kicking is around the league. Reichard had his first recorded miss of the year on a blocked 59-yard attempt in the 4th quarter. He was 4/4 on other kicks and excellent on kick-off duty. Better blocking and he’d probably still be perfect on the year. Dallas Turner Turner was in the backfield all day. He only got 1/2 the sack with Harrison Smith, but was clearly there first. Turner spent the afternoon making sure Daniel Jones never got comfortable in the pocket. Turner has stepped into Jonathan Greenard’s role without missing a beat this season.

The Vikings defeated the Colts 16-10. Skol! Join Vikings fans on the SB Nation app! Experience every game with fans who understand the excitement—and the stress—of Vikings football. Chat live throughout the game Enjoy fewer ads Jump easily between communities Comment and post faster Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Our friends at the FanDuel Sportsbook have opened the betting lines for Week 8 in the National Football League, and the Vikings are currently a 3-point underdog as they head into their NFC North matchup with the Detroit Lions at Ford Field. The over/under for this one currently rests at 46.5 points. On Sunday, the Vikings once again struggled on offense against a team that they probably shouldn’t have struggled against on offense, as they managed to get into the end zone just one time against the Indianapolis Colts. Thanks to another stellar performance by the defense, however, that was enough, as they managed to hold on for a 16-10 victory to push their record to 6-0. With the San Francisco 49ers losing to the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday afternoon and the Kansas City Chiefs falling to the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday Night Football, the Vikings are now the only team in the league that still has a donut in the loss column. Week 7 in Detroit saw a game of “You take it. . .no, you take it” between the Lions and another NFC North rival of ours, the Green Bay Packers. The game featured bad interceptions on both sides and the standard dumb Dan Campbell fourth-down decision, going for it on 4th-and-1 from his own 24-yard line in a 17-17 game with five minutes remaining. That failed fourth down was immediately followed by Green Bay kicker Trey Smack having a 35-yard field goal attempt blocked to preserve the tie. The Lions then pushed the ball down the field far enough for Jake Bates to kick the game-winning field goal and help the Lions escape with a 20-17 win. The Vikings will be looking for their third straight win over the Lions. . .and, apparently, their third straight win as an underdog. . .after sweeping the season series last year. They defeated the Lions in Detroit last year behind three J.J. McCarthy touchdowns in a 27-24 nail-biter, and effectively ended the Lions’ season at U.S. Bank Stadium on Christmas Day, forcing six Detroit turnovers in a 23-10 triumph. Do you think that the Vikings should be underdogs heading into this one, folks? Let us know what you think!

title: Patriots injury analysis after Bears loss in Week 7
summary: The New England Patriots dropped to 4-3 on the year and out of the current AFC playoff picture with their loss to the Chicago Bears on Thursday night. However, not all was bad: the injury-ravaged team received a much-needed reprieve. In fact, there were only two noticeable injuries after rewatching the contest. Patriots injury analysis: […]
full_text: The New England Patriots dropped to 4-3 on the year and out of the current AFC playoff picture with their loss to the Chicago Bears on Thursday night. However, not all was bad: the injury-ravaged team received a much-needed reprieve. In fact, there were only two noticeable injuries after rewatching the contest. Patriots injury analysis: NFL Week 7 S Kevin Byard III: Early in the second quarter, the veteran safety had to be checked out by trainers on the field due to an apparent left shoulder injury. He subsequently jogged off the field under his own power and into the blue medical tent, but reemerged after a brief evaluation. Byard ended up missing just four snaps before his return. He ended the game with a 94% playing time share , not missing any other reps down the stretch. DT Christian Barmore: Barmore made what could have been one of the biggest plays of the game in the late fourth quarter, sacking Caleb Williams for a 10-yard loss. Unfortunately, the play did not end up mattering — kicker Cairo Santos kicked a career-long field goal to effectively ice the game — while the sixth-year defensive tackle remained on the ground afterwards: he had landed awkwardly on his right hand and required medical assistance. Barmore walked off the field and with the Patriots playing no more defensive snaps did not get an opportunity to reenter the game. What this means for the Patriots While the injuries to both Kevin Byard and Christian Barmore could have been potentially concerning, it appears neither will be a long-term issue. Byard returned to the game, while head coach Mike Vrabel said about Barmore on Monday that “he’ll be fine.” Him and Barmore both being present at practice on Monday is concrete proof of that. For the Patriots, especially considering that they were on a short week, this is definitive good news. The team, after all, had at least lost some starters or key reserves to injury in almost every game this season so far. Now heading into a Week 8 contest against the Miami Dolphins off a mini-bye, they seemingly are trending in the right direction again. No major injuries were added on Thursday, while the team is getting healthier — as evidenced by the fact that guard Ben Brown (knee) also was back on the practice fields on Monday. The first injury report of the week will be published on Wednesday afternoon, and give more information about the current state of the team. Kickoff between the Patriots and Dolphins at Miami’s Hard Rock Stadium is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET on Sunday.

title: Patriots playoff picture after losing to the Bears in Week 7
summary: Their 30-24 loss to the Chicago Bears last Thursday put an end to the New England Patriots’ three-game winning streak, and also impacts their standing in the AFC playoff picture. Entering Week 7 as the fifth seed in the conference, they woke up on Friday morning out of the playoff picture and having dropped all […]
full_text: Their 30-24 loss to the Chicago Bears last Thursday put an end to the New England Patriots’ three-game winning streak, and also impacts their standing in the AFC playoff picture. Entering Week 7 as the fifth seed in the conference, they woke up on Friday morning out of the playoff picture and having dropped all the way to No. 9. Of course, a majority of Week 7 was still left to be played at that point. With those games now all in the books, let’s update the standings. AFC East standings Buffalo Bills (5-1) New England Patriots (4-2) New York Jets (2-5) Miami Dolphins (1-5) The Patriots remain in second place in their division even after losing to the Bears, and would have stayed put regardless of what the weekend slate would have brought. The Bills, after all, were on a bye, meaning New England would not have overtaken them even in case of a win. That said, what was a one-game deficit entering Thursday is now a 1.5-game gap that needs to be overcome. Elsewhere in the division, the Dolphins celebrated their first win of the year. After looking like arguably the worst team in the NFL, they beat the Jets 28-25 on the road to improve to 1-5 on the year — a likely morale boost heading into this week’s home game with the Patriots. The Jets, meanwhile, are now 0-2 in the division and in real danger of their season slipping away already. AFC playoff standings Kansas City Chiefs (5-1) Buffalo Bills (5-1) Cleveland Browns (5-2) Jacksonville Jaguars (4-2) Denver Broncos (5-2) Pittsburgh Steelers (5-2) Cincinnati Bengals (4-2) On the bubble: 8. New England Patriots (4-3) , 9. Baltimore Ravens (4-3), 10. Las Vegas Raiders (3-4), 11. New York Jets (2-5), 12. Indianapolis Colts (2-5), 13. Houston Texans (2- 5) Not yet eliminated, but let’s be real here: 14. Miami Dolphins (1-5), 15. Tennessee Titans (1-6), 16. Los Angeles Chargers (0-6) As noted above, the Patriots found themselves in the ninth seed coming out of Thursday’s game. However, the Bengals and Ravens playing each other on Sunday meant that at least one of those teams would drop below New England when all was said and done. It was the Ravens, who lost 35-13 despite taking a 13-0 lead into the locker room at halftime. That one game was not enough to catapult the Patriots back into the top seven, though, because both the Broncos and Steelers ended up winning their contests; the former won 30-16 in Arizona, and the latter 16-10 against the Saints in Paris. Both have a worse conference record than New England at the moment — with the Patriots also holding the head-to-head advantage over Pittsburgh — but remain ahead in the standings. At the top of the conference, the Chiefs suffered their first defeat of the season. Patrick Mahomes and company were unable to play competent offensive football against the Seahawks on Sunday night, losing 20-3.

title: Why did the Patriots release Bryce Baringer? Mike Vrabel explains.
summary: The New England Patriots opted to part ways with their punter of the last three seasons, Bryce Baringer, on Monday. The 2023 sixth-round draft pick was released off of injured reserve. Why did the team make the move, though, that officially hands the keys to the position over to injury replacement Mitch Wishnowsky? For Patriots […]
full_text: The New England Patriots opted to part ways with their punter of the last three seasons, Bryce Baringer, on Monday. The 2023 sixth-round draft pick was released off of injured reserve . Why did the team make the move, though, that officially hands the keys to the position over to injury replacement Mitch Wishnowsky? For Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel, it was a combination of factors. “It’s just give him an opportunity to go kick and have an opportunity to go work out. There’s a lot of things that he’ll be able to do now not being on IR,” Vrabel explained on Monday. “We just felt like this was best for us, best for Bryce, and to give him an opportunity to go punt and see if somebody needs a punter. If we would need him back and he was there, then we would want to have him back. You just make a decision with a specialist, and as long as it’s going well, which I think it is, and everybody else does, you just stick with it.” After appearing in a combined 55 regular season and playoff games between 2023 and 2025, Baringer entered this year’s training camp as the only punter on the Patriots’ roster. He remained so until suffering an injury in the second preseason game (one that prompted rookie quarterback Behren Morton to assume punting duties). Matt Haack was the first player brought in to replace Baringer, but he was let go again at the roster cutdown deadline. With Baringer them moving to IR, Wishnowsky was added first to the practice squad and then the active roster. With him performing well, Baringer apparently became expendable. “I certainly appreciate what Bryce has been able to do for us,” said Vrabel. “Those are tough decisions. I don’t think those are things that you’d necessarily take lightly.” Even though the door on a return does not appear to be closed, the Patriots have made it clear that — at least for the remainder of 2026 — Wishnowsky is their man at the punter position. “Mitch, he’s punted a lot of games in the National Football League. He’s punted, could flip the field,” Vrabel said about the 34-year-old. “I think that he gets it off quickly. I think the plus-50s have improved. He’s got different punts and different kicks that he uses, and I think he’s been pretty consistent. I think the hang time’s been pretty good.”

title: Patriots re-sign edge rusher Jose Ramirez to practice squad, release offensive lineman
summary: After two weeks away, Jose Ramirez has reclaimed a locker at Gillette Stadium. The New England Patriots officially re-signed the outside linebacker to the practice squad on Monday and released offensive lineman Jacob Rizy to make room among the 17-man group. ESPN’s Mike Reiss and Patriots on SI’s Ethan Hurwitz were first to report the […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - AUGUST 04: Philadelphia Eagles linebacker Jose Ramirez #43 runs a drill during the Philadelphia Eagles training camp on August 4th, 2026 at Jefferson Health Training Center in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images After two weeks away, Jose Ramirez has reclaimed a locker at Gillette Stadium. The New England Patriots officially re-signed the outside linebacker to the practice squad on Monday and released offensive lineman Jacob Rizy to make room among the 17-man group. ESPN’s Mike Reiss and Patriots on SI’s Ethan Hurwitz were first to report the moves heading out of the mini bye. Ramirez, 27, originally landed in head coach Mike Vrabel’s fold after being waived by the Philadelphia Eagles at the NFL’s 53-man roster deadline in August. The 6-foot-2, 252-pound preseason visitor to Foxborough earned a promotion in late September. He checked into two games while on the active roster and recorded one tackle across 30 snaps between defense and special teams. Upon clearing waivers , a return to the practice squad followed in October. So did the edge rusher’s release ahead of what became a 26-19 AFC East win over the New York Jets. Selected in the sixth round of the 2023 draft class at No. 196 overall, Ramirez appeared in four games and notched one quarterback hit while a member of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The former MAC Defensive Player of the Year by way of Arizona, Riverside City College and Eastern Michigan went on to spend part of 2025 with the Hamilton Tiger-Cats and recorded four tackles to go with one sack in three games. He circled back from the CFL to the NFL on a futures contract in January. Rizy, 24, had been brought back on New England’s practice squad after injuries depleted the interior line ahead of last week’s 30-24 loss to the Chicago Bears. The 6-foot-5, 306-pound rookie first joined the scout team at its formation and was released midway through September. Signed by the Patriots as part of the organization’s undrafted class of 2026, Rizy played 155 offensive snaps at center through three preseason games before being waived leading up to the NFL’s cutdown deadline. A former second-team and first-team All-Ivy League selection, Rizy spent three years at Harvard and two years at Florida State. He made 27 starts over that span while logging work at center, left guard, right guard and right tackle. A spot remains open on the 53-man roster as a divisional matchup nears. The Miami Dolphins host next Sunday’s 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff at Hard Rock Stadium.

title: What releasing Bryce Baringer means for the Patriots
summary: Coming out of their mini-bye, the New England Patriots have decided to part ways with one of their longest-tenured players. Bryce Baringer, who had been with the organization since his arrival as a sixth-round draft pick in 2023, has been released off the team’s injured reserve list. Let’s assess what the move means for the […]
full_text: Coming out of their mini-bye, the New England Patriots have decided to part ways with one of their longest-tenured players. Bryce Baringer, who had been with the organization since his arrival as a sixth-round draft pick in 2023, has been released off the team’s injured reserve list . Let’s assess what the move means for the Patriots from a big-picture perspective. Official changing of the guard Since arriving in New England, Baringer survived two head coaching changes and appeared in all 55 possible regular season and playoff games. He did have the occasional ups and downs, but on the whole was generally reliable in his capacity as a punter and holder. That said, his long-term outlook entering the final year of his rookie contract was in question; despite being a solid player, he hadn’t yet proven himself worthy of an extension or staying put beyond 2026. Apparently, the Patriots agreed with this assessment, and the injury he suffered in preseason in combination with Mitch Wishnowsky doing a decent job as a replacement, sealed his fate. The punter baton is therefore now officially being handed from Baringer to Wishnowsky. At least for the remainder of the 2026 season, the 34-year-old will be holding down the fort. So far, he has done so on 22 punts that he sent an average of 47.1 yards with a net of 41.2. He also tried one onside kick last week against Chicago, but that was recovered by the Bears. That said, at age 34 it would not be a surprise if Wishnowsky also was not a long-term option and the Patriots decided to bring in competition and a possible successor during next year’s draft. New(ish)-look operation As noted above, Baringer also served as the Patriots’ holder on field goals and extra points. As such, he played an integral role in the kicking game operation particularly when working with two rookies — kicker Andy Borregales and long snapper Julian Ashby — last season. “You look at the operation on the field goal, being able to calm everything down, be able to handle the snap and just the good placement, ball placement for Andy,” Vrabel said in 2025. “Bryce really kind of helps out in all regards in special teams, and he’s done a nice job, whether that’s helping on kickoff return or kickoff or just helping at practice.” That element of his presence on the roster is now gone, and like the rest of his contributions replaced by Wishnowsky. Of course, Borregales and Ashby being second-year players with some experience under their belts now helps with that transition as well. IR-return candidate gone NFL teams have the ability to return up to eight players from injured reserve during the regular season. The Patriots have so far used the designation two times, on offensive tackle Marcus Bryant and wide receiver A.J. Brown. This left them with six available spots for players to come back from IR, but too many candidates to realistically get brought back onto the 53-man team. With Baringer out of the equation, the final six spots will come down to fullback Reggie Gilliam, wide receivers Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs, offensive linemen Alijah Vera-Tucker, Greg Van Roten and, to a less-realistic degree, Mike Onwenu, linebackers Quintayvious Hutchins and Khalil Jacobs, and safety Dell Pettus. Belichick ties keep disappearing Baringer joined the Patriots as part of the final draft class under long-time head coach/de facto general manager Bill Belichick. With him now gone, so is another tie to the Belichick regime. As a consequence, only 10 players brought in before 2024 remain with the team (year of arrival in parentheses): RB Rhamondre Stevenson (2021) WR DeMario Douglas (2023) TE Hunter Henry (2021) RG Mike Onwenu (2020) DT Christian Barmore (2021) DT Jeremiah Pharms Jr. (2022) LB Christian Elliss (2023) CB Christian Gonzalez (2023) CB Marcus Jones (2022) S Brenden Schooler (2022) What this list of names shows is that the group may be lacking in quantity but not quality: it includes some of the Patriots’ best and most important players.

title: Patriots release punter Bryce Baringer

full_text: The New England Patriots are officially making a change at the punter position. Bryce Baringer, who had played the role since his arrival in 2023 but most recently found himself on injured reserve, is being released by the team. NFL insider Jordan Schultz was first to report the move. Baringer, 27, originally joined the Patriots as a sixth-round selection in the 2023 draft. The Michigan State product went on to appear in all 55 possible regular season and playoff games over his first three years with the club, serving a dual role as punter as well as holder on field goal and extra point tries. In total, Baringer punted the ball 247 times for an average of 47.1 yards per kick. Subtracting opponents’ returns, his net punting average stands at 40.6 yards a punt. Baringer entered the 2026 season as the featured option at the position, but he suffered an undisclosed injury in the second preseason game. The move eventually prompted the Patriots to sign veteran free agent Mitch Wishnowsky and place the incumbent on injured reserve. Now healthy again, Baringer will not be activated to the active roster but instead let go by the team. Wishnowsky has played all seven of New England’s games so far this season. He has punted 22 times for an average of 47.1 yards with a net of 41.2. The 4-3 Patriots will travel to Miami this week to take on the 1-5 Dolphins.

title: TreVeyon Henderson still enjoys Patriots’ trust despite quiet season so far
summary: There were moments during his 2025 rookie season that TreVeyon Henderson looked like a superstar in the making and potential future difference maker for the New England Patriots offense. Seven weeks into his sophomore campaign, that future has not yet arrived. In fact, the opposite has been the case. Henderson has been largely quiet and […]
full_text: There were moments during his 2025 rookie season that TreVeyon Henderson looked like a superstar in the making and potential future difference maker for the New England Patriots offense. Seven weeks into his sophomore campaign, that future has not yet arrived. In fact, the opposite has been the case. Henderson has been largely quiet and is trailing his rookie production so far. However, he still enjoys the Patriots’ full support as head coach Mike Vrabel confirmed after the young running back played only 13 of 54 snaps during last Thursday’s loss to the Chicago Bears. “We had some things for him, packages or personnel groupings,” Vrabel said. “TreVeyon will help us, but I wanted to see where we were with Corey [Kiner] getting a couple carries too.” Henderson’s limited usage against the Bears appears to be the result of two factors: third running back Corey Kiner coming off a solid performance four days earlier versus the New York Jets, and the 24-year-old himself being just 11 days removed from suffering a reported high ankle sprain. In general, Henderson has been limited by injuries for much of 2026 so far. Besides his recent sprained ankle, he also suffered an ankle injury in late August that forced him out multiple weeks into the regular season. Since his return in Week 2 against Pittsburgh — a game that saw him score a 39-yard touchdown reminiscent of his 2025 form — he has touched the ball 57 total times for 248 scrimmage yards and that one score. Those numbers put him on track for around 700 yards and three touchdowns this season, a far cry from the 1,132 and 10 TDs he had last year. Obviously, the circumstances do not work in his favor so far; besides his own injury woes, RB1 Rhamondre Stevenson has been reliable both in terms of availability and production. That said, Henderson himself is also still dealing with some of the same issues that plagued him as a first-year pro: his vision remains underdeveloped and his pass protection a work in progress. Even so, his head coach is confident that the Patriots will find a way to get him involved at a higher rate. “TreVeyon will help us plenty here down the stretch and helped us a little bit tonight,” Vrabel said on Thursday. With the Patriots entering their upcoming game against the Dolphins off a mini-bye, and the extra rest it brings, Henderson might get his chance to help the team as early as Week 8.

title: Recap: Saints play Steelers in inaugural Paris matchup
summary: In the first-ever NFL regular-season matchup on French soil, the New Orleans Saints were hoping to make it back-to-back wins for the first time this year as they faced off against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Here’s a recap of everything that went down at the Stade de France. First Quarter The Steelers got the opening drive […]
full_text: PARIS, FRANCE - OCTOBER 25: Devaughn Vele of the New Orleans Saints run with the ball under pressure from Jaquan Brisker of the Pittsburgh Steelers during the NFL game between Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints at Stade de France on October 25, 2026 in Paris, France. (Photo by Franco Arland/Getty Images) | Getty Images In the first-ever NFL regular-season matchup on French soil, the New Orleans Saints were hoping to make it back-to-back wins for the first time this year as they faced off against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Here’s a recap of everything that went down at the Stade de France. First Quarter The Steelers got the opening drive off to a fast start as Jaylen Warren broke into Saints territory with a 29-yard run. After four more runs, two each from Warren and Rico Dowdle, Aaron Rodgers was incomplete with a pass intended for DK Metcalf on third down. Chris Boswell’s 28-yard chip shot gave Pittsburgh a 3-0 lead. The Saints responded well to begin their opening series, as Tyler Shough found Bryce Lance and Chris Olave for medium gains before converting a third down with a 14-yard pass to Devaughn Vele. But after a run for no gain from Alvin Kamara and a pair of incompletions, the black and gold had to punt. Starting at his own 4-yard line, Rodgers worked his way near midfield with a variety of short throws alongside runs from Warren. Second Quarter After a pair of incompletions, Pittsburgh had to punt. Shough began the ensuing possession with a huge chunk gain, connecting with Barion Brown for a 49-yard pass. Soon after, he found Kendre Miller for 13 more, but was then forced into a 3rd-and-long after taking a sack. Daniel Carlson converted from 38 yards to tie the game. Warren continued to hurt the Saints on the next series, with a 26-yard catch-and-run to begin the drive. A few plays later, on 3rd-and-14, Rodgers found Metcalf for 51 yards to give Pittsburgh 1st-and-goal. Darnell Washington made the catch in the end zone to put the Steelers up 10-3. New Orleans faced 4th down straight away as they looked for a response, which Shough converted on an 11-yard throw to Olave. He then found Vele and Lance before converting another third down with a 13-yard pass to Kamara, who nearly found the end zone. A couple of plays later, on 4th-and-goal, Vele caught the 1-yard touchdown pass to tie the game at 10-10. Rodgers then got to work in the two-minute drill, setting up a 47-yard kick from Boswell to give Pittsburgh a 13-10 halftime lead. Third Quarter New Orleans embarked on a mammoth drive to begin the second half, highlighted by a 24-yard connection from Shough to Vele on a 3rd-and-long. But on the edge of the red zone, Shough’s pass intended for Olave was intercepted by Payton Wilson. Rodgers responded with a long drive of his own, as Pittsburgh moved into Saints territory with Warren continuing to run at will. Brandon Smith caught a 20-yard pass to put the ball in the red zone, but the first sack of the afternoon for the black and gold came at a good time as Chase Young and Carl Granderson were able to force Pittsburgh into a field goal attempt. Boswell was good again from 39 yards. Fourth Quarter Trailing 16-10, New Orleans put together an 11-play, 47-yard drive on which Shough was 7-for-7. But penalties hampered their efforts, and Carlson was soon out to attempt another field goal. He was no good from 52 yards. Pittsburgh proceeded to go three-and-out as Young got to Rodgers again. But the Saints only found one first down on the ensuing series before punting themselves. From there, the Steelers ran down the clock to great effect, with Rodgers scrambling on a 3rd down for the decisive yardage. Boswell came out to convert a 39-yard kick to ice the game, but an offside penalty against the black and gold meant Pittsburgh could kneel out the clock instead to secure a 16-10 victory. The Saints return home after the bye week to play the Cleveland Browns on November 8.
