title: Saquon Barkley’s hamstring is still an issue, but the Eagles needed him
summary: The Eagles offense was finally able to move the ball early on Monday night against the Cowboys, and even managed to score a touchdown on their first offensive drive. A big reason for this success was thanks to Saquon Barkley being back on the field after missing several games due to a hamstring injury. Barkley […]
full_text: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images | Getty Images The Eagles offense was finally able to move the ball early on Monday night against the Cowboys, and even managed to score a touchdown on their first offensive drive. A big reason for this success was thanks to Saquon Barkley being back on the field after missing several games due to a hamstring injury. Barkley admitted before the game that he would have to see how he feels early on, and explained that he wanted to be smart about his return. The RB was tested quickly, during his second carry, when a Cowboys defender missed the tackle, but was able to pull Barkley’s leg during the attempted takedown. He was noticeably hesitant following the play, limping a little, but was able to stay on the field and finish the drive — which ended with the running back carrying the ball into the endzone for the first TD of the game. WELCOME BACK, 26 pic.twitter.com/hrkFoZNlNT — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) October 27, 2026 He went straight for the stationary bike when he left the field, and was seen talking to trainers, stretching, and sitting on the bench. At one point, as Barkley peddled on the bike, he pointed to his head in what looked like a message to someone that he was being smart about things. His impact was immediate, and the decimation of the running back room certainly affected Barkley returning for this Monday night game. While he lined up for several snaps after that first offensive drive, Dameon Pierce started taking more of the workload through the rest of the first half. Barkley was in for the first offensive play coming out of halftime and had a nice 12-yard run, but after the play, he once again made his way back to the sideline. The broadcast captured his grimace up close as he unclipped his chinstrap, and the RB was clearly playing through some discomfort. Through three quarters, he was on the field for 10 snaps and carried the ball each of those times. Early in the fourth quarter, the Eagles listed Barkley as questionable to return with a back injury, essentially ending his game with 62 rushing yards. Based on his pre-game comments, and how soon his hot hand was passed on, the Eagles were actively managing Barkley’s pitch count against the Cowboys. Hopefully he didn’t re-aggravate his hamstring injury during his limited time on the field, and is able to continue to build strength back on his way toward a full workload.

title: Eagles roster news: 6 moves announced
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced six roster moves ahead of the team’s Week 7 Monday night game against the Dallas Cowboys. Here’s an overview: Note: teams are permitted to temporarily elevate up to two practice squad players per game. A player can be elevated up to three times in the regular season and an unlimited […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 22: Eli Stowers #87 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on prior to an NFL preseason football game against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced six roster moves ahead of the team’s Week 7 Monday night game against the Dallas Cowboys. Here’s an overview: OG Landon Dickerson, TE Grant Calcaterra, and TE Eli Stowers were activated from injured reserve to the roster. EDGE Keyshawn James-Newby and RB Elijah Mitchell were temporarily elevated from the practice squad. CB Jakorian Bennett was ruled out for the game. Note: teams are permitted to temporarily elevate up to two practice squad players per game . A player can be elevated up to three times in the regular season and an unlimited number of times in the postseason. Let’s sort through this news on a player-by-player basis. LANDON DICKERSON Dickerson is returning to the starting lineup for the first time since mightily struggling in Week 1. The Eagles are hoping that Dickerson’s time on injured reserve allowed him to get healthy. But there’s real reason to wonder if the three-time Pro Bowler might just not be nearly as good as he was in the past due to injuries taking a toll on him. Will be interesting to see how he fares on Monday night and moving forward. GRANT CALCATERRA The Eagles needed more tight end depth since Dallas Goedert (who is playing despite being on the injury report) and Johnny Mundt are the only players at their position on the roster. Can’t imagine fans are excited to see Calcaterra back, though. He can help on special teams but we all know his blocking is bad. ELI STOWERS Stowers is set to make his NFL debut after the Eagles placed their rookie tight end on injured reserve ahead of Week 1. Stowers failed to impress during the offseason and it’s unclear how much he’s equipped to even help out on special teams, where he played just six snaps in five years of college football. It’s not exactly like the Eagles are loaded with great tight end options, though, so maybe he’ll get some chances. KEYSHAWN JAMES-NEWBY The Eagles needed more edge rusher depth with Jalyx Hunt and Jonathan Greenard questionable to suit up. ELIJAH MITCHELL The Eagles were in need of more running back depth. JAKORIAN BENNETT Bennett is still on IR. NON-MOVE The Eagles maxed out Ertz’s three temporary practice squad elevations from Week 3 through Week 5. He was ineligible to play in Week 6 while remaining on the practice squad. The team did not put him on the roster for Week 7.

title: Eagles-Cowboys Week 7 prediction

full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 4: Zack Baun #53 of the Philadelphia Eagles tackles Miles Sanders #27 of the Dallas Cowboys during the first quarter of an NFL game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lincoln Financial Field on September 4, 2025 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. Admittedly, I can’t say the Eagles winning tonight is the most logical prediction. The Birds are really bad and really banged up. But it’s not like the Cowboys are all that. Dallas has the worst defense in the NFL. Their offense is in a rut they haven’t experienced with Dak Prescott starting since the 2019 season. Even some homer Cowboys fans are taking the Eagles to win this game. I expect the players to put forth a good effort on the night of Jeffrey Lurie’s induction into the Eagles Hall of Fame. I would think this enshrinement has not been glossed over in the team’s internal messaging. I can understand why some might feel like the Eagles winning is impossible. But even the league’s worst team typically win some games each year. And the NFL is weird and unpredictable. Maybe the Eagles pull off the upset today. No one will be surprised if they don’t. And even if they do, it won’t necessarily be an indication that the season is saved. But even if the joy of a win is short-lived, it’ll be a nice reprieve from an otherwise hellish season. title: Eagles-Cowboys Game Preview: 5 questions and answers with the Week 7 enemy
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are in primetime once again as they host the Dallas Cowboys at Lincoln Financial Field on Monday night. The Birds will be looking to break a four-game losing streak to help keep their season alive. In order to preview this Week 7 NFC East battle, I reached out to our enemies over […]
full_text: Jul 29, 2026; Oxnard, CA, USA; Dallas Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker at training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Philadelphia Eagles are in primetime once again as they host the Dallas Cowboys at Lincoln Financial Field on Monday night. The Birds will be looking to break a four-game losing streak to help keep their season alive. In order to preview this Week 7 NFC East battle, I reached out to our enemies over at Blogging The Boys . The deft Dave Halprin kindly took the time to answer my questions about this upcoming battle. Let’s take a look at the answers. 1 – The Cowboys are 2-4 and Brian Schottenheimer seems to be in the crosshairs. To what extent deserve does he deserve blame for this team’s struggles? He has to take a lot of the blame this year, and not just because as a head coach you have to take the blame when your team is stumbling. It’s not like he was handed a roster devoid of talent. Maybe some of it was overrated, but there are legitimate stars on the roster. Additionally, his play-calling and in-game management decisions have been puzzling at times, and that is a kind way of describing it. A lot of this concerns the offense, but he also kept a special teams coach from last year who was very poor in 2025. Most expected he would be let go in the offseason, but Schottenheimer kept him and it has definitely hurt us more than helped. In his own defense, during his time in Dallas Schottenheimer has been saddled by a really poor defense, something we’ll discuss a little later. But the offense seems to be regressing, that’s his side of the ball, and this is largely with the same personnel that was an elite offense in 2025. This has all been surprising as the Cowboys fanbase and punditry felt like Schotty did a fairly good job in 2025, and it seemed to be a very positive offseason. So this poor start was not what was envisioned. 2 – Christian Parker is off to a rough start. Is there any confidence he’ll rebound? Especially now that Mike Pettine is here? Beyond coaching, how much is personnel an issue? I think it is way too early to decide anything about Christian Parker. Unlike Schottenheimer, he was handed a defense that has had very little success recently and not much star power. He is patching things together with players who may not all fit his scheme. He has also been hit incredibly hard with injuries, especially in the secondary. So the hope is Parker is fighting some strong headwinds because the product currently on the field has been the problem for most of the season. The Cowboys suffer from two problems, and when you mix them together they are lethal. First is they can’t rush the passer. Second is they have trouble covering receivers. You can probably work out the problem from that. Their edge players have moments when they create pressure, but actually hitting and sacking the QB is not their specialty at the moment. It feels like they will have to blitz more to make things happen in that department. The secondary has been wiped out by injury, and they are having coverage breakdowns regularly. So blitzing that doesn’t get home leaves a vulnerable secondary even more vulnerable. There have been moments when you can see Parker’s vision. The second half of the Packers game was one of those moments, and there have been other stretches too. I think you have to give him at least the whole season until you can really start making an informed decision about what he’s trying to do. 3 – The Dallas defense hasn’t been good but it’s not like the offense has played well over the past two weeks, either. What’s the problem there? There are plenty of theories about what is going wrong with the offense. The big overarching thing that is happening is that both the Bucs and the Packers decided to blitz Dallas a lot and trust their corners to cover. Previously, this was a foolish decision because Dak Prescott was statistically one of the best QBs versus the blitz. The Cowboys used to pray teams would blitz them. Suddenly, the blitz is working. Prescott has two bad games in a row. Some say it is Schottenheimer’s route concepts and play-calling. Some say the offensive line is doing a poor job of identifying the blitzers. Some say the lack of commitment to the run game is putting Prescott into too much danger. I would say that it is a mix of all that going on. But it is incumbent on Schottenheimer to get that fixed. He calls the plays and the offense is his specialty. 4 – What’s the biggest matchup in the Cowboys’ favor and the biggest matchup against their favor ? Right now, the Cowboys best weapon is the combo of Dak Prescott and wide receivers CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. On paper at least. Even that has not been smooth throughout the season and has really suffered in the last few weeks. Now, lots of fans would tell you that the Cowboys should commit more to their running game with an offensive line that is built to run in the middle. That was very effective last year, but we’ve yet to see it take hold this year. The Cowboys biggest disadvantage is their coverage in the secondary, especially when it comes to third down. They are just terrible, teams are converting 3rd-and-longs against us at an embarrassing rate. And don’t think that young, unknown quarterbacks can’t get it done either because Jalon Daniels for the Bucs did it. 5 – Who wins this game and why? With the Cowboys currently listed as 4.5-point road favorites, what’s your score prediction? I’m going to say Dallas is going to win it, but with absolutely no conviction behind that. It’s more because I don’t want the season to be over this early and going to 2-5 on the year feels like the end. The slight improvement in the defense in the second half last week gives me hope that Mike Pettine is starting to help. And you guys are certainly going through your own amount of turmoil. Let’s say: Cowboys 27 – Eagles 23.

title: Steelers Week 7 grades in win over Saints
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers are 5-2 after a 16-10 win over the New Orleans Saints in Paris. As always, Joey Bray and I are here to give your weekly grades, so let’s get into it. QB Aaron Rodgers Jarrett Bailey: Rodgers continues to be efficient while adding a pinch of explosiveness that lifts the Steelers’ offense. […]
full_text: (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers are 5-2 after a 16-10 win over the New Orleans Saints in Paris. As always, Joey Bray and I are here to give your weekly grades, so let’s get into it. QB Aaron Rodgers Jarrett Bailey: Rodgers continues to be efficient while adding a pinch of explosiveness that lifts the Steelers’ offense. His best play of the day came on a 3rd-and-14 where he escaped pressure from the pocket, ran to his left, and uncorked a moon ball to DK Metcalf, who hauled it in for a gain of 51 inside the five yard-line. Plus, the eight-yard scramble to end the game was as clutch as it comes from a quarterback who has spent six presidential terms making clutch plays. It wasn’t an extraordinary performance, but it was a good overall showing from Rodgers. Grade: B+ Joey Bray : It wasn’t Rodgers’ most impressive stat line this season, but his 30 passing attempts were the fewest of the season. The Steelers controlled the clock with their running game and felt in control the entire time. Rodgers maneuvered the pocket better this game than he has all season, highlighted by an 8-yard run on third down late in the contest that helped the Steelers run the clock out. Rodgers continues to put the Steelers offense in positions to win. Grade: C RB Jaylen Warren Jarrett Bailey: Warren’s emergence as a legitimate top five running back has been so fun to watch in real time. The Steelers made it clear that he would be the focal point of the offense on the first drive, as he racked up 43 yards on the opening series and finished with 101 on the ground and 36 as a receiver. He continues to make a strong potential All-Pro case for himself as the Steelers continue to ride him to victories: Grade: A Joey Bray: According to Matt Williamson , Jaylen Warren is the first running back to have 550+ rushing yards and 250+ receiving yards in his first seven games in a season since Christian McCaffrey in 2019. Warren posted over 100 scrimmage yards in the first half on Sunday, and continues to be the most dynamic and effective player on the Steelers offense. Grade: A+ RB Rico Dowdle Jarrett Bailey : The Steelers have found the right balance of carries for Warren and Dowdle. Warren had 18 carries, Dowdle had nine for 41 yards and added 45 yards as a receiver. This balance of working Dowdle in to get touches while Warren remains the clear cut No. 1 is the best way for Pittsburgh to find success in its backfield. This is the second straight game that Dowdle has given them some juice in this role. Grade: B Joey Bray: Put some respect on Rico Dowdle’s name. Since he has returned from injury, Dowdle has been a great complement to Jaylen Warren. The efficiency has also drastically improved for Dowdle, who averaged 4.6 yards per carry on Sunday, while also hauling in six passes. Dowdle and Warren are becoming the one-two punch that Steelers fans were hoping they would be at the start of the season. Grade: B Offense Jarrett Bailey: There were a lot of things to like about the way the offense performed. Offensive line wise, it was maybe the best game the Steelers had all year, especially when it came to run blocking. Yes, Chase Young made a couple plays, but Rodgers was tied for the fifth-fewest pressures faced in Week 7. However, there was plenty to dislike. The fade routes to DK Metcalf should be burnt with fire and never called again, especially in the red zone on third down. Those are almost certainly Rodgers’ doing, and they need to end immediately. Finishing drives as a whole needs to be something that gets better, as well. The Steelers had four red zone trips and only turned one of them into a touchdown. 16 points isn’t going to be enough against the great teams in the league. Grade: C+ Joey Bray: My biggest complaint from yesterday would be about the Steelers struggling to finish drives and having to settle for field goals. It seems like small potatoes since they won, but Aaron Rodgers’ visible frustration on the sidelines in the fourth quarter after having to settle for a field goal was notable. The playcalling in plus territory was particularly questionable yesterday. With plenty of quality teams and divisional opponents in the second half of their schedule, the offense will have to be better and turn some of those field goals into touchdowns even if it didn’t end up mattering yesterday. Grade: C EDGE T.J Watt Jarrett Bailey: Watt has officially re-emerged as an elite edge rusher. He had another sack on Sunday, and was robbed of the trifecta of a sack,s trip, and recovery despite the ball clearly moving when he sacked Tyler Shough. Regardless, he is now fourth in the league in sacks and continues to look like his former self. Grade: A Joey Bray: The Steelers’ star defender was probably robbed of a strip-sack of Saints quarterback Tyler Shough. Although the strip was called back, Watt brought his sack total to 5.5 on the season. The edge rusher rotation in the Steelers’ defense this season has seemed to keep Watt fresh, as he has returned to being someone who can be a double digit sack guy, which he is well on pace to be again this season. Nobody has forced more strip sacks since 2017 than Watt, and he continues to prove he can change the game in the blink of an eye. Grade: A LB Patrick Queen Jarrett Bailey: Queen was awesome on Sunday in what was one of his best games as a Steeler. He had 10 tackles and seven impact plays, per Sumer Sports. The only linebacker with more such plays was Blake Cashman of the Minnesota Vikings. For a guy that gets more scrutiny from Steelers fans than any other player, it was good to see him play so well. I’ll throw in a hat tip to Payton Wilson, as well, who had the interception that swung the game. Good day for the Steelers’ linebacker duo. Grade: A Joey Bray: All things considered, this was one of the best games that Patrick Queen has played as a Steeler. Yes, the dropped pick was tough, but it’s hard for me to harp on linebackers dropping interceptions. Especially with the way Queen responded, as he led the team in tackles and came up with a huge sack in which he made a great move to get by the Saints’ offensive line. Queen was around the ball a lot yesterday and made several phenomenal plays. Grade: A+ Defense Jarrett Bailey: The defense has allowed just three touchdowns over their last three games, and have allowed just one second-half touchdown this entire season. Allowing just 18 yards on 17 carries is absurd at any level, and Pittsburgh’s run defense has been the best in the league over the last three weeks. There are things that need cleaned up, specifically the third down success rate for the Saints (6-of-12), but limiting New Orleans to under five yards per play is something they can hang their hat on. If they can sustain this high-level of play, they can beat anyone. Grade: A Joey Bray: Once again, the zone defense was frustrating to watch as Tyler Shough went 30/38 passing in the contest. Many online have dubbed the Steelers defense as the first “bend don’t break” defense in history. The secondary is going to continue to be an issue until a serious corner is added, which may very well not happen anytime this season. I think Graham deserves a lot of credit for having a great defensive game plan that held New Orleans to just 10 points. The defense played with plenty of aggressiveness as they had several forced fumbles called back. Regardless, the Steelers’ defense continues to bend more than they break. Grade: B+ Special teams Jarrett Bailey: Chris Boswell was great, going three-of-three on field goals. Pittsburgh can’t seem to go a game without a special teams penalty, was Sean Murphy-Bunting was penalized on a punt, and the Steelers allowed a 42-yard kickoff return. The kick coverage unit is still a problem. Grade: B- Joey Bray: His consistency has been shaky this season, but Chris Boswell nailed all three of his field goals on Sunday. Given the offense’s struggles to punch the ball into…

title: Steelers’ Mike McCarthy praises jumbo package, OL Spencer Anderson
summary: In a callback to the Steelers’ 2025 offense under Arthur Smith, Pittsburgh broke out its six-offensive-lineman package versus the Saints on Sunday. And in a 16-10 win where the Steelers out-rushed New Orleans 148 yards to 18, it’s fair to say the decision paid off. Like last year, utility offensive lineman Spencer Anderson served as […]
full_text: Photo By Winslow Townson/Getty Images | Getty Images In a callback to the Steelers’ 2025 offense under Arthur Smith, Pittsburgh broke out its six-offensive-lineman package versus the Saints on Sunday. And in a 16-10 win where the Steelers out-rushed New Orleans 148 yards to 18, it’s fair to say the decision paid off. Like last year, utility offensive lineman Spencer Anderson served as the extra blocker in the jumbo package, playing 13 snaps on Sunday. Twelve of those were run plays, and per Steelers writer Tom Mead , the results on those rushes were 77 yards, 6.4 yards per carry and three runs over nine or more yards. Speaking to the media on Monday, Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said the Steelers’ jumbo package success in 2025 “absolutely” played a role in its return in 2026. “When you get the job, the first thing you do, you sit and down and starting going through the personnel,” McCarthy said. “And Spencer (Anderson), I was so impressed with him and it was a big part of the discussion of how we were trying to forecast him for where we felt he could play, because he played so many positions.” McCarthy compared Anderson to current Bills and former Cowboys lineman Conner McGovern, saying he can play every role from center to guard to fullback: “We gotta get him on the field,” McCarthy said. “When you have someone like Spencer with his unique talents, it gives you such great versatility,” he added. McCarthy hinted that part of why the jumbo package didn’t play a major role in the Steelers’ game plan until Week 7 was because the Steelers first gave Anderson the starting right guard role to open the season. Then, Anderson dealt with a bone chip in his right leg in late September. “In fairness to (Anderson), I wanted to give him a chance to compete for a job, and that’s why we started the way we did with him at right guard, and then he had the injury and so forth,” McCarthy said. Despite free agent signing Brock Hoffman having secured the starting right guard spot moving forward, McCarthy indicated that the Steelers still want to find ways to get Anderson on the field. “(Anderson) carries a lot of value on our football team, especially up front,” the Pittsburgh head coach said, “and it’s important for us to continue to create opportunities for him.”

title: Steelers UDFA rookie emerges as diamond in the rough vs. Saints.
summary: You wouldn’t be able to tell from the mere 1.1 yards per carry the Steelers gave up to the Saints offense on Sunday, but Pittsburgh’s defensive line depth was shorthanded ahead of its Week 7 matchup in Paris. Derrick Harmon, one of the Steelers’ top run stuffers and a 2025 first-round pick, was on injured […]
full_text: Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images | Getty Images You wouldn’t be able to tell from the mere 1.1 yards per carry the Steelers gave up to the Saints offense on Sunday, but Pittsburgh’s defensive line depth was shorthanded ahead of its Week 7 matchup in Paris. Derrick Harmon, one of the Steelers’ top run stuffers and a 2025 first-round pick, was on injured reserve. He was joined on IR shortly after by Sebastian Joseph-Day, one of the team’s top free-agent signings this offseason. While Pittsburgh was still able to lean on the excellent play of Cam Heyward and Keeanu Benton versus New Orleans, the team also had to ask more from D-line contributors lower on the depth chart such as Yahya Black and seventh-round rookie Gabriel Rubio, both of whom have impressed in their snaps so far this season. But Pittsburgh also had to introduce a new name into the rotation versus the Saints: undrafted rookie Kevin Jobity Jr., who saw the first 15 snaps of his NFL career in Paris on Sunday. And maybe there’s something special with UDFA defenders wearing No. 92, but Jobity — in limited snaps — looks like another potential find by the Steelers front office. Entering the draft from Syracuse this spring, the highlight of Jobity’s scouting report was his impressive 8.87 relative athletic score — at 6’4, 308 pounds, he had a 1.69-second 10-yard split and a 32-inch vertical. The Steelers definitely saw that athleticism as well, using Jobity as the lone lineman on their kickoff return and coverage teams against the Saints. This shouldn’t come as a surprise, but it’s a rare sight to see players of Jobity’s size in that phase of the game — linemen’s physicality can be an asset on special teams, but kickoffs are about finding blocks and making tackles in space, which is a tough assignment for those over 300 pounds. However, Jobity looked like he belonged on kickoff teams, landing a few solid blocks and even helping corral a returner on a fantastic coverage play. In the second clip below, he can’t sustain his block quite long enough, but if Lew Nichols hadn’t stumbled on the return, Jobity’s effort would’ve helped clear a lane. And the final rep is an impressive display of athleticism for a man his size. #Steelers UDFA Kevin Jobity Jr. on kickoff teams. Really impressive athleticism for a guy his size. pic.twitter.com/n2tN7rTUZZ — Ryland Bickley (@_Ryland_B) October 26, 2026 That special teams ability will help Jobity stay in the mix when it comes to earning a helmet on future game days. But he also showed some ability on defense, with the Steelers giving him a handful of snaps on the line in the second half versus New Orleans. Those reps weren’t always clean wins, but effort has been a standout trait of Jobity’s, even from the preseason. He plays through the whistle and tries to be a part of every tackle. In the first rep below, he does a good job dropping a knee to avoid losing position before exploding towards the ball. On the second, he initially gets shoved out the play, but keeps his eyes on the runner to get back to the gang tackle. pic.twitter.com/uo072Pq0IL — Ryland Bickley (@_Ryland_B) October 26, 2026 Here, Jobity showed some nice upper body strength, forcing Saints tackle Taliese Fuaga off-balance on a run play. pic.twitter.com/lnTpKrQTcY — Ryland Bickley (@_Ryland_B) October 26, 2026 And this was Jobity’s best rush of the day: condensing the pocket just enough to force a scramble from New Orleans quarterback Tyler Shough. pic.twitter.com/v0LstjsamJ — Ryland Bickley (@_Ryland_B) October 26, 2026 Jobity’s physical tools have never been a question, but it’s encouraging to see him showing some flashes this early in his career. In an aside that could be an entirely different article, new Pittsburgh defensive line coach Domata Peko has been one of the most underrated names on the team’s staff this year, getting the most out of every player in the team’s D-line room. With such a small sample size, it’s hard to draw many conclusions or set many expectations for Jobity moving forward. But the undrafted free agent — and the 11th rookie to make the Steelers’ 53-man roster this year — looks like he’s earned his spot in the team’s defensive line room.
author: Ryland Bickley

title: The Steelers’ defense has reached elite territory
summary: Entering the 2026 season, the Pittsburgh Steelers defense felt like it was facing its expiration date. Like a hair band from the ‘80s trying to remain relevant in the 2000s – either adapt or be left behind and forgotten. Pittsburgh’s defense had become more nostalgia act than on-field production. Sure, several future Hall of Famers […]
full_text: (Photo by Franco Arland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Entering the 2026 season, the Pittsburgh Steelers defense felt like it was facing its expiration date. Like a hair band from the ‘80s trying to remain relevant in the 2000s – either adapt or be left behind and forgotten. Pittsburgh’s defense had become more nostalgia act than on-field production. Sure, several future Hall of Famers are on the roster, but their numbers in 2025 were rough. They finished the 2025 season 20th in defensive EPA per play and 28th in total yards allowed. The never-changing defensive philosophy was severely hindering any chance for a motley crew Steelers defense to find any level of consistent play, and made it easy for the league’s best offenses to pick them apart. Which is why when the Steelers hired Mike McCarthy in January, many rolled their eyes at the thought of this band going on tour again. But with the hiring of Patrick Graham, Pittsburgh got with the times. The sound changed. The vocals improved. Are these music puns doing anything for you? Yeah, me either, I’m done with them. I did a lot of completely useless ‘80s music research purely for the bit. Would a Duran Duran reference to their 2004 album Astronaut save it? You get the point. The Steelers adapted and they evolved, which is something they needed to if they wanted to make any sort of noise during the 2026 season. Through seven weeks, the Steelers are tied for sixth in defensive EPA per play. They’re also allowing the sixth-fewest yards per game. DVOA wise , the Steelers rank seventh in the NFL, and they are second in DVOA against the run, trailing only the Jacksonville Jaguars. And while the entire season has seen the Steelers’ defensive pendulum swing to the other side, the last three games in particular have been especially terrific. Since Week 5, the Steelers have allowed just three touchdowns, which is tied with the Minnesota Vikings for the fewest in the league over that span. Their defensive success rate ranks third in the league, and their success rate against the run is the NFL’s best over that span, nearly a full two percentage points better than the second-place Chicago Bears. Passing wise, they are giving up just 5.67 yards per attempt during this three-game win streak, and they’ve picked off three passes compared to just two touchdown passes. This is an elite unit by just about every measure there is to offer. And if the offense can continue its own level of success (eighth in EPA per play, fourth in rush success rate since Week 5), this is a team that can hang with anyone. It’s the morning after game day, and don’t look now, but the Steelers are good. Big Patrick Queen game I don’t think there is a player more scrutinized by Steelers fans than Patrick Queen, but he had one of his best games as a Steeler on Sunday. Queen led the team with 10 tackles, one of which was a sack that would end up being the final play of the game for the Saints’ offense. He was credited with three run stops and seven impact plays, per Sumer Sports , which was the second-highest of any linebacker in Week 7. Only Blake Cashman of the Minnesota Vikings had more – a really good outing from No. 6. Jaylen Warren continues his fantastic season I’m going to do a stand-alone piece on this because his play is more than deserving of it. So if this seems a little bare bones, don’t worry. Warren had 101 yards on the ground and added 36 yards as a receiver. The tear that he is on right now is pretty special, and I’ll have more on it later. Quick hitters The third-down defense was obviously an issue. Can’t allow a team to convert on 50 percent of their third downs. After a Hall of Fame performance agains the Bucs, Jalen Ramsey had a rough outing. Per Sumer Sports, he gave up nine receptions on 10 targets for 78 yards and a touchdown. Payton Wilson had a strong outing with six tackles, two run stuffs, and the interception in the red zone that completely swung the game. T.J. Watt is firmly back in the elite pass rusher conversation. He had a sack – and what should have been a forced fumble and recovery that was overturned. Nevertheless, he is fourth in the NFL in sacks and fifth in pressure to sack percentage among all players who have played 100 snaps. The 2-1 carry ratio for Warren and Rico Dowdle is a good one. Warren finished with 18 carries to Dowdle’s nine. Overall, Warren had 21 touches to Dowdle’s 15, with the latter adding a very solid 86 yards from scrimmage. title: 5 takeaways from the Steelers’ 16-10 win over the Saints in Paris
summary: The Steelers’ offense left the door open for the Saints to make a comeback, but the defense did just enough for the team to escape Paris with a 16-10 win. That puts the Steelers’ record at 5-2, tied with the Browns atop the AFC North. Cleveland currently holds the tiebreaker over Pittsburgh, but with Baltimore […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Steelers’ offense left the door open for the Saints to make a comeback, but the defense did just enough for the team to escape Paris with a 16-10 win. That puts the Steelers’ record at 5-2, tied with the Browns atop the AFC North. Cleveland currently holds the tiebreaker over Pittsburgh, but with Baltimore falling to Cincinnati, the stage is set for the winner of Steelers-Browns next week to claim the division lead at the halfway point of the season. I’m filling in for Ryland this week, so the takeaways this week might have a slightly different tone, even if my fellow Read & React columnist and I tend to agree on a lot of our football philosophy. Regardless, let’s get to the takeaways from this game. 1. Jaylen Warren is inevitable, but Rico Dowdle is claiming his stake in the RB committee Through seven games, it’s apparent that Warren is the Steelers’ best and most consistent weapon on offense. He once again stuffed the stat sheet, racking up 101 yards on the ground on 18 carries (5.6 YPC) while adding 36 through the air on three catches. Warren has received at least 20 touches in four out of seven contests, and he’s paid off that commitment towards getting him the ball with performances of 179, 126, 188, and now 137 yards from scrimmage. The Steelers are 3-1 when Warren gets 20-plus touches, with the only loss coming against the Browns in a weird game where the Steelers looked like the better team in all but one disastrous second quarter. In games this season where Warren has 20 or more touches, the Steelers are averaging 26 points per game. In games where he has less than that magical number, Pittsburgh is averaging 16.3 points per game. Now, sure, the small sample size makes those averages a bit noisy. After all, the Steelers got Warren the rock 21 times today, and yet they scored just 16 points — though 19, spiritually, if not for a Saints penalty that wiped away a Chris Boswell field goal late in the fourth quarter and let the Steelers kneel out the game instead. I’ll also acknowledge that merely getting Warren 20 touches alone doesn’t fullproof anything. The Browns game proves that. But the idea does point to something most Steelers fans have come to understand: on a team that struggles to consistently produce explosive plays from the passing game, Warren serves as a spark plug for the Pittsburgh offense. Jaylen Warren isn't slowing down. PITvsNO on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/KL0xSY8XqM — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 That’s why I suspect I was not alone yesterday in feeling a twinge of frustration every time Rico Dowdle was on the field instead of Warren. Warren going crazy in the first half but let's keep trying to make Rico Dowdle happen — Ryan Parish (@ArmchairScout21) October 25, 2026 But while fans might not like it, or at least not like when and where the Steelers choose to work Dowdle in, the Steelers have made it clear they don’t want to grind Warren to dust with overuse. In the four games where both running backs have been available, the Steelers have distributed the ball at a nearly 60-40 split to Warren (65 touches) and Dowdle (44). And if we are going to point to “wins” when highlighting Warren’s touch total, it’s also worth noting that the Steelers are 3-1, too, in games where both running backs have been active this season. And for what it’s worth, Dowdle has now put together back-to-back strong performances in the change-of-pace role since returning to the lineup. Last week, he averaged 5.7 yards on nine carries in his first game back from injury. On Sunday, Dowdle had undoubtedly his best game yet as a Steeler, totaling 86 yards from scrimmage with six catches and averaging 4.6 yards per carry. He’s also produced a run of 15-plus yards in consecutive games. Big run for Rico Dowdle! #Steelers #NFL pic.twitter.com/UO1eXdlA8r — Blitzburgh (@Blitz_Burgh) October 25, 2026 For as bad as Dowdle looked in the first two games of the season, it’s worth considering that not only have the Steelers changed the right side of their offensive line since then, but they’ve also changed how they’re calling the run game. Through the first two weeks, Pittsburgh was calling zone concepts on roughly 60% of their runs , with a heavy skew (roughly 40%) towards outside zone concepts. That changed in Week 3, along with the right side of the line, and since then the Steelers have become a team that relies on power/gap schemes much more, especially duo concepts. Heading into Week 7, the Steelers’ season-long rate of zone-versus-gap schemes had reached a near 50-50 split, with duo being called on roughly 35% of their runs . That’s a dramatic shift, and one that better fits Dowdle’s skill set, and arguably Warren’s too. Dowdle is starting to look like the sidekick to Warren we all hoped and envisioned he’d be when the Steelers acquired him this offseason. We may always be left wanting more Warren, but it’s probably in the best interest of both the player and the team for the Steelers to continue to keep this backfield at a roughly 60-40 split. Hopefully, Dowdle can continue to make plays, and McCarthy can get a better feel for when to pull Warren — ideally not in the red zone, Big Mike! 2. The Steelers’ defense bent, but didn’t break… this time Coming into Week 7, the Steelers’ defense was allowing opposing teams an average of 204.3 passing yards a game. Some of that may have to do with the level of quarterbacks they’ve faced so far, but it certainly felt like Tyler Shough was dicing this team up in a way few quarterbacks have this season, on his way to 278 passing yards. Adding to that feeling was the length of New Orleans’ drives. The Saints possessed the ball just six times in this game, but four of those resulted in drives with at least eleven plays and lasting over five minutes. The Steelers’ zone scheme seemingly had no answers for throws underneath, with the Saints’ running backs combining for 10 catches and 79 yards, and four separate players totaling at least 50 yards receiving. Despite the Steelers stonewalling the Saints’ rushing attack — 18 yards on 17 carries (1.1 YPC) — and setting them up with several third-and-longs, the Saints went 6-of-12 on third down and converted both fourth-down attempts they went for. New Orleans punted on their first drive of the game, and wouldn’t again until the Saints’ final possession of the fourth quarter. And yet, only two Saints pass catchers averaged double-digit yards per catch, and Shough’s average yards per completion was 7.3. The Saints were able to nickel and dime Pittsburgh, but they lacked in explosive plays. Receiver Chris Olave came into the week as the second-leading receiver in terms of yardage, but was held to just 56 yards on six catches. New Orleans was able to move the ball, but they were only able to score twice, and just one of them was a touchdown. Credit, then, must go to the Steeler defense, which came up clutch in several big moments. The Saints crossed the fifty-yard line on their first drive of the game, but linebacker Patrick Queen ended their drive when he nearly came away with an interception on a third-and-long. Patrick Queen nearly gets the interception… 👀👀👀👀👀👀👀👀👀 @Patrickqueen_ #NFL #Steelers pic.twitter.com/2QP9XZljUu — The Standard (@TheStandard412) October 25, 2026 On the Saints’ next possession, they drove the ball to the red zone, but their drive came to a screeching halt on a second-quarter sack from T.J. Watt that was initially ruled a forced fumble and recovery before being overturned on review. While the overruling was questionable at best, it forced the Saints into a third-and-long that the Steelers were able to stifle and force New Orleans to settle for a field goal. This is unbelievable from TJ Watt PITvsNO on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ebASjMbWpp — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 The Saints would tie the game up on their third possession, but a…

title: Enemy Reaction 2026: Kansas City Chiefs (with bonus 49ers meltdown!)
summary: The Seattle Seahawks have rediscovered their primetime magic in home games over the past couple of seasons, and what a way to snap a losing skid! They throttled the Kansas City Chiefs in a barely competitive 20-3 win, putting themselves back in the NFC West chase and sending a message to the NFL that, as […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks have rediscovered their primetime magic in home games over the past couple of seasons, and what a way to snap a losing skid! They throttled the Kansas City Chiefs in a barely competitive 20-3 win, putting themselves back in the NFC West chase and sending a message to the NFL that, as long as they don’t sabotage themselves with turnovers, they’re extraordinarily hard to beat. Hell, they’re hard to beat even when they do commit a bunch of turnovers! This was a doubly sweet weekend for Seahawks fans, with the San Francisco 49ers suffering an upset loss to the Atlanta Falcons. You know what that means! Enemy Reaction is back for the first time since Week 2—we skipped over the Los Angeles Chargers—and there is a healthy bonus meltdown coming from 49ers fans. Chiefs game thread comments are courtesy of Arrowhead Pride ! (3-0 SEA) THAT'S TY'S BALL 🔥 @tyokada 's first INT of the season. 📺: @SNFonNBC pic.twitter.com/VI76EKHkC4 — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 26, 2026 Sam Darnold throws a dime to Jaxon Smith-Njigba for a touchdown! KCvsSEA on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/vnhaC6WufL — NFL (@NFL) October 26, 2026 George Holani breaks multiple tackles to convert 3rd and long! (13-0 SEA) George Holani breaks a pair of tackles on 3rd and 10 to move the chains 😮 pic.twitter.com/2wJb0wY8Vs — Prysm Sports (@PrysmSports) October 26, 2026 Derick Hall whacks Patrick Mahomes, who somehow gets his own fumble (13-3 SEA) FORCED IT 💥 @derick_hall9 📺: @SNFonNBC pic.twitter.com/JAHEpYix98 — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 26, 2026 Harrison Butker misses his second field goal of the game (13-3 SEA) harrison butker noooo good pic.twitter.com/1pBD7hX7rD — wok (@wokdior) October 26, 2026 Emanuel Wilson seals the deal with a 21-yard touchdown! (20-3 SEA FINAL) That was niiiiice 😮‍💨 TOUCHDOWN EMANUEL WILSON. 📺: @SNFonNBC pic.twitter.com/YfJgdXKJ4Y — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 26, 2026 Post-game: The Chiefs 5-0 start looks suspect ( Vahe Gregorian, KC Star ) Early on, anyway, the 2026 Chiefs sure were trending toward redemption and resumption of their modern identity as a perennial championship contender. In the wake of the distressing 6-11 dud last season, they entered Sunday night’s game against reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle at Lumen Field as one of just two remaining undefeated NFL teams. Moreover, they led the league in offensive yards per game, were second in points allowed and generally seemed to be restoring the new world order of the Mahomes Era. But their 20-3 loss to the Seahawks (4-3) was so thorough, unsightly and disillusioning as to render the 5-0 run-up to it entirely suspect — especially considering the Chiefs’ thorny schedule ahead. Yes, Seattle is a fine team and the ol’ one-game overreaction is a real phenomenon when it comes to NFL games. No doubt the Chiefs are capable of resetting. Trouble is, this loss seemed to expose every worrisome vulnerability they had flashed in beating teams with a combined record of 11-22. And it also came with the deflating issue of the stifling of something we were starting to take for granted: the exhilarating play of former Seahawks running back Kenneth Walker III, who had been a revelation until he mustered just 36 yards on 14 carries Sunday. An inconsistent offensive line couldn’t make room for Walker. FOX | NFL+ pic.twitter.com/7VBExpgNMh — Atlanta Falcons (@AtlantaFalcons) October 25, 2026 GEORGE KITTLE LOSES THE BALL AND THE FALCONS WILL WIN THE GAME! pic.twitter.com/JOpGjkEbbI — TSN (@TSN_Sports) October 25, 2026 Enemy Preaction: Chicago Bears RHAMONDRE STEVENSON‼️ 📺 Prime Video pic.twitter.com/heXDiTFnzW — New England Patriots (@Patriots) October 23, 2026 SANTOS JUST DRILLED A 58-YARDER TO GO UP TWO POSSESSIONS. NEvsCHI on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/XgUaLFdlzS — NFL (@NFL) October 23, 2026 Alright, so the Seahawks aren’t condemned to an early offseason just yet. They’ve gone through a rough patch and still come out the other side of it with a winning record. Up next are the Chicago Bears, who are 5-2 with a more potent offense (on paper) than the Chiefs. Mike Macdonald vs. Ben Johnson. ‘The Dark Side’ versus Caleb Williams, D’Andre Swift, Luther Burden, Colston Loveland, and local legend Rome Odunze. Dennis Allen’s defense against a Seahawks offense that showed signs of life. What a way to wrap up three straight nationally televised games, and what a way to kick off November with one more primetime showdown at Lumen Field! If the Seahawks prevail, then they’ll have withstood the toughest part of their schedule and still reached 5-3. All things considered, that would be pretty encouraging. Thanks for reading and go ‘Hawks!

title: Seahawks fan chat: Cowboys face what’s left of the Eagles on ‘Monday Night Football’
summary: The Seattle Seahawks still have three games to play against the NFC East, and two of their opponents are playing on Monday night to wrap up Week 7. There are certain games that look enticing when the NFL schedule releases in May. The Dallas Cowboys and Philadelphia Eagles are normally good for some entertaining football, […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks still have three games to play against the NFC East, and two of their opponents are playing on Monday night to wrap up Week 7. There are certain games that look enticing when the NFL schedule releases in May. The Dallas Cowboys and Philadelphia Eagles are normally good for some entertaining football, even if one of those teams isn’t particularly good. I don’t think anyone predicted both teams would be 2-4 and that the Eagles would be this depleted after six weeks. By far the most frightening loss for Philadelphia is quarterback Jalen Hurts, who’s out for the season due to blood clots. This is Tanner McKee’s team until further notice, and while he won’t have Devonta Smith or Dontayvion Wicks, he will have Saquon Barkley in the backfield again. Brian Schottenheimer’s Dallas Cowboys have surprisingly fizzled on offense over the past two weeks, and find themselves still unable to grasp the idea that they are required to play defense in the NFL in order to win games. At this point, the Cowboys shouldn’t be a comfortable favorite over anyone until they prove otherwise. The NFC East is pretty weak, but the New York Giants are surprising everyone at 4-2-1, so losing this game would be devastating for either team. Join us in the comments for a leisurely evening of MNF! The game starts at 5:15 pm PT on ESPN/ABC, but I’m sure some of you would rather watch the World Series. At least that’s been kickass to watch. title: Snap Reactions: All nickel, no base as Seahawks stymie Chiefs
summary: And just like that the Seattle Seahawks are back. After consecutive losses to the San Francisco 49ers and Denver Broncos had fans in despair at the state of the title defense for the Seahawks, a resounding 20-3 thumping of the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday Night Football has changed things. Seattle was far from an […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 25: Kenneth Walker III #9 of the Kansas City Chiefs is tackled by Nick Emmanwori #3 of the Seattle Seahawks and Josh Jobe #29 of the Seattle Seahawks during the second quarter at Lumen Field on October 25, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images And just like that the Seattle Seahawks are back. After consecutive losses to the San Francisco 49ers and Denver Broncos had fans in despair at the state of the title defense for the Seahawks, a resounding 20-3 thumping of the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday Night Football has changed things. Seattle was far from an offensive juggernaut, but with the defense showing up in midseason form, all the offense needed to do was put points on the board, and that they did. Anthony Bradford played every offensive snap in his return from injured reserve, while Charles Cross missed a dozen snaps after leaving with a high ankle sprain that is expected to keep him out of the lineup for some time. Josh Jones stepped in for Cross, playing more snaps against Kansas City than he had through the first six weeks combined. At running back Emanuel Wilson continued to earn the bulk of the workload in Jadarian Price’s absence, while at tight end Nick Kallerup’s 26 offensive snaps had him on the field more than fellow tight end Eric Saubert and almost as much as receiver Tory Horton. On defense, the Seahawks spent the entire game in nickel, with Julian Love, Nick Emmanwori, Devon Witherspoon, Josh Jobe and Ty Okada all playing every snap, with Nehemiah Pritchett joining the party for 11 snaps and Trevon Diggs on the field for a half dozen plays after being relegated to the practice squad, but then elevated for the game. For those who might have expected a beefed up defensive front from Mike Macdonald to slow down the running back with the most rushing yards second most rushing yards in the NFL, Jarran Reed and Brandon Pili combined for just 21 snaps. And on special teams there was a slight tweak as well, with Mike Morris finishing with 17 special teams snaps, which put him ahead of Brady Russell by a single snap. Rodney Thomas, Nehemiah Pritchett, Patrick O’Connell, Irv Charles and Jimmy Ciarlo all finished the game in double digits for snaps played on special teams. And now it’s on to another Sunday of football without stressing about the Seahawks, as Seattle will host another primetime game at Lumen Field on Monday Night Football in Week 8 when the Chicago Bears come to town.

title: Seahawks injury updates: Charles Cross to miss time with high ankle sprain
summary: Despite spoiling Kenneth Walker III’s return and shutting down the Kansas City Chiefs offense en route to a much needed 20-3 victory, it came at a cost. The Seattle Seahawks are now in position to be without their star left tackle for at least a short period of time. According to Ian Rapoport, left tackle […]
full_text: SEATTLE, CO - OCTOBER 15: Charles Cross #67 of the Seattle Seahawks runs out of the tunnel prior to an NFL football game against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Seattle, Colorado. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Despite spoiling Kenneth Walker III’s return and shutting down the Kansas City Chiefs offense en route to a much needed 20-3 victory , it came at a cost. The Seattle Seahawks are now in position to be without their star left tackle for at least a short period of time. According to Ian Rapoport, left tackle Charles Cross suffered a high ankle sprain in the fourth quarter of Sunday’s win and is expected to miss time, with optimism he can return within 1-2 weeks. It’s unclear if the team plans to place him on injured reserve. #Seahawks OT Charles Cross, who suffered an ankle injury on Sunday, has a high-ankle sprain and will miss time, the MRI revealed. The hope is he’s back in 1-2 weeks, but it depends on how rehab goes. pic.twitter.com/4yVx2jmupL — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 26, 2026 Rapoport’s estimated timeline seemingly rules him out for Seattle’s next two games against the Chicago Bears and Arizona Cardinals, with a return in Week 10 against the Las Vegas Raiders a possibility. However, with the Seahawks bye week coming right after, Week 12 against the San Francisco 49ers appears far more realistic, barring a quick rehab. Cross exited the game prior to Emanuel Wilson’s touchdown that put Seattle up 20-3, and after being evaluated by team trainers on the sideline—was quickly ruled out. Veteran Josh Jones slotted in on the left side, and is in line to start for the time being. Rashid Shaheed injury feedback ‘positive’ While Cross’s absence is a huge blow, wide receiver Rashid Shaheed appears to have avoided a serious injury. According to head coach Mike Macdonald, early tests on Shaheed’s knee yielded positive results, although he didn’t provide context on whether he’d be required to miss any time. The veteran receiver caught two passes for one yard before he exited late in the second quarter and was later ruled out. Shaheed suffered the injury on quarterback Sam Darnold’s interception during the Seahawks’ final drive of the first half, when he colilded with teammate Jaxon Smith-Njigba in the back of the end zone while in the air trying to receive the pass. Should he be forced to miss time, second year wideout Tory Horton will likely see an uptick in targets, alongside Cooper Kupp and tight end AJ Barner—who finished second on the team in receptions as well as receiving yards against Kansas City. Although Cross and Shaheed’s injuries leave the status of Seattle’s offense in question, they’re set to receive another significant backfield upgrade in the coming weeks. Jadarian Price nearing return Macdonald added the team intends to open running back Jadarian Price’s (chest) 21-day practice window this week, which will help determine his game status against the Bears. The rookie ball carrier was placed on injured reserve at the beginning of October after re-aggravating the chest injury he suffered against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 2, but appears to be nearing a return—even if it doesn’t come against Chicago. Upon re-taking to field, he’ll likely split carries with Zach Charbonnet (knee), who—like Price is expected back sooner than later. It’ll be worth monitoring the status of both Shaheed and Price when the team releases their first practice report of the week on Thursday afternoon.

title: Seahawks Droppings: Seattle destroys Kansas City Chiefs, puts NFL on notice
summary: I almost made the headline “Anthony Bradford’s return kickstarts Seahawks offense”, and that wouldn’t have been a lie. Finally, the 2026 Seattle Seahawks played a complete game, looking absolutely dominant in a 20-3 shellacking of the previously unbeaten Kansas City Chiefs on the same day that the San Francisco 49ers lost to the Atlanta Falcons. […]
full_text: I almost made the headline “Anthony Bradford’s return kickstarts Seahawks offense”, and that wouldn’t have been a lie. Finally, the 2026 Seattle Seahawks played a complete game, looking absolutely dominant in a 20-3 shellacking of the previously unbeaten Kansas City Chiefs on the same day that the San Francisco 49ers lost to the Atlanta Falcons. Talk about a perfect way to cap the weekend…in those beautiful throwback jerseys nonetheless! All season long, the story has been the offense’s struggles marring elite defensive performances. We still got a goofy Sam Darnold pick just before the half, otherwise the score could’ve been even worse. No worries, the Seahawks defense stepped up in a big way holding former Seattle RB Kenneth Walker III to just 36 yards rushing. Meanwhile, Seattle ran for 153 yards and put up over 400 yards of offense. The mini bye was good to the Seahawks. Seahawks Droppings Seattle muzzled K9 and harassed Patrick Mahomes all game. Walker was one of the leading rushers in the NFL, but had no room to bounce outside against the Seahawks. They only sacked Mahomes one time, but kept him to 19/33 for 165 yards passing and 1 INT. The Chiefs never reached the red zone…maybe that’s a good thing considering the defense’s struggles in that area. Regardless, that defensive performance was exquisite and Mike Macdonald should take a bow. Nick Emmanwori is a cheat code. Looking at his stats won’t tell the entire story. He’s been used all over the field this season, showing out as both a pass-rusher and coverage player. Emmanwori’s pressure on Mahomes directly resulted in Ty Okada’s interception. Later in the game, he was matched up one-on-one with speedster Xavier Worthy. No problem as Emmanwori stayed with him step for step on a deep ball that resulted in an incompletion. Sometimes I forget that he’s just 22 years old and that he missed all of training camp. Emmanwori will keep getting better, which is a scary thought for the rest of the NFL. Sam Darnold was dropping dimes. The interception was terrible, I’ll just get that out of the way. Those two deep throws to Jaxon Smith-Njigba, though? Beautiful. Sam made huge plays with his legs today as well, getting some key first downs. If he plays games like he did today, the Seahawks will win a lot more games this season. Jaxon Smith-Njigba is unstoppable. Literally. JSN reeled in 9 catches for 150 yards and 1 TD. He had those two huge aforementioned deep passes to go along with crossers over the middle. Credit Brian Fleury for finding ways to get JSN open and Darnold for finding him. Rashid Shaheed injured his knee and didn’t play in the second half. That will be something to monitor, but JSN will still get his. Seattle’s run game showed up. Emmanuel Wilson ran hard, gaining 100 yards on 24 carries with a game-clinching late TD. George Holani had a key third down conversion as well. Reinforcements should be on the way as Zach Charbonnet could make his season debut in Week 8 and Jadarian Price will be eligible to return from IR as well. That would give the run game even more juice which will in turn help the pass game. No sacks on Darnold. Is it a coincidence that in the week Anthony Bradford returns, Seattle rushes for a bunch of yards and Darnold isn’t sacked at all? Maybe, but Bradford – despite what you might read on the internet – is actually a good player. Charles Cross went out late with an ankle injury. Hopefully that heals up quickly. Fleury called a great game. Seattle was able to stick with the run game which allowed Fleury to mix it up. His playcalling on that late, game-clinching drive was clutch. That TE screen to AJ Barner was a thing of beauty. He had Darnold getting the ball out quickly which contributed to the protection. Once Fleury has his full stable of running backs, we’ll hopefully see the offense break out even more. The most frustrating thing about the last few weeks is that the Seahawks were clearly better than both the Niners and Denver Broncos, losing very winnable games because of turnovers and poor offensive performance. Seattle’s performance against the formerly undefeated Chiefs just underscores that point. They need to use this game as a springboard to keep playing complementary football and get this thing rolling. Seattle is not done. The Niners lost today and sustained more injuries. This Seahawks defense will give them a chance to win every game for the rest of the season. It’s up to the offense to hold up their end of the bargain. If they play like they did today, Seattle will be right in the thick of things.

title: Seahawks vs. Bears odds: Opening lines for Week 8 matchup
summary: The Seattle Seahawks will host the Chicago Bears on Monday Night Football in Week 8, with FanDuel Sportsbook opening Seattle as a 3-point favorite. The Seahawks are priced at -172 on the moneyline, while Chicago sits at +144. The over/under is set at 46.5 points. Chicago enters the matchup with a 5-2 record after defeating […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks will host the Chicago Bears on Monday Night Football in Week 8, with FanDuel Sportsbook opening Seattle as a 3-point favorite . The Seahawks are priced at -172 on the moneyline, while Chicago sits at +144. The over/under is set at 46.5 points. Chicago enters the matchup with a 5-2 record after defeating the New England Patriots 30-24 on Thursday night, getting a mini-bye before the matchup against the Seahawks. Seattle, meanwhile, improved to 4-3 with a convincing 20-3 win over the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday Night Football . The Seahawks’ defense dominated Patrick Mahomes and company, while the offense leaned on its running game and another outstanding performance from Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Despite Chicago’s better record, oddsmakers are giving Seattle the edge at Lumen Field. For comparison, Kansas City opened as a three-point underdog at Seattle in Week 7 despite entering that game undefeated, and Seattle won comfortably. The total of 46.5 points suggests expectations of a more competitive scoring affair than Sunday’s defensive battle against Kansas City. Chicago scored 30 points against New England, while Seattle held the Chiefs to just a field goal, making this a compelling matchup between a productive Bears offense led by Ben Johnson, and a Seahawks defense coming off one of its strongest performances of the season. Seattle will look to carry that momentum into another prime-time game, but Chicago presents a different challenge. The Bears will arrive in Seattle looking to prove they belong among the NFC’s contenders. 12s, make your voices heard on the SB Nation app! title: 49ers News: Two weeks left to stew on that loss
summary: Kyle Shanahan shares 49ers updates headed into the bye week“We won’t get back with the players until next Monday. We just spent all day with them today, just finished here a little bit ago. Tomorrow they’ll come in, they’ll do all workouts and things like that, do a little exercise on the field, have a […]
full_text: Kyle Shanahan shares 49ers updates headed into the bye week “We won’t get back with the players until next Monday. We just spent all day with them today, just finished here a little bit ago. Tomorrow they’ll come in, they’ll do all workouts and things like that, do a little exercise on the field, have a meeting and then we’ll be done with them. Then we’ll come back Monday ready to go.” 49ers vs. Falcons PFF grades: Best and worst from the game, plus snap counts “Colby allowed a game-high five pressures, contributing to his 45.4 pass-blocking grade, the lowest among the game’s offensive linemen. He also received the lowest overall offensive grade among offensive linemen, finishing at 45.7.” 49ers’ Christian McCaffrey has mild hamstring strain. Will he return after bye week? (Paywall) “Postgame, McCaffrey told reporters that his leg “just died” on him. “I was trying to get it going for the whole rest of the game, but it just sucks trying to play like that. But I know I’ll be all right.” 49ers grades: The defensive line laid an egg; Secondary struggles continue “The group that has punched above its weight class all season finally came back down to earth. We’ve been spoiled by defensive tackles who controlled the game. That was not the case in Atlanta. Gracen Halton was invisible for the first time. Sebastian Valdez’s only stat was a missed tackle. Osa Odighizuwa has the same pass-rush win rate as Kyle Shanahan, who tore Odighizuwa a new one on the sideline after the veteran jumped offside on 4th and 4. Rookie James Thompson was the most active, with a pressure and two run stops. But, and this wasn’t on him, a penalty gifted Atlanta a fresh set of downs on 3rd and 2. Three edge rushers played over 30 snaps: Romello Height (38), Keion White (35), and Mykel Williams (31). The edge group had zero tackles for loss. Mykel missed a pair of tackles. He had one pressure. Keion had two. Romello had zero, but he and Williams both had run stops. They bottled up Bijan Robinson, who had only one 10+ yard run, but they still moved off the ball more than usual. Robinson had 19 yards before contact, and Khalil Herbert had four on two carries.”

title: Cowboys-Eagles live discussion: Hang out with your families tonight
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles host the Dallas Cowboys as arguably the worst division in football gets another primetime game. The Eagles will be without DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, but they’ll have Saquon Barkley, Landon Dickerson, and Eli Stowers. The Cowboys have lost two in a row and are 2-4. They haven’t scored two touchdowns in […]
full_text: (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles host the Dallas Cowboys as arguably the worst division in football gets another primetime game. The Eagles will be without DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, but they’ll have Saquon Barkley, Landon Dickerson, and Eli Stowers. The Cowboys have lost two in a row and are 2-4. They haven’t scored two touchdowns in their last two games. Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb are struggling on that side of the ball. Will that change against the Eagles? Philadelphia let the Panthers score 25 on them. Bryce Young threw for 281 yards and a pair of touchdowns last week. If the Cowboys have a get-right defense, it’s this iteration of their rival Eagles. Tanner McKee gets the nod with Jalen Hurts out. Part of Carolina’s success last week came from running 74 plays, thanks to the Eagles averaging 3.6 yards per play. If the Eagles are going to give Dallas that many opportunities to score, they will. This is the kind of game where you hang out with your family, go outside, or watch literally anything else on TV. The World Series and WNBA finals are on at the same time as this game.
author: Kyle Posey

title: 49ers ‘pretty optimistic’ Christian McCaffrey’s mild hamstring strain won’t cause him to miss time
summary: One bright spot for the San Francisco 49ers was their injury report coming out of Week 7. Running back Christian McCaffrey left with what was initially diagnosed as a thigh injury. Head coach Kyle Shanahan said it’s a mild hamstring strain for McCaffrey. The good news is Shanahan said the 49ers are “pretty optimistic” that […]
full_text: (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images One bright spot for the San Francisco 49ers was their injury report coming out of Week 7. Running back Christian McCaffrey left with what was initially diagnosed as a thigh injury. Head coach Kyle Shanahan said it’s a mild hamstring strain for McCaffrey. The good news is Shanahan said the 49ers are “pretty optimistic” that McCaffrey will be fine coming out of the bye week. He wouldn’t guarantee their return, but Shanahan said several players currently out with injuries could return after the bye. It’s a lengthy list: WR Mike Evans WR Deebo Samuel WR Demarcus Robinson DE Nick Bosa DT CJ West S Marques Sigle LB Garret Wallow LB Luke Gifford CB Upton Stout The wide receiver rotation could look a lot different when the 49ers offense takes the field against the Raiders. Despite missing a game, Evans still has far and away the most snaps of any receiver on the roster at 192. Deebo has missed two games, and he’s second in snaps with 164. Through the first two games of the season, Robinson was tied with Samuel for the second-most snaps. We’ll see how that changes with Christian Kirk in the mix and after Jordan Watkins has played, but it’s likely the end of the road for Brandin Cooks. It’ll be interesting to see what happens with West. He’s been out since Week 2. In Week 1, Gracen Halton was already outsnapping West. James Thompson only played one fewer snap than him. West played more than Thompson in Week 2, but still fell short of Halton and Osa Odighizuwa. Based on how things were before the season, West would take Sebastian Valdez’s spot. But Valdez isn’t this no-name off the practice squad anymore. He’s played well in his role. You could argue he’s given the defense more than West would have if he were healthy. Sigle rotated with Malik Mustapha and occasionally Ji’Ayir Brown before he went down with an injury. When he played, we didn’t see the same rookie mistakes from Sigle that he made a year ago. For what the 49ers ask of their safeties and the speed element he brings to the table, Mustapha and Sigle might be their best duo
